}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{29:30}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: He said, "My Lord, support me against the corrupting people."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: He said: My Lord! Give me victory over folk who work corruption.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَ رَبِّ ٱنصُرْنِى عَلَى ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلْمُفْسِدِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{29:31}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And when Our messengers [i.e., angels] came to Abraham with the good tidings, they said, "Indeed, we will destroy the people of that [i.e., Lot's] city. Indeed, its people have been wrongdoers."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And when Our messengers brought Abraham the good news, they said: Lo! we are about to destroy the people of that township, for its people are wrong-doers.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَلَمَّا جَآءَتْ رُسُلُنَآ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ بِٱلْبُشْرَىٰ قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّا مُهْلِكُوٓا۟ أَهْلِ هَـٰذِهِ ٱلْقَرْيَةِ  إِنَّ أَهْلَهَا كَانُوا۟ ظَـٰلِمِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{29:32}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: [Abraham] said, "Indeed, within it is Lot." They said, "We are more knowing of who is within it. We will surely save him and his family, except his wife. She is to be of those who remain behind."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: He said: Lo! Lot is there. They said: We are best aware of who is there. We are to deliver him and his household, all save his wife, who is of those who stay behind.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَ إِنَّ فِيهَا لُوطًا  قَالُوا۟ نَحْنُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَن فِيهَا  لَنُنَجِّيَنَّهُ وَأَهْلَهُٓ إِلَّا ٱمْرَأَتَهُ كَانَتْ مِنَ ٱلْغَـٰبِرِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{29:33}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And when Our messengers [i.e., angels] came to Lot, he was distressed for them and felt for them great discomfort. They said, "Fear not, nor grieve. Indeed, we will save you and your family, except your wife; she is to be of those who remain behind.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And when Our messengers came unto Lot, he was troubled upon their account, for he could not protect them; but they said: Fear not, nor grieve! Lo! we are to deliver thee and thy household, (all) save thy wife, who is of those who stay behind.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَلَمَّآ أَن جَآءَتْ رُسُلُنَا لُوطًا سِىٓءَ بِهِمْ وَضَاقَ بِهِمْ ذَرْعًا وَقَالُوا۟ لَا تَخَفْ وَلَا تَحْزَنْ  إِنَّا مُنَجُّوكَ وَأَهْلَكَ إِلَّا ٱمْرَأَتَكَ كَانَتْ مِنَ ٱلْغَـٰبِرِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{29:34}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Indeed, we will bring down on the people of this city punishment from the sky because they have been defiantly disobedient."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Lo! We are about to bring down upon the folk of this township a fury from the sky because they are evil-livers.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
إِنَّا مُنزِلُونَ عَلَىٰٓ أَهْلِ هَـٰذِهِ ٱلْقَرْيَةِ رِجْزًا مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ بِمَا كَانُوا۟ يَفْسُقُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{29:35}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And We have certainly left of it a sign as clear evidence for a people who use reason.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And verily of that We have left a clear sign for people who have sense.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَلَقَد تَّرَكْنَا مِنْهَآ ءَايَةً بَيِّنَةً لِّقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}

\section{Surah 2, Al-Baqarah (The Cow)
Verses 258 -- 260}

The 87th revealed Surah. Revealed in Madinah


\noindent[\textbf{2:258}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Have you not considered the one who argued with Abraham about his Lord [merely] because Allāh had given him kingship? When Abraham said, "My Lord is the one who gives life and causes death," he said, "I give life and cause death." Abraham said, "Indeed, Allāh brings up the sun from the east, so bring it up from the west." So the disbeliever was overwhelmed [by astonishment], and Allāh does not guide the wrongdoing people.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Bethink thee of him who had an argument with Abraham about his Lord, because Allah had given him the kingdom; how, when Abraham said: My Lord is He Who giveth life and causeth death, he answered: I give life and cause death. Abraham said: Lo! Allah causeth the sun to rise in the East, so do thou cause it to come up from the West. Thus was the disbeliever abashed. And Allah guideth not wrongdoing folk.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِى حَآجَّ إِبْرَٰهِـمَ فِى رَبِّهِٓ أَنْ ءَاتَىٰهُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْمُلْكَ إِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَٰهِـمُ رَبِّىَ ٱلَّذِى يُحْىِ وَيُمِيتُ قَالَ أَنَا أُحْىِ وَأُمِيتُ  قَالَ إِبْرَٰهِـمُ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَأْتِى بِٱلشَّمْسِ مِنَ ٱلْمَشْرِقِ فَأْتِ بِهَا مِنَ ٱلْمَغْرِبِ فَبُهِتَ ٱلَّذِى كَفَرَ  وَٱللَّهُ لَا يَهْدِى ٱلْقَوْمَ ٱلظَّـٰلِمِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{2:259}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Or [consider such an example] as the one who passed by a township which had fallen into ruin. He said, "How will Allāh bring this to life after its death?" So Allāh caused him to die for a hundred years; then He revived him. He said, "How long have you remained?" He [the man] said, "I have remained a day or part of a day." He said, "Rather, you have remained one hundred years. Look at your food and your drink; it has not changed with time. And look at your donkey; and We will make you a sign for the people. And look at the bones [of this donkey] - how We raise them and then We cover them with flesh." And when it became clear to him, he said, "I know that Allāh is over all things competent."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Or (bethink thee of) the like of him who, passing by a township which had fallen into utter ruin, exclaimed: How shall Allah give this township life after its death? And Allah made him die a hundred years, then brought him back to life. He said: How long hast thou tarried? (The man) said: I have tarried a day or part of a day. (He) said: Nay, but thou hast tarried for a hundred years. Just look at thy food and drink which have not rotted! Look at thine ass! And, that We may make thee a token unto mankind, look at the bones, how We adjust them and then cover them with flesh! And when (the matter) became clear unto him, he said: I know now that Allah is Able to do all things.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
أَوْ كَٱلَّذِى مَرَّ عَلَىٰ قَرْيَةٍ وَهِىَ خَاوِيَةٌ عَلَىٰ عُرُوشِهَا قَالَ أَنَّىٰ يُحْىِ هَـٰذِهِ ٱللَّهُ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَا  فَأَمَاتَهُ ٱللَّهُ مِا۟ئَةَ عَامٍ ثُمَّ بَعَثَهُ  قَالَ كَمْ لَبِثْتَ  قَالَ لَبِثْتُ يَوْمًا أَوْ بَعْضَ يَوْمٍ  قَالَ بَل لَّبِثْتَ مِا۟ئَةَ عَامٍ فَٱنظُرْ إِلَىٰ طَعَامِكَ وَشَرَابِكَ لَمْ يَتَسَنَّهْ  وَٱنظُرْ إِلَىٰ حِمَارِكَ وَلِنَجْعَلَكَ ءَايَةً لِّلنَّاسِ  وَٱنظُرْ إِلَى ٱلْعِظَامِ كَيْفَ نُنشِزُهَا ثُمَّ نَكْسُوهَا لَحْمًا  فَلَمَّا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُ قَالَ أَعْلَمُ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{2:260}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And [mention] when Abraham said, "My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead." [Allāh] said, "Have you not believed?" He said, "Yes, but [I ask] only that my heart may be satisfied." [Allāh] said, "Take four birds and commit them to yourself. Then [after slaughtering them] put on each hill a portion of them; then call them - they will come [flying] to you in haste. And know that Allāh is Exalted in Might and Wise."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And when Abraham said (unto his Lord): My Lord! Show me how Thou givest life to the dead, He said: Dost thou not believe? Abraham said: Yea, but (I ask) in order that my heart may be at ease. (His Lord) said: Take four of the birds and cause them to incline unto thee, then place a part of them on each hill, then call them, they will come to thee in haste, and know that Allah is Mighty, Wise.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَٰهِـمُ رَبِّ أَرِنِى كَيْفَ تُحْىِ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ  قَالَ أَوَلَمْ تُؤْمِن  قَالَ بَلَىٰ وَلَـٰكِن لِّيَطْمَئِنَّ قَلْبِى  قَالَ فَخُذْ أَرْبَعَةً مِّنَ ٱلطَّيْرِ فَصُرْهُنَّ إِلَيْكَ ثُمَّ ٱجْعَلْ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ جَبَلٍ مِّنْهُنَّ جُزْءًا ثُمَّ ٱدْعُهُنَّ يَأْتِينَكَ سَعْيًا  وَٱعْلَمْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}

\section{Surah 37, Aş-Şāffāt (Those who set the Ranks)
Verses 133 -- 138}

The 56th revealed Surah. Revealed in Makkah


\noindent[\textbf{37:133}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And indeed, Lot was among the messengers.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And lo! Lot verily was of those sent (to warn).

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَإِنَّ لُوطًا لَّمِنَ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{37:134}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: [So mention] when We saved him and his family, all,

\textit{M. Pickthall}: When We saved him and his household, every one,

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
إِذْ نَجَّيْنَـٰهُ وَأَهْلَهُٓ أَجْمَعِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{37:135}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Except an old woman [i.e., his wife] among those who remained [with the evildoers].

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Save an old woman among those who stayed behind;

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
إِلَّا عَجُوزًا فِى ٱلْغَـٰبِرِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{37:136}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Then We destroyed the others.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Then We destroyed the others.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
ثُمَّ دَمَّرْنَا ٱلْـَٔاخَرِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{37:137}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And indeed, you pass by them in the morning

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And lo! ye verily pass by (the ruin of) them in the morning

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَإِنَّكُمْ لَتَمُرُّونَ عَلَيْهِم مُّصْبِحِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{37:138}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And at night. Then will you not use reason?

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And at night-time; have ye then no sense?

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَبِٱلَّيْلِ  أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}

\section{Surah 27, An-Naml (The Ant)
Verses 54 -- 58}

The 48th revealed Surah. Revealed in Makkah


\noindent[\textbf{27:54}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And [mention] Lot, when he said to his people, "Do you commit immorality while you are seeing?

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And Lot! when he said unto his folk: Will ye commit abomination knowingly?

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَلُوطًا إِذْ قَالَ لِقَوْمِهِٓ أَتَأْتُونَ ٱلْفَـٰحِشَةَ وَأَنتُمْ تُبْصِرُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{27:55}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Do you indeed approach men with desire instead of women? Rather, you are a people behaving ignorantly."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Must ye needs lust after men instead of women? Nay, but ye are folk who act senselessly.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
أَئِنَّكُمْ لَتَأْتُونَ ٱلرِّجَالَ شَهْوَةً مِّن دُونِ ٱلنِّسَآءِ  بَلْ أَنتُمْ قَوْمٌ تَجْهَلُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{27:56}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: But the answer of his people was not except that they said, "Expel the family of Lot from your city. Indeed, they are people who keep themselves pure."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: But the answer of his folk was naught save that they said: Expel the household of Lot from your township, for they (forsooth) are folk who would keep clean!

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
۞ فَمَا كَانَ جَوَابَ قَوْمِهِٓ إِلَّآ أَن قَالُوٓا۟ أَخْرِجُوٓا۟ ءَالَ لُوطٍ مِّن قَرْيَتِكُمْ  إِنَّهُمْ أُنَاسٌ يَتَطَهَّرُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{27:57}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: So We saved him and his family, except for his wife; We destined her to be of those who remained behind.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Then We saved him and his household save his wife; We destined her to be of those who stayed behind.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَأَنجَيْنَـٰهُ وَأَهْلَهُٓ إِلَّا ٱمْرَأَتَهُ قَدَّرْنَـٰهَا مِنَ ٱلْغَـٰبِرِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{27:58}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And We rained upon them a rain [of stones], and evil was the rain of those who were warned.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And We rained a rain upon them. Dreadful is the rain of those who have been warned.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَأَمْطَرْنَا عَلَيْهِم مَّطَرًا  فَسَآءَ مَطَرُ ٱلْمُنذَرِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}

\section{Surah 12, Yūsuf (Joseph)
All Verses (1 -- 111)}

The 53rd revealed Surah. Revealed in Makkah


\noindent[\textbf{12:1}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Alif, Lām, Rā. These are the verses of the clear Book.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Alif. Lam. Ra. These are verse of the Scripture that maketh plain.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
 الٓر  تِلْكَ ءَايَـٰتُ ٱلْكِتَـٰبِ ٱلْمُبِينِ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:2}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Indeed, We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur’ān that you might understand.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Lo! We have revealed it, a Lecture in Arabic, that ye may understand.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
إِنَّآ أَنزَلْنَـٰهُ قُرْءَٰنًا عَرَبِيًّا لَّعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:3}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: We relate to you, [O Muḥammad], the best of stories in what We have revealed to you of this Qur’ān although you were, before it, among the unaware.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: We narrate unto thee (Muhammad) the best of narratives in that We have inspired in thee this Qur'an, though aforetime thou wast of the heedless.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
نَحْنُ نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ أَحْسَنَ ٱلْقَصَصِ بِمَآ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْكَ هَـٰذَا ٱلْقُرْءَانَ وَإِن كُنتَ مِن قَبْلِهِ لَمِنَ ٱلْغَـٰفِلِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:4}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: [Of these stories mention] when Joseph said to his father, "O my father, indeed I have seen [in a dream] eleven stars and the sun and the moon; I saw them prostrating to me."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: When Joseph said unto his father: O my father! Lo! I saw in a dream eleven planets and the sun and the moon, I saw them prostrating themselves unto me.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
إِذْ قَالَ يُوسُفُ لِأَبِيهِ يَـٰٓأَبَتِ إِنِّى رَأَيْتُ أَحَدَ عَشَرَ كَوْكَبًا وَٱلشَّمْسَ وَٱلْقَمَرَ رَأَيْتُهُمْ لِى سَـٰجِدِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:5}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: He said, "O my son, do not relate your vision to your brothers or they will contrive against you a plan. Indeed Satan, to man, is a manifest enemy.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: He said: O my dear son! Tell not thy brethren of thy vision, lest they plot a plot against thee. Lo! Satan is for man an open foe.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَ يَـٰبُنَىَّ لَا تَقْصُصْ رُءْيَاكَ عَلَىٰٓ إِخْوَتِكَ فَيَكِيدُوا۟ لَكَ كَيْدًا  إِنَّ ٱلشَّيْطَـٰنَ لِلْإِنسَـٰنِ عَدُوٌّ مُّبِينٌ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:6}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And thus will your Lord choose you and teach you the interpretation of narratives [i.e., events or dreams] and complete His favor upon you and upon the family of Jacob, as He completed it upon your fathers before, Abraham and Isaac. Indeed, your Lord is Knowing and Wise."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Thus thy Lord will prefer thee and will teach thee the interpretation of events, and will perfect His grace upon thee and upon the family of Jacob as He perfected it upon thy forefathers, Abraham and Isaac. Lo! thy Lord is Knower, Wise.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَكَذَٰلِكَ يَجْتَبِيكَ رَبُّكَ وَيُعَلِّمُكَ مِن تَأْوِيلِ ٱلْأَحَادِيثِ وَيُتِمُّ نِعْمَتَهُ عَلَيْكَ وَعَلَىٰٓ ءَالِ يَعْقُوبَ كَمَآ أَتَمَّهَا عَلَىٰٓ أَبَوَيْكَ مِن قَبْلُ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ وَإِسْحَـٰقَ  إِنَّ رَبَّكَ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:7}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Certainly were there in Joseph and his brothers signs for those who ask, [such as]

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Verily in Joseph and his brethren are signs (of Allah's Sovereignty) for the inquiring.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
۞ لَّقَدْ كَانَ فِى يُوسُفَ وَإِخْوَتِهِٓ ءَايَـٰتٌ لِّلسَّآئِلِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:8}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: When they said, "Joseph and his brother are more beloved to our father than we, while we are a clan. Indeed, our father is in clear error.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: When they said: Verily Joseph and his brother are dearer to our father than we are, many though we be. Lo! our father is in plain aberration.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
إِذْ قَالُوا۟ لَيُوسُفُ وَأَخُوهُ أَحَبُّ إِلَىٰٓ أَبِينَا مِنَّا وَنَحْنُ عُصْبَةٌ إِنَّ أَبَانَا لَفِى ضَلَـٰلٍ مُّبِينٍ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:9}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Kill Joseph or cast him out to [another] land; the countenance [i.e., attention] of your father will [then] be only for you, and you will be after that a righteous people."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: (One said): Kill Joseph or cast him to some (other) land, so that your father's favour may be all for you, and (that) ye may afterward be righteous folk.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
ٱقْتُلُوا۟ يُوسُفَ أَوِ ٱطْرَحُوهُ أَرْضًا يَخْلُ لَكُمْ وَجْهُ أَبِيكُمْ وَتَكُونُوا۟ مِن بَعْدِهِ قَوْمًا صَـٰلِحِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:10}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Said a speaker among them, "Do not kill Joseph but throw him into the bottom of the well; some travelers will pick him up - if you would do [something]."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: One among them said: Kill not Joseph but, if ye must be doing, fling him into the depth of the pit; some caravan will find him.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَ قَآئِلٌ مِّنْهُمْ لَا تَقْتُلُوا۟ يُوسُفَ وَأَلْقُوهُ فِى غَيَـٰبَتِ ٱلْجُبِّ يَلْتَقِطْهُ بَعْضُ ٱلسَّيَّارَةِ إِن كُنتُمْ فَـٰعِلِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:11}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: They said, "O our father, why do you not entrust us with Joseph while indeed, we are to him sincere counselors?

\textit{M. Pickthall}: They said: O our father! Why wilt thou not trust us with Joseph, when lo! we are good friends to him?

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالُوا۟ يَـٰٓأَبَانَا مَا لَكَ لَا تَأْمَ۫نَّا عَلَىٰ يُوسُفَ وَإِنَّا لَهُ لَنَـٰصِحُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:12}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Send him with us tomorrow that he may eat well and play. And indeed, we will be his guardians."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Send him with us to-morrow that he may enjoy himself and play. And lo! we shall take good care of him.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
أَرْسِلْهُ مَعَنَا غَدًا يَرْتَعْ وَيَلْعَبْ وَإِنَّا لَهُ لَحَـٰفِظُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:13}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: [Jacob] said, "Indeed, it saddens me that you should take him, and I fear that a wolf would eat him while you are of him unaware."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: He said: Lo! in truth it saddens me that ye should take him with you, and I fear less the wolf devour him while ye are heedless of him.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَ إِنِّى لَيَحْزُنُنِىٓ أَن تَذْهَبُوا۟ بِهِ وَأَخَافُ أَن يَأْكُلَهُ ٱلذِّئْبُ وَأَنتُمْ عَنْهُ غَـٰفِلُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:14}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: They said, "If a wolf should eat him while we are a [strong] clan, indeed, we would then be losers."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: They said: If the wolf should devour him when we are (so strong) a band, then surely we should have already perished.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالُوا۟ لَئِنْ أَكَلَهُ ٱلذِّئْبُ وَنَحْنُ عُصْبَةٌ إِنَّآ إِذًا لَّخَـٰسِرُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:15}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: So when they took him [out] and agreed to put him into the bottom of the well... But We inspired to him, "You will surely inform them [someday] about this affair of theirs while they do not perceive [your identity]."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Then, when they led him off, and were of one mind that they should place him in the depth of the pit, We inspired in him: Thou wilt tell them of this deed of theirs when they know (thee) not.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَلَمَّا ذَهَبُوا۟ بِهِ وَأَجْمَعُوٓا۟ أَن يَجْعَلُوهُ فِى غَيَـٰبَتِ ٱلْجُبِّ  وَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْهِ لَتُنَبِّئَنَّهُم بِأَمْرِهِمْ هَـٰذَا وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:16}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And they came to their father at night, weeping.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And they came weeping to their father in the evening.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَجَآءُوٓ أَبَاهُمْ عِشَآءً يَبْكُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:17}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: They said, "O our father, indeed we went racing each other and left Joseph with our possessions, and a wolf ate him. But you would not believe us, even if we were truthful."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Saying: O our father! We went racing one with another, and left Joseph by our things, and the wolf devoured him, and thou believest not our saying even when we speak the truth.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالُوا۟ يَـٰٓأَبَانَآ إِنَّا ذَهَبْنَا نَسْتَبِقُ وَتَرَكْنَا يُوسُفَ عِندَ مَتَـٰعِنَا فَأَكَلَهُ ٱلذِّئْبُ  وَمَآ أَنتَ بِمُؤْمِنٍ لَّنَا وَلَوْ كُنَّا صَـٰدِقِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:18}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And they brought upon his shirt false blood. [Jacob] said, "Rather, your souls have enticed you to something, so patience is most fitting. And Allāh is the one sought for help against that which you describe."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And they came with false blood on his shirt. He said: Nay, but your minds have beguiled you into something. (My course is) comely patience. And Allah it is Whose help is to be sought in that (predicament) which ye describe.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَجَآءُو عَلَىٰ قَمِيصِهِ بِدَمٍ كَذِبٍ  قَالَ بَلْ سَوَّلَتْ لَكُمْ أَنفُسُكُمْ أَمْرًا  فَصَبْرٌ جَمِيلٌ  وَٱللَّهُ ٱلْمُسْتَعَانُ عَلَىٰ مَا تَصِفُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:19}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And there came a company of travelers; then they sent their water drawer, and he let down his bucket. He said, "Good news! Here is a boy." And they concealed him, [taking him] as merchandise; and Allāh was Knowing of what they did.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And there came a caravan, and they sent their waterdrawer. He let down his pail (into the pit). He said: Good luck! Here is a youth. And they hid him as a treasure, and Allah was Aware of what they did.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَجَآءَتْ سَيَّارَةٌ فَأَرْسَلُوا۟ وَارِدَهُمْ فَأَدْلَىٰ دَلْوَهُ  قَالَ يَـٰبُشْرَىٰ هَـٰذَا غُلَـٰمٌ  وَأَسَرُّوهُ بِضَـٰعَةً  وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِمَا يَعْمَلُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:20}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And they sold him for a reduced price - a few dirhams - and they were, concerning him, of those content with little.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And they sold him for a low price, a number of silver coins; and they attached no value to him.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَشَرَوْهُ بِثَمَنٍۭ بَخْسٍ دَرَٰهِمَ مَعْدُودَةٍ وَكَانُوا۟ فِيهِ مِنَ ٱلزَّٰهِدِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:21}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And the one from Egypt who bought him said to his wife, "Make his residence comfortable. Perhaps he will benefit us, or we will adopt him as a son." And thus, We established Joseph in the land that We might teach him the interpretation of events [i.e., dreams]. And Allāh is predominant over His affair, but most of the people do not know.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And he of Egypt who purchased him said unto his wife: Receive him honourably. Perchance he may prove useful to us or we may adopt him as a son. Thus we established Joseph in the land that We might teach him the interpretation of events. And Allah was predominant in His career, but most of mankind know not.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِى ٱشْتَرَىٰهُ مِن مِّصْرَ لِٱمْرَأَتِهِٓ أَكْرِمِى مَثْوَىٰهُ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَنفَعَنَآ أَوْ نَتَّخِذَهُ وَلَدًا  وَكَذَٰلِكَ مَكَّنَّا لِيُوسُفَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَلِنُعَلِّمَهُ مِن تَأْوِيلِ ٱلْأَحَادِيثِ  وَٱللَّهُ غَالِبٌ عَلَىٰٓ أَمْرِهِ وَلَـٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:22}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And when he [i.e., Joseph] reached maturity, We gave him judgement and knowledge. And thus We reward the doers of good.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And And when he reached his prime We gave him wisdom and knowledge. Thus We reward the good.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَلَمَّا بَلَغَ أَشُدَّهُٓ ءَاتَيْنَـٰهُ حُكْمًا وَعِلْمًا  وَكَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:23}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And she, in whose house he was, sought to seduce him. She closed the doors and said, "Come, you." He said, "[I seek] the refuge of Allāh. Indeed, he is my master, who has made good my residence. Indeed, wrongdoers will not succeed."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And she, in whose house he was, asked of him an evil act. She bolted the doors and said: Come! He said: I seek refuge in Allah! Lo! he is my lord, who hath treated me honourably. Lo! wrong-doers never prosper.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَرَٰوَدَتْهُ ٱلَّتِى هُوَ فِى بَيْتِهَا عَن نَّفْسِهِ وَغَلَّقَتِ ٱلْأَبْوَٰبَ وَقَالَتْ هَيْتَ لَكَ  قَالَ مَعَاذَ ٱللَّهِ  إِنَّهُ رَبِّىٓ أَحْسَنَ مَثْوَاىَ  إِنَّهُ لَا يُفْلِحُ ٱلظَّـٰلِمُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:24}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And she certainly determined [to seduce] him, and he would have inclined to her had he not seen the proof [i.e., sign] of his Lord. And thus [it was] that We should avert from him evil and immorality. Indeed, he was of Our chosen servants.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: She verily desired him, and he would have desired her if it had not been that he saw the argument of his Lord. Thus it was, that We might ward off from him evil and lewdness. Lo! he was of Our chosen slaves.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَلَقَدْ هَمَّتْ بِهِ  وَهَمَّ بِهَا لَوْلَآ أَن رَّءَا بُرْهَـٰنَ رَبِّهِ  كَذَٰلِكَ لِنَصْرِفَ عَنْهُ ٱلسُّوٓءَ وَٱلْفَحْشَآءَ  إِنَّهُ مِنْ عِبَادِنَا ٱلْمُخْلَصِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:25}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And they both raced to the door, and she tore his shirt from the back, and they found her husband at the door. She said, "What is the recompense of one who intended evil for your wife but that he be imprisoned or a painful punishment?"

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And they raced with one another to the door, and she tore his shirt from behind, and they met her lord and master at the door. She said: What shall be his reward, who wisheth evil to thy folk, save prison or a painful doom?

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَٱسْتَبَقَا ٱلْبَابَ وَقَدَّتْ قَمِيصَهُ مِن دُبُرٍ وَأَلْفَيَا سَيِّدَهَا لَدَا ٱلْبَابِ  قَالَتْ مَا جَزَآءُ مَنْ أَرَادَ بِأَهْلِكَ سُوٓءًا إِلَّآ أَن يُسْجَنَ أَوْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:26}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: [Joseph] said, "It was she who sought to seduce me." And a witness from her family testified, "If his shirt is torn from the front, then she has told the truth, and he is of the liars.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: (Joseph) said: She it was who asked of me an evil act. And a witness of her own folk testified: If his shirt is torn from before, then she speaketh truth and he is of the liars.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَ هِىَ رَٰوَدَتْنِى عَن نَّفْسِى  وَشَهِدَ شَاهِدٌ مِّنْ أَهْلِهَآ إِن كَانَ قَمِيصُهُ قُدَّ مِن قُبُلٍ فَصَدَقَتْ وَهُوَ مِنَ ٱلْكَـٰذِبِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:27}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: But if his shirt is torn from the back, then she has lied, and he is of the truthful."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And if his shirt is torn from behind, then she hath lied and he is of the truthful.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَإِن كَانَ قَمِيصُهُ قُدَّ مِن دُبُرٍ فَكَذَبَتْ وَهُوَ مِنَ ٱلصَّـٰدِقِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:28}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: So when he [i.e., her husband] saw his shirt torn from the back, he said, "Indeed, it is of your [i.e., women's] plan. Indeed, your plan is great [i.e., vehement].

\textit{M. Pickthall}: So when he saw his shirt torn from behind, he said: Lo! this is of the guile of you women. Lo! the guile of you is very great.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَلَمَّا رَءَا قَمِيصَهُ قُدَّ مِن دُبُرٍ قَالَ إِنَّهُ مِن كَيْدِكُنَّ  إِنَّ كَيْدَكُنَّ عَظِيمٌ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:29}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Joseph, ignore this. And, [my wife], ask forgiveness for your sin. Indeed, you were of the sinful."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: O Joseph! Turn away from this, and thou, (O woman), ask forgiveness for thy sin. Lo! thou art of the faulty.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
يُوسُفُ أَعْرِضْ عَنْ هَـٰذَا  وَٱسْتَغْفِرِى لِذَنبِكِ  إِنَّكِ كُنتِ مِنَ ٱلْخَاطِـِٔينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:30}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And women in the city said, "The wife of al-ʿAzeez is seeking to seduce her slave boy; he has impassioned her with love. Indeed, we see her [to be] in clear error."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And women in the city said: The ruler's wife is asking of her slave-boy an ill-deed. Indeed he has smitten her to the heart with love. We behold her in plain aberration.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
۞ وَقَالَ نِسْوَةٌ فِى ٱلْمَدِينَةِ ٱمْرَأَتُ ٱلْعَزِيزِ تُرَٰوِدُ فَتَىٰهَا عَن نَّفْسِهِ  قَدْ شَغَفَهَا حُبًّا  إِنَّا لَنَرَىٰهَا فِى ضَلَـٰلٍ مُّبِينٍ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:31}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: So when she heard of their scheming, she sent for them and prepared for them a banquet and gave each one of them a knife and said [to Joseph], "Come out before them." And when they saw him, they greatly admired him and cut their hands and said, "Perfect is Allāh! This is not a man; this is none but a noble angel."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And when she heard of their sly talk, she sent to them and prepared for them a cushioned couch (to lie on at the feast) and gave to every one of them a knife and said (to Joseph): Come out unto them! And when they saw him they exalted him and cut their hands, exclaiming: Allah Blameless! This is no a human being. This is not other than some gracious angel.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ بِمَكْرِهِنَّ أَرْسَلَتْ إِلَيْهِنَّ وَأَعْتَدَتْ لَهُنَّ مُتَّكَـًٔا وَءَاتَتْ كُلَّ وَٰحِدَةٍ مِّنْهُنَّ سِكِّينًا وَقَالَتِ ٱخْرُجْ عَلَيْهِنَّ  فَلَمَّا رَأَيْنَهُٓ أَكْبَرْنَهُ وَقَطَّعْنَ أَيْدِيَهُنَّ وَقُلْنَ حَـٰشَ لِلَّهِ مَا هَـٰذَا بَشَرًا إِنْ هَـٰذَآ إِلَّا مَلَكٌ كَرِيمٌ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:32}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: She said, "That is the one about whom you blamed me. And I certainly sought to seduce him, but he firmly refused; and if he will not do what I order him, he will surely be imprisoned and will be of those debased."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: She said: This is he on whose account ye blamed me. I asked of him an evil act, but he proved continent, but if he do not my behest he verily shall be imprisoned, and verily shall be of those brought low.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَتْ فَذَٰلِكُنَّ ٱلَّذِى لُمْتُنَّنِى فِيهِ  وَلَقَدْ رَٰوَدتُّهُ عَن نَّفْسِهِ فَٱسْتَعْصَمَ  وَلَئِن لَّمْ يَفْعَلْ مَآ ءَامُرُهُ لَيُسْجَنَنَّ وَلَيَكُونًا مِّنَ ٱلصَّـٰغِرِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:33}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: He said, "My Lord, prison is more to my liking than that to which they invite me. And if You do not avert from me their plan, I might incline toward them and [thus] be of the ignorant."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: He said: O my Lord! Prison is more dear than that unto which they urge me, and if Thou fend not off their wiles from me I shall incline unto them and become of the foolish.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَ رَبِّ ٱلسِّجْنُ أَحَبُّ إِلَىَّ مِمَّا يَدْعُونَنِىٓ إِلَيْهِ  وَإِلَّا تَصْرِفْ عَنِّى كَيْدَهُنَّ أَصْبُ إِلَيْهِنَّ وَأَكُن مِّنَ ٱلْجَـٰهِلِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:34}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: So his Lord responded to him and averted from him their plan. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: So his Lord heard his prayer and fended off their wiles from him. Lo! He is Hearer, Knower.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَٱسْتَجَابَ لَهُ رَبُّهُ فَصَرَفَ عَنْهُ كَيْدَهُنَّ  إِنَّهُ هُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:35}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Then it appeared to them after they had seen the signs that he [i.e., al-ʿAzeez] should surely imprison him for a time.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And it seemed good to them (the men-folk) after they had seen the signs (of his innocence) to imprison him for a time.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
ثُمَّ بَدَا لَهُم مِّن بَعْدِ مَا رَأَوُا۟ ٱلْـَٔايَـٰتِ لَيَسْجُنُنَّهُ حَتَّىٰ حِينٍ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:36}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And there entered the prison with him two young men. One of them said, "Indeed, I have seen myself [in a dream] pressing [grapes for] wine." The other said, "Indeed, I have seen myself carrying upon my head [some] bread, from which the birds were eating. Inform us of its interpretation; indeed, we see you to be of those who do good."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And two young men went to prison with him. One of them said: I dreamed that I was pressing wine. The other said: I dreamed that I was carrying upon my head bread whereof the birds were eating. Announce unto us the interpretation, for we see thee of those good (at interpretation).

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَدَخَلَ مَعَهُ ٱلسِّجْنَ فَتَيَانِ  قَالَ أَحَدُهُمَآ إِنِّىٓ أَرَىٰنِىٓ أَعْصِرُ خَمْرًا  وَقَالَ ٱلْـَٔاخَرُ إِنِّىٓ أَرَىٰنِىٓ أَحْمِلُ فَوْقَ رَأْسِى خُبْزًا تَأْكُلُ ٱلطَّيْرُ مِنْهُ  نَبِّئْنَا بِتَأْوِيلِهِٓ  إِنَّا نَرَىٰكَ مِنَ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:37}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: He said, "You will not receive food that is provided to you except that I will inform you of its interpretation before it comes to you. That is from what my Lord has taught me. Indeed, I have left the religion of a people who do not believe in Allāh, and they, in the Hereafter, are disbelievers.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: He said: The food which ye are given (daily) shall not come unto you but I shall tell you the interpretation ere it cometh unto you. This is of that which my Lord hath taught me. Lo! I have forsaken the religion of folk who believe not in Allah and are disbelievers in the Hereafter.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَ لَا يَأْتِيكُمَا طَعَامٌ تُرْزَقَانِهِٓ إِلَّا نَبَّأْتُكُمَا بِتَأْوِيلِهِ قَبْلَ أَن يَأْتِيَكُمَا  ذَٰلِكُمَا مِمَّا عَلَّمَنِى رَبِّىٓ  إِنِّى تَرَكْتُ مِلَّةَ قَوْمٍ لَّا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَهُم بِٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ هُمْ كَـٰفِرُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:38}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And I have followed the religion of my fathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. And it was not for us to associate anything with Allāh. That is from the favor of Allāh upon us and upon the people, but most of the people are not grateful.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And I have followed the religion of my fathers, Abraham and Isaac and Jacob. It never was for us to attribute aught as partner to Allah. This is of the bounty of Allah unto us (the seed of Abraham) and unto mankind; but most men give not thanks.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَٱتَّبَعْتُ مِلَّةَ ءَابَآءِىٓ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ وَإِسْحَـٰقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ  مَا كَانَ لَنَآ أَن نُّشْرِكَ بِٱللَّهِ مِن شَىْءٍ  ذَٰلِكَ مِن فَضْلِ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْنَا وَعَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ وَلَـٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَشْكُرُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:39}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: O [my] two companions of prison, are separate lords better or Allāh, the One, the Prevailing?

\textit{M. Pickthall}: O my fellow-prisoners! Are divers lords better, or Allah the One, Almighty?

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
يَـٰصَـٰحِبَىِ ٱلسِّجْنِ ءَأَرْبَابٌ مُّتَفَرِّقُونَ خَيْرٌ أَمِ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْوَٰحِدُ ٱلْقَهَّارُ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:40}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: You worship not besides Him except [mere] names you have named them, you and your fathers, for which Allāh has sent down no evidence. Legislation is not but for Allāh. He has commanded that you worship not except Him. That is the correct religion, but most of the people do not know.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Those whom ye worship beside Him are but names which ye have named, ye and your fathers. Allah hath revealed no sanction for them. The decision rests with Allah only, Who hath commanded you that ye worship none save Him. This is the right religion, but most men know not.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
مَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِهِٓ إِلَّآ أَسْمَآءً سَمَّيْتُمُوهَآ أَنتُمْ وَءَابَآؤُكُم مَّآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ بِهَا مِن سُلْطَـٰنٍ  إِنِ ٱلْحُكْمُ إِلَّا لِلَّهِ  أَمَرَ أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ إِيَّاهُ  ذَٰلِكَ ٱلدِّينُ ٱلْقَيِّمُ وَلَـٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:41}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: O two companions of prison, as for one of you, he will give drink to his master of wine; but as for the other, he will be crucified, and the birds will eat from his head. The matter has been decreed about which you both inquire."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: O my two fellow-prisoners! As for one of you, he will pour out wine for his lord to drink; and as for the other, he will be crucified so that the birds will eat from his head. Thus is the case judged concerning which ye did inquire.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
يَـٰصَـٰحِبَىِ ٱلسِّجْنِ أَمَّآ أَحَدُكُمَا فَيَسْقِى رَبَّهُ خَمْرًا  وَأَمَّا ٱلْـَٔاخَرُ فَيُصْلَبُ فَتَأْكُلُ ٱلطَّيْرُ مِن رَّأْسِهِ  قُضِىَ ٱلْأَمْرُ ٱلَّذِى فِيهِ تَسْتَفْتِيَانِ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:42}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And he said to the one whom he knew would go free, "Mention me before your master." But Satan made him forget the mention [to] his master, and he [i.e., Joseph] remained in prison several years.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And he said unto him of the twain who he knew would be released: Mention me in the presence of thy lord. But Satan caused him to forget to mention it to his lord, so he (Joseph) stayed in prison for some years.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَقَالَ لِلَّذِى ظَنَّ أَنَّهُ نَاجٍ مِّنْهُمَا ٱذْكُرْنِى عِندَ رَبِّكَ فَأَنسَىٰهُ ٱلشَّيْطَـٰنُ ذِكْرَ رَبِّهِ فَلَبِثَ فِى ٱلسِّجْنِ بِضْعَ سِنِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:43}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And [subsequently] the king said, "Indeed, I have seen [in a dream] seven fat cows being eaten by seven [that were] lean, and seven green spikes [of grain] and others [that were] dry. O eminent ones, explain to me my vision, if you should interpret visions."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And the king said: Lo! I saw in a dream seven fat kine which seven lean were eating, and seven green ears of corn and other (seven) dry. O notables! Expound for me my vision, if ye can interpret dreams.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَقَالَ ٱلْمَلِكُ إِنِّىٓ أَرَىٰ سَبْعَ بَقَرَٰتٍ سِمَانٍ يَأْكُلُهُنَّ سَبْعٌ عِجَافٌ وَسَبْعَ سُنبُلَـٰتٍ خُضْرٍ وَأُخَرَ يَابِسَـٰتٍ  يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْمَلَأُ أَفْتُونِى فِى رُءْيَـٰىَ إِن كُنتُمْ لِلرُّءْيَا تَعْبُرُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:44}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: They said, "[It is but] a mixture of false dreams, and we are not learned in the interpretation of dreams."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: They answered: Jumbled dreams! And we are not knowing in the interpretation of dreams.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالُوٓا۟ أَضْغَـٰثُ أَحْلَـٰمٍ  وَمَا نَحْنُ بِتَأْوِيلِ ٱلْأَحْلَـٰمِ بِعَـٰلِمِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:45}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: But the one who was freed and remembered after a time said, "I will inform you of its interpretation, so send me forth."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And he of the two who was released, and (now) at length remembered, said: I am going to announce unto you the interpretation, therefore send me forth.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِى نَجَا مِنْهُمَا وَٱدَّكَرَ بَعْدَ أُمَّةٍ أَنَا أُنَبِّئُكُم بِتَأْوِيلِهِ فَأَرْسِلُونِ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:46}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: [He said], "Joseph, O man of truth, explain to us about seven fat cows eaten by seven [that were] lean, and seven green spikes [of grain] and others [that were] dry - that I may return to the people [i.e., the king and his court]; perhaps they will know [about you]."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: (And when he came to Joseph in the prison, he exclaimed): Joseph! O thou truthful one! Expound for us the seven fat kine which seven lean were eating and the seven green ears of corn and other (seven) dry, that I may return unto the people, so that they may know.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
يُوسُفُ أَيُّهَا ٱلصِّدِّيقُ أَفْتِنَا فِى سَبْعِ بَقَرَٰتٍ سِمَانٍ يَأْكُلُهُنَّ سَبْعٌ عِجَافٌ وَسَبْعِ سُنبُلَـٰتٍ خُضْرٍ وَأُخَرَ يَابِسَـٰتٍ لَّعَلِّىٓ أَرْجِعُ إِلَى ٱلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:47}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: [Joseph] said, "You will plant for seven years consecutively; and what you harvest leave in its spikes, except a little from which you will eat.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: He said: Ye shall sow seven years as usual, but that which ye reap, leave it in the ear, all save a little which ye eat.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَ تَزْرَعُونَ سَبْعَ سِنِينَ دَأَبًا فَمَا حَصَدتُّمْ فَذَرُوهُ فِى سُنبُلِهِٓ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِّمَّا تَأْكُلُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:48}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Then will come after that seven difficult [years] which will consume what you advanced [i.e., saved] for them, except a little from which you will store.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Then after that will come seven hard years which will devour all that ye have prepared for them, save a little of that which ye have stored.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
ثُمَّ يَأْتِى مِن بَعْدِ ذَٰلِكَ سَبْعٌ شِدَادٌ يَأْكُلْنَ مَا قَدَّمْتُمْ لَهُنَّ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِّمَّا تُحْصِنُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:49}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Then will come after that a year in which the people will be given rain and in which they will press [olives and grapes]."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Then, after that, will come a year when the people will have plenteous crops and when they will press (wine and oil).

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
ثُمَّ يَأْتِى مِن بَعْدِ ذَٰلِكَ عَامٌ فِيهِ يُغَاثُ ٱلنَّاسُ وَفِيهِ يَعْصِرُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:50}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And the king said, "Bring him to me." But when the messenger came to him, [Joseph] said, "Return to your master and ask him what is the case of the women who cut their hands. Indeed, my Lord is Knowing of their plan."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And the king said: Bring him unto me. And when the messenger came unto him, he (Joseph) said: Return unto thy lord and ask him what was the case of the women who cut their hands. Lo! my Lord knoweth their guile.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَقَالَ ٱلْمَلِكُ ٱئْتُونِى بِهِ  فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُ ٱلرَّسُولُ قَالَ ٱرْجِعْ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ فَسْـَٔلْهُ مَا بَالُ ٱلنِّسْوَةِ ٱلَّـٰتِى قَطَّعْنَ أَيْدِيَهُنَّ  إِنَّ رَبِّى بِكَيْدِهِنَّ عَلِيمٌ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:51}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Said [the king to the women], "What was your condition when you sought to seduce Joseph?" They said, "Perfect is Allāh! We know about him no evil." The wife of al-ʿAzeez said, "Now the truth has become evident. It was I who sought to seduce him, and indeed, he is of the truthful.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: He (the king) (then sent for those women and) said: What happened when ye asked an evil act of Joseph? They answered: Allah Blameless! We know no evil of him. Said the wife of the ruler: Now the truth is out. I asked of him an evil act, and he is surely of the truthful.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَ مَا خَطْبُكُنَّ إِذْ رَٰوَدتُّنَّ يُوسُفَ عَن نَّفْسِهِ  قُلْنَ حَـٰشَ لِلَّهِ مَا عَلِمْنَا عَلَيْهِ مِن سُوٓءٍ  قَالَتِ ٱمْرَأَتُ ٱلْعَزِيزِ ٱلْـَٔـٰنَ حَصْحَصَ ٱلْحَقُّ أَنَا رَٰوَدتُّهُ عَن نَّفْسِهِ وَإِنَّهُ لَمِنَ ٱلصَّـٰدِقِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:52}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: That is so he [i.e., al-ʿAzeez] will know that I did not betray him in [his] absence and that Allāh does not guide the plan of betrayers.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: (Then Joseph said: I asked for) this, that he (my lord) may know that I betrayed him not in secret, and that surely Allah guideth not the snare of the betrayers.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
ذَٰلِكَ لِيَعْلَمَ أَنِّى لَمْ أَخُنْهُ بِٱلْغَيْبِ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِى كَيْدَ ٱلْخَآئِنِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:53}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And I do not acquit myself. Indeed, the soul is a persistent enjoiner of evil, except those upon which my Lord has mercy. Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: I do not exculpate myself. Lo! the (human) soul enjoineth unto evil, save that whereon my Lord hath mercy. Lo! my Lord is Forgiving, Merciful.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
۞ وَمَآ أُبَرِّئُ نَفْسِىٓ  إِنَّ ٱلنَّفْسَ لَأَمَّارَةٌ بِٱلسُّوٓءِ إِلَّا مَا رَحِمَ رَبِّىٓ  إِنَّ رَبِّى غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:54}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And the king said, "Bring him to me; I will appoint him exclusively for myself." And when he spoke to him, he said, "Indeed, you are today established [in position] and trusted."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And the king said: Bring him unto me that I may attach him to my person. And when he had talked with him he said: Lo! thou art to-day in our presence established and trusted.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَقَالَ ٱلْمَلِكُ ٱئْتُونِى بِهِٓ أَسْتَخْلِصْهُ لِنَفْسِى  فَلَمَّا كَلَّمَهُ قَالَ إِنَّكَ ٱلْيَوْمَ لَدَيْنَا مَكِينٌ أَمِينٌ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:55}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: [Joseph] said, "Appoint me over the storehouses of the land. Indeed, I will be a knowing guardian."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: He said: Set me over the storehouses of the land. Lo! I am a skilled custodian.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَ ٱجْعَلْنِى عَلَىٰ خَزَآئِنِ ٱلْأَرْضِ  إِنِّى حَفِيظٌ عَلِيمٌ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:56}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And thus We established Joseph in the land to settle therein wherever he willed. We touch with Our mercy whom We will, and We do not allow to be lost the reward of those who do good.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Thus gave We power to Joseph in the land. He was the owner of it where he pleased. We reach with Our mercy whom We will. We lose not the reward of the good.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَكَذَٰلِكَ مَكَّنَّا لِيُوسُفَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ يَتَبَوَّأُ مِنْهَا حَيْثُ يَشَآءُ  نُصِيبُ بِرَحْمَتِنَا مَن نَّشَآءُ  وَلَا نُضِيعُ أَجْرَ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:57}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And the reward of the Hereafter is better for those who believed and were fearing Allāh.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And the reward of the Hereafter is better, for those who believe and ward off (evil).

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَلَأَجْرُ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ خَيْرٌ لِّلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَكَانُوا۟ يَتَّقُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:58}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And the brothers of Joseph came [seeking food], and they entered upon him; and he recognized them, but he was to them unknown.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And Joseph's brethren came and presented themselves before him, and he knew them but they knew him not.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَجَآءَ إِخْوَةُ يُوسُفَ فَدَخَلُوا۟ عَلَيْهِ فَعَرَفَهُمْ وَهُمْ لَهُ مُنكِرُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:59}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And when he had furnished them with their supplies, he said, "Bring me a brother of yours from your father. Do you not see that I give full measure and that I am the best of accommodators?

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And when he provided them with their provision he said: Bring unto me a brother of yours from your father. See ye not that I fill up the measure and I am the best of hosts?

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَلَمَّا جَهَّزَهُم بِجَهَازِهِمْ قَالَ ٱئْتُونِى بِأَخٍ لَّكُم مِّنْ أَبِيكُمْ  أَلَا تَرَوْنَ أَنِّىٓ أُوفِى ٱلْكَيْلَ وَأَنَا خَيْرُ ٱلْمُنزِلِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:60}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: But if you do not bring him to me, no measure will there be [hereafter] for you from me, nor will you approach me."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And if ye bring him not unto me, then there shall be no measure for you with me, nor shall ye draw near.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَإِن لَّمْ تَأْتُونِى بِهِ فَلَا كَيْلَ لَكُمْ عِندِى وَلَا تَقْرَبُونِ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:61}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: They said, "We will attempt to dissuade his father from [keeping] him, and indeed, we will do [it]."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: They said: We will try to win him from his father: that we will surely do.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالُوا۟ سَنُرَٰوِدُ عَنْهُ أَبَاهُ وَإِنَّا لَفَـٰعِلُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:62}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And [Joseph] said to his servants, "Put their merchandise into their saddlebags so they might recognize it when they have gone back to their people that perhaps they will [again] return."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: He said unto his young men: Place their merchandise in their saddlebags, so that they may know it when they go back to their folk, and so will come again.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَقَالَ لِفِتْيَـٰنِهِ ٱجْعَلُوا۟ بِضَـٰعَتَهُمْ فِى رِحَالِهِمْ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَعْرِفُونَهَآ إِذَا ٱنقَلَبُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰٓ أَهْلِهِمْ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:63}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: So when they returned to their father, they said, "O our father, [further] measure has been denied to us, so send with us our brother [that] we will be given measure. And indeed, we will be his guardians."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: So when they went back to their father they said: O our father! The measure is denied us, so send with us our brother that we may obtain the measure, surely we will guard him well.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَلَمَّا رَجَعُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰٓ أَبِيهِمْ قَالُوا۟ يَـٰٓأَبَانَا مُنِعَ مِنَّا ٱلْكَيْلُ فَأَرْسِلْ مَعَنَآ أَخَانَا نَكْتَلْ وَإِنَّا لَهُ لَحَـٰفِظُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:64}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: He said, "Should I entrust you with him except [under coercion] as I entrusted you with his brother before? But Allāh is the best guardian, and He is the most merciful of the merciful."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: He said: Can I entrust him to you save as I entrusted his brother to you aforetime? Allah is better at guarding, and He is the Most Merciful of those who show mercy.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَ هَلْ ءَامَنُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ إِلَّا كَمَآ أَمِنتُكُمْ عَلَىٰٓ أَخِيهِ مِن قَبْلُ  فَٱللَّهُ خَيْرٌ حَـٰفِظًا  وَهُوَ أَرْحَمُ ٱلرَّٰحِمِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:65}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And when they opened their baggage, they found their merchandise returned to them. They said, "O our father, what [more] could we desire? This is our merchandise returned to us. And we will obtain supplies [i.e., food] for our family and protect our brother and obtain an increase of a camel's load; that is an easy measurement."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And when they opened their belongings they discovered that their merchandise had been returned to them. They said: O our father! What (more) can we ask? Here is our merchandise returned to us. We shall get provision for our folk and guard our brother, and we shall have the extra measure of a camel (load). This (that we bring now) is a light measure.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَلَمَّا فَتَحُوا۟ مَتَـٰعَهُمْ وَجَدُوا۟ بِضَـٰعَتَهُمْ رُدَّتْ إِلَيْهِمْ  قَالُوا۟ يَـٰٓأَبَانَا مَا نَبْغِى  هَـٰذِهِ بِضَـٰعَتُنَا رُدَّتْ إِلَيْنَا  وَنَمِيرُ أَهْلَنَا وَنَحْفَظُ أَخَانَا وَنَزْدَادُ كَيْلَ بَعِيرٍ  ذَٰلِكَ كَيْلٌ يَسِيرٌ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:66}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: [Jacob] said, "Never will I send him with you until you give me a promise [i.e., oath] by Allāh that you will bring him [back] to me, unless you should be surrounded [i.e., overcome by enemies]." And when they had given their promise, he said, "Allāh, over what we say, is Entrusted."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: He said: I will not send him with you till ye give me an undertaking in the name of Allah that ye will bring him back to me, unless ye are surrounded. And when they gave him their undertaking he said: Allah is the Warden over what we say.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَ لَنْ أُرْسِلَهُ مَعَكُمْ حَتَّىٰ تُؤْتُونِ مَوْثِقًا مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ لَتَأْتُنَّنِى بِهِٓ إِلَّآ أَن يُحَاطَ بِكُمْ  فَلَمَّآ ءَاتَوْهُ مَوْثِقَهُمْ قَالَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ مَا نَقُولُ وَكِيلٌ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:67}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And he said, "O my sons, do not enter from one gate but enter from different gates; and I cannot avail you against [the decree of] Allāh at all. The decision is only for Allāh; upon Him I have relied, and upon Him let those who would rely [indeed] rely."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And he said: O my sons! Go not in by one gate; go in by different gates. I can naught avail you as against Allah. Lo! the decision rests with Allah only. In Him do I put my trust, and in Him let all the trusting put their trust.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَقَالَ يَـٰبَنِىَّ لَا تَدْخُلُوا۟ مِن بَابٍ وَٰحِدٍ وَٱدْخُلُوا۟ مِنْ أَبْوَٰبٍ مُّتَفَرِّقَةٍ  وَمَآ أُغْنِى عَنكُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ مِن شَىْءٍ  إِنِ ٱلْحُكْمُ إِلَّا لِلَّهِ  عَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ  وَعَلَيْهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ ٱلْمُتَوَكِّلُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:68}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And when they entered from where their father had ordered them, it did not avail them against Allāh at all except [it was] a need [i.e., concern] within the soul of Jacob, which he satisfied. And indeed, he was a possessor of knowledge because of what We had taught him, but most of the people do not know.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And when they entered in the manner which their father had enjoined, it would have naught availed them as against Allah; it was but a need of Jacob's soul which he thus satisfied; and lo! he was a lord of knowledge because We had taught him; but most of mankind know not.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَلَمَّا دَخَلُوا۟ مِنْ حَيْثُ أَمَرَهُمْ أَبُوهُم مَّا كَانَ يُغْنِى عَنْهُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ مِن شَىْءٍ إِلَّا حَاجَةً فِى نَفْسِ يَعْقُوبَ قَضَىٰهَا  وَإِنَّهُ لَذُو عِلْمٍ لِّمَا عَلَّمْنَـٰهُ وَلَـٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:69}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And when they entered upon Joseph, he took his brother to himself; he said, "Indeed, I am your brother, so do not despair over what they used to do [to me]."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And when they went in before Joseph, he took his brother unto him, saying: Lo! I, even I, am thy brother, therefore sorrow not for what they did.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَلَمَّا دَخَلُوا۟ عَلَىٰ يُوسُفَ ءَاوَىٰٓ إِلَيْهِ أَخَاهُ  قَالَ إِنِّىٓ أَنَا أَخُوكَ فَلَا تَبْتَئِسْ بِمَا كَانُوا۟ يَعْمَلُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:70}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: So when he had furnished them with their supplies, he put the [gold measuring] bowl into the bag of his brother. Then an announcer called out, "O caravan, indeed you are thieves."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And when he provided them with their provision, he put the drinking-cup in his brother's saddlebag, and then a crier cried: O camel-riders! Lo! ye are surely thieves!

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَلَمَّا جَهَّزَهُم بِجَهَازِهِمْ جَعَلَ ٱلسِّقَايَةَ فِى رَحْلِ أَخِيهِ ثُمَّ أَذَّنَ مُؤَذِّنٌ أَيَّتُهَا ٱلْعِيرُ إِنَّكُمْ لَسَـٰرِقُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:71}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: They said while approaching them, "What is it you are missing?"

\textit{M. Pickthall}: They cried, coming toward them: What is it ye have lost?

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالُوا۟ وَأَقْبَلُوا۟ عَلَيْهِم مَّاذَا تَفْقِدُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:72}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: They said, "We are missing the measure of the king. And for he who produces it is [the reward of] a camel's load, and I am responsible for it."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: They said: We have lost the king's cup, and he who bringeth it shall have a camel-load, and I (said Joseph) am answerable for it.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالُوا۟ نَفْقِدُ صُوَاعَ ٱلْمَلِكِ وَلِمَن جَآءَ بِهِ حِمْلُ بَعِيرٍ وَأَنَا بِهِ زَعِيمٌ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:73}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: They said, "By Allāh, you have certainly known that we did not come to cause corruption in the land, and we have not been thieves."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: They said: By Allah, well ye know we came not to do evil in the land, and are no thieves.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالُوا۟ تَٱللَّهِ لَقَدْ عَلِمْتُم مَّا جِئْنَا لِنُفْسِدَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا كُنَّا سَـٰرِقِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:74}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: They [the accusers] said, "Then what would be its recompense if you should be liars?"

\textit{M. Pickthall}: They said: And what shall be the penalty for it, if ye prove liars?

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالُوا۟ فَمَا جَزَٰٓؤُهُٓ إِن كُنتُمْ كَـٰذِبِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:75}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: [The brothers] said, "Its recompense is that he in whose bag it is found - he [himself] will be its recompense. Thus do we recompense the wrongdoers."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: They said: The penalty for it! He in whose bag (the cup) is found, he is the penalty for it. Thus we requite wrong-doers.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالُوا۟ جَزَٰٓؤُهُ مَن وُجِدَ فِى رَحْلِهِ فَهُوَ جَزَٰٓؤُهُ  كَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى ٱلظَّـٰلِمِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:76}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: So he began [the search] with their bags before the bag of his brother; then he extracted it from the bag of his brother. Thus did We plan for Joseph. He could not have taken his brother within the religion [i.e., law] of the king except that Allāh willed. We raise in degrees whom We will, but over every possessor of knowledge is one [more] knowing.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Then he (Joseph) began the search with their bags before his brother's bag, then he produced it from his brother's bag. Thus did We contrive for Joseph. He could not have taken his brother according to the king's law unless Allah willed. We raise by grades (of mercy) whom We will, and over every lord of knowledge there is one more knowing.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَبَدَأَ بِأَوْعِيَتِهِمْ قَبْلَ وِعَآءِ أَخِيهِ ثُمَّ ٱسْتَخْرَجَهَا مِن وِعَآءِ أَخِيهِ  كَذَٰلِكَ كِدْنَا لِيُوسُفَ  مَا كَانَ لِيَأْخُذَ أَخَاهُ فِى دِينِ ٱلْمَلِكِ إِلَّآ أَن يَشَآءَ ٱللَّهُ  نَرْفَعُ دَرَجَـٰتٍ مَّن نَّشَآءُ  وَفَوْقَ كُلِّ ذِى عِلْمٍ عَلِيمٌ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:77}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: They said, "If he steals - a brother of his has stolen before." But Joseph kept it within himself and did not reveal it to them. He said, "You are worse in position, and Allāh is most knowing of what you describe."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: They said: If he stealeth, a brother of his stole before. But Joseph kept it secret in his soul and revealed it not unto them. He said (within himself): Ye are in worse case, and Allah knoweth best (the truth of) that which ye allege.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
۞ قَالُوٓا۟ إِن يَسْرِقْ فَقَدْ سَرَقَ أَخٌ لَّهُ مِن قَبْلُ  فَأَسَرَّهَا يُوسُفُ فِى نَفْسِهِ وَلَمْ يُبْدِهَا لَهُمْ  قَالَ أَنتُمْ شَرٌّ مَّكَانًا  وَٱللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا تَصِفُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:78}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: They said, "O ʿAzeez, indeed he has a father [who is] an old man, so take one of us in place of him. Indeed, we see you as a doer of good."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: They said: O ruler of the land! Lo! he hath a very aged father, so take one of us instead of him. Lo! we behold thee of those who do kindness.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالُوا۟ يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْعَزِيزُ إِنَّ لَهُٓ أَبًا شَيْخًا كَبِيرًا فَخُذْ أَحَدَنَا مَكَانَهُٓ  إِنَّا نَرَىٰكَ مِنَ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:79}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: He said, "[I seek] the refuge of Allāh [to prevent] that we take except him with whom we found our possession. Indeed, we would then be unjust."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: He said: Allah forbid that we should seize save him with whom we found our property; then truly we should be wrong-doers.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَ مَعَاذَ ٱللَّهِ أَن نَّأْخُذَ إِلَّا مَن وَجَدْنَا مَتَـٰعَنَا عِندَهُٓ إِنَّآ إِذًا لَّظَـٰلِمُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:80}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: So when they had despaired of him, they secluded themselves in private consultation. The eldest of them said, "Do you not know that your father has taken upon you an oath by Allāh and [that] before you failed in [your duty to] Joseph? So I will never leave [this] land until my father permits me or Allāh decides for me, and He is the best of judges.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: So, When they despaired of (moving) him, they conferred together apart. The eldest of them said: Know ye not how your father took an undertaking from you in Allah's name and how ye failed in the case of Joseph aforetime? Therefore I shall not go forth from the land until my father giveth leave or Allah judgeth for me. He is the Best of Judges.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَلَمَّا ٱسْتَيْـَٔسُوا۟ مِنْهُ خَلَصُوا۟ نَجِيًّا  قَالَ كَبِيرُهُمْ أَلَمْ تَعْلَمُوٓا۟ أَنَّ أَبَاكُمْ قَدْ أَخَذَ عَلَيْكُم مَّوْثِقًا مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَمِن قَبْلُ مَا فَرَّطتُمْ فِى يُوسُفَ  فَلَنْ أَبْرَحَ ٱلْأَرْضَ حَتَّىٰ يَأْذَنَ لِىٓ أَبِىٓ أَوْ يَحْكُمَ ٱللَّهُ لِى  وَهُوَ خَيْرُ ٱلْحَـٰكِمِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:81}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Return to your father and say, 'O our father, indeed your son has stolen, and we did not testify except to what we knew. And we were not witnesses of the unseen.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Return unto your father and say: O our father! Lo! thy son hath stolen. We testify only to that which we know; we are not guardians of the Unseen.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
ٱرْجِعُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰٓ أَبِيكُمْ فَقُولُوا۟ يَـٰٓأَبَانَآ إِنَّ ٱبْنَكَ سَرَقَ وَمَا شَهِدْنَآ إِلَّا بِمَا عَلِمْنَا وَمَا كُنَّا لِلْغَيْبِ حَـٰفِظِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:82}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And ask the city in which we were and the caravan in which we came - and indeed, we are truthful.'"

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Ask the township where we were, and the caravan with which we travelled hither. Lo! we speak the truth.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَسْـَٔلِ ٱلْقَرْيَةَ ٱلَّتِى كُنَّا فِيهَا وَٱلْعِيرَ ٱلَّتِىٓ أَقْبَلْنَا فِيهَا  وَإِنَّا لَصَـٰدِقُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:83}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: [Jacob] said, "Rather, your souls have enticed you to something, so patience is most fitting. Perhaps Allāh will bring them to me all together. Indeed, it is He who is the Knowing, the Wise."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: (And when they came unto their father and had spoken thus to him) he said: Nay, but your minds have beguiled you into something. (My course is) comely patience! It may be that Allah will bring them all unto me. Lo! He, only He, is the Knower, the Wise.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَ بَلْ سَوَّلَتْ لَكُمْ أَنفُسُكُمْ أَمْرًا  فَصَبْرٌ جَمِيلٌ  عَسَى ٱللَّهُ أَن يَأْتِيَنِى بِهِمْ جَمِيعًا  إِنَّهُ هُوَ ٱلْعَلِيمُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:84}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And he turned away from them and said, "Oh, my sorrow over Joseph," and his eyes became white from grief, for he was [of that] a suppressor.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And he turned away from them and said: Alas, my grief for Joseph! And his eyes were whitened with the sorrow that he was suppressing.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَتَوَلَّىٰ عَنْهُمْ وَقَالَ يَـٰٓأَسَفَىٰ عَلَىٰ يُوسُفَ وَٱبْيَضَّتْ عَيْنَاهُ مِنَ ٱلْحُزْنِ فَهُوَ كَظِيمٌ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:85}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: They said, "By Allāh, you will not cease remembering Joseph until you become fatally ill or become of those who perish."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: They said: By Allah, thou wilt never cease remembering Joseph till thy health is ruined or thou art of those who perish!

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالُوا۟ تَٱللَّهِ تَفْتَؤُا۟ تَذْكُرُ يُوسُفَ حَتَّىٰ تَكُونَ حَرَضًا أَوْ تَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْهَـٰلِكِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:86}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: He said, "I only complain of my suffering and my grief to Allāh, and I know from Allāh that which you do not know.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: He said: I expose my distress and anguish only unto Allah, and I know from Allah that which ye know not.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَ إِنَّمَآ أَشْكُوا۟ بَثِّى وَحُزْنِىٓ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَأَعْلَمُ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:87}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: O my sons, go and find out about Joseph and his brother and despair not of relief from Allāh. Indeed, no one despairs of relief from Allāh except the disbelieving people."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Go, O my sons, and ascertain concerning Joseph and his brother, and despair not of the Spirit of Allah. Lo! none despaireth of the Spirit of Allah save disbelieving folk.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
يَـٰبَنِىَّ ٱذْهَبُوا۟ فَتَحَسَّسُوا۟ مِن يُوسُفَ وَأَخِيهِ وَلَا تَا۟يْـَٔسُوا۟ مِن رَّوْحِ ٱللَّهِ  إِنَّهُ لَا يَا۟يْـَٔسُ مِن رَّوْحِ ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا ٱلْقَوْمُ ٱلْكَـٰفِرُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:88}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: So when they entered upon him [i.e., Joseph], they said, "O ʿAzeez, adversity has touched us and our family, and we have come with goods poor in quality, but give us full measure and be charitable to us. Indeed, Allāh rewards the charitable."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And when they came (again) before him (Joseph) they said: O ruler! Misfortune hath touched us and our folk, and we bring but poor merchandise, so fill for us the measure and be charitable unto us. Lo! Allah will requite the charitable,

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَلَمَّا دَخَلُوا۟ عَلَيْهِ قَالُوا۟ يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْعَزِيزُ مَسَّنَا وَأَهْلَنَا ٱلضُّرُّ وَجِئْنَا بِبِضَـٰعَةٍ مُّزْجَىٰةٍ فَأَوْفِ لَنَا ٱلْكَيْلَ وَتَصَدَّقْ عَلَيْنَآ  إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَجْزِى ٱلْمُتَصَدِّقِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:89}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: He said, "Do you know what you did with Joseph and his brother when you were ignorant?"

\textit{M. Pickthall}: He said: Know ye what ye did unto Joseph and his brother in your ignorance?

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَ هَلْ عَلِمْتُم مَّا فَعَلْتُم بِيُوسُفَ وَأَخِيهِ إِذْ أَنتُمْ جَـٰهِلُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:90}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: They said, "Are you indeed Joseph?" He said, "I am Joseph, and this is my brother. Allāh has certainly favored us. Indeed, he who fears Allāh and is patient, then indeed, Allāh does not allow to be lost the reward of those who do good."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: They said: Is it indeed thou who art Joseph? He said: I am Joseph and this is my brother. Allah hath shown us favour. Lo! he who wardeth off (evil) and endureth (findeth favour); for lo! Allah loseth not the wages of the kindly.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالُوٓا۟ أَءِنَّكَ لَأَنتَ يُوسُفُ  قَالَ أَنَا يُوسُفُ وَهَـٰذَآ أَخِى  قَدْ مَنَّ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْنَآ  إِنَّهُ مَن يَتَّقِ وَيَصْبِرْ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُضِيعُ أَجْرَ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:91}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: They said, "By Allāh, certainly has Allāh preferred you over us, and indeed, we have been sinners."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: They said: By Allah, verily Allah hath preferred thee above us, and we were indeed sinful.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالُوا۟ تَٱللَّهِ لَقَدْ ءَاثَرَكَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْنَا وَإِن كُنَّا لَخَـٰطِـِٔينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:92}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: He said, "No blame will there be upon you today. May Allāh forgive you; and He is the most merciful of the merciful.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: He said: Have no fear this day! May Allah forgive you, and He is the Most Merciful of those who show mercy.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَ لَا تَثْرِيبَ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْيَوْمَ  يَغْفِرُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمْ  وَهُوَ أَرْحَمُ ٱلرَّٰحِمِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:93}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Take this, my shirt, and cast it over the face of my father; he will become seeing. And bring me your family, all together."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Go with this shirt of mine and lay it on my father's face, he will become (again) a seer; and come to me with all your folk.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
ٱذْهَبُوا۟ بِقَمِيصِى هَـٰذَا فَأَلْقُوهُ عَلَىٰ وَجْهِ أَبِى يَأْتِ بَصِيرًا وَأْتُونِى بِأَهْلِكُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:94}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And when the caravan departed [from Egypt], their father said, "Indeed, I find the smell of Joseph [and would say that he was alive] if you did not think me weakened in mind."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: When the caravan departed their father had said: Truly I am conscious of the breath of Joseph, though ye call me dotard.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَلَمَّا فَصَلَتِ ٱلْعِيرُ قَالَ أَبُوهُمْ إِنِّى لَأَجِدُ رِيحَ يُوسُفَ  لَوْلَآ أَن تُفَنِّدُونِ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:95}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: They said, "By Allāh, indeed you are in your [same] old error."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: (Those around him) said: By Allah, lo! thou art in thine old aberration.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالُوا۟ تَٱللَّهِ إِنَّكَ لَفِى ضَلَـٰلِكَ ٱلْقَدِيمِ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:96}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And when the bearer of good tidings arrived, he cast it over his face, and he returned [once again] seeing. He said, "Did I not tell you that I know from Allāh that which you do not know?"

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Then, when the bearer of glad tidings came, he laid it on his face and he became a seer once more. He said: Said I not unto you that I know from Allah that which ye know not?

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَلَمَّآ أَن جَآءَ ٱلْبَشِيرُ أَلْقَىٰهُ عَلَىٰ وَجْهِهِ فَٱرْتَدَّ بَصِيرًا  قَالَ أَلَمْ أَقُل لَّكُمْ إِنِّىٓ أَعْلَمُ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:97}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: They said, "O our father, ask for us forgiveness of our sins; indeed, we have been sinners."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: They said: O our father! Ask forgiveness of our sins for us, for lo! we were sinful.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالُوا۟ يَـٰٓأَبَانَا ٱسْتَغْفِرْ لَنَا ذُنُوبَنَآ إِنَّا كُنَّا خَـٰطِـِٔينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:98}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: He said, "I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: He said: I shall ask forgiveness for you of my Lord. Lo! He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَ سَوْفَ أَسْتَغْفِرُ لَكُمْ رَبِّىٓ  إِنَّهُ هُوَ ٱلْغَفُورُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:99}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And when they entered upon Joseph, he took his parents to himself [i.e., embraced them] and said, "Enter Egypt, Allāh willing, safe [and secure]."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And when they came in before Joseph, he took his parents unto him, and said: Come into Egypt safe, if Allah will!

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَلَمَّا دَخَلُوا۟ عَلَىٰ يُوسُفَ ءَاوَىٰٓ إِلَيْهِ أَبَوَيْهِ وَقَالَ ٱدْخُلُوا۟ مِصْرَ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ ءَامِنِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:100}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And he raised his parents upon the throne, and they bowed to him in prostration. And he said, "O my father, this is the explanation of my vision of before. My Lord has made it reality. And He was certainly good to me when He took me out of prison and brought you [here] from bedouin life after Satan had induced [estrangement] between me and my brothers. Indeed, my Lord is Subtle in what He wills. Indeed, it is He who is the Knowing, the Wise.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And he placed his parents on the dais and they fell down before him prostrate, and he said: O my father! This is the interpretation of my dream of old. My Lord hath made it true, and He hath shown me kindness, since He took me out of the prison and hath brought you from the desert after Satan had made strife between me and my brethren. Lo! my Lord is tender unto whom He will. He is the Knower, the Wise.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَرَفَعَ أَبَوَيْهِ عَلَى ٱلْعَرْشِ وَخَرُّوا۟ لَهُ سُجَّدًا  وَقَالَ يَـٰٓأَبَتِ هَـٰذَا تَأْوِيلُ رُءْيَـٰىَ مِن قَبْلُ قَدْ جَعَلَهَا رَبِّى حَقًّا  وَقَدْ أَحْسَنَ بِىٓ إِذْ أَخْرَجَنِى مِنَ ٱلسِّجْنِ وَجَآءَ بِكُم مِّنَ ٱلْبَدْوِ مِن بَعْدِ أَن نَّزَغَ ٱلشَّيْطَـٰنُ بَيْنِى وَبَيْنَ إِخْوَتِىٓ  إِنَّ رَبِّى لَطِيفٌ لِّمَا يَشَآءُ  إِنَّهُ هُوَ ٱلْعَلِيمُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:101}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: My Lord, You have given me [something] of sovereignty and taught me of the interpretation of dreams. Creator of the heavens and earth, You are my protector in this world and the Hereafter. Cause me to die a Muslim and join me with the righteous."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: O my Lord! Thou hast given me (something) of sovereignty and hast taught me (something) of the interpretation of events - Creator of the heavens and the earth! Thou art my Protecting Guardian in the world and the Hereafter. Make me to die muslim (unto Thee), and join me to the righteous.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
۞ رَبِّ قَدْ ءَاتَيْتَنِى مِنَ ٱلْمُلْكِ وَعَلَّمْتَنِى مِن تَأْوِيلِ ٱلْأَحَادِيثِ  فَاطِرَ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ أَنتَ وَلِىِّ فِى ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ  تَوَفَّنِى مُسْلِمًا وَأَلْحِقْنِى بِٱلصَّـٰلِحِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:102}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: That is from the news of the unseen which We reveal, [O Muḥammad], to you. And you were not with them when they put together their plan while they conspired.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: This is of the tidings of the Unseen which We inspire in thee (Muhammad). Thou wast not present with them when they fixed their plan and they were scheming.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
ذَٰلِكَ مِنْ أَنبَآءِ ٱلْغَيْبِ نُوحِيهِ إِلَيْكَ  وَمَا كُنتَ لَدَيْهِمْ إِذْ أَجْمَعُوٓا۟ أَمْرَهُمْ وَهُمْ يَمْكُرُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:103}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And most of the people, although you strive [for it], are not believers.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And though thou try much, most men will not believe.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَمَآ أَكْثَرُ ٱلنَّاسِ وَلَوْ حَرَصْتَ بِمُؤْمِنِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:104}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And you do not ask of them for it any payment. It is not except a reminder to the worlds.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Thou askest them no fee for it. It is naught else than a reminder unto the peoples.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَمَا تَسْـَٔلُهُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ  إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا ذِكْرٌ لِّلْعَـٰلَمِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:105}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And how many a sign within the heavens and earth do they pass over while they, therefrom, are turning away.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: How many a portent is there in the heavens and the earth which they pass by with face averted!

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَكَأَيِّن مِّنْ ءَايَةٍ فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ يَمُرُّونَ عَلَيْهَا وَهُمْ عَنْهَا مُعْرِضُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:106}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And most of them believe not in Allāh except while they associate others with Him.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And most of them believe not in Allah except that they attribute partners (unto Him).

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَمَا يُؤْمِنُ أَكْثَرُهُم بِٱللَّهِ إِلَّا وَهُم مُّشْرِكُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:107}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Then do they feel secure that there will not come to them an overwhelming [aspect] of the punishment of Allāh or that the Hour will not come upon them suddenly while they do not perceive?

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Deem they themselves secure from the coming on them of a pall of Allah's punishment, or the coming of the Hour suddenly while they are unaware?

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
أَفَأَمِنُوٓا۟ أَن تَأْتِيَهُمْ غَـٰشِيَةٌ مِّنْ عَذَابِ ٱللَّهِ أَوْ تَأْتِيَهُمُ ٱلسَّاعَةُ بَغْتَةً وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:108}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Say, "This is my way; I invite to Allāh with insight, I and those who follow me. And exalted is Allāh; and I am not of those who associate others with Him."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Say: This is my Way: I call on Allah with sure knowledge. I and whosoever followeth me - Glory be to Allah! - and I am not of the idolaters.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قُلْ هَـٰذِهِ سَبِيلِىٓ أَدْعُوٓا۟ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ  عَلَىٰ بَصِيرَةٍ أَنَا وَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَنِى  وَسُبْحَـٰنَ ٱللَّهِ وَمَآ أَنَا مِنَ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:109}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And We sent not before you [as messengers] except men to whom We revealed from among the people of cities. So have they not traveled through the earth and observed how was the end of those before them? And the home of the Hereafter is best for those who fear Allāh; then will you not reason?

\textit{M. Pickthall}: We sent not before thee (any messengers) save men whom We inspired from among the folk of the townships - Have they not travelled in the land and seen the nature of the consequence for those who were before them? And verily the abode of the Hereafter, for those who ward off (evil), is best. Have ye then no sense? -

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ إِلَّا رِجَالًا نُّوحِىٓ إِلَيْهِم مِّنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْقُرَىٰٓ  أَفَلَمْ يَسِيرُوا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ فَيَنظُرُوا۟ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَـٰقِبَةُ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ  وَلَدَارُ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ خَيْرٌ لِّلَّذِينَ ٱتَّقَوْا۟  أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:110}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: [They continued] until, when the messengers despaired and were certain that they had been denied, there came to them Our victory, and whoever We willed was saved. And Our punishment cannot be repelled from the people who are criminals.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Till, when the messengers despaired and thought that they were denied, then came unto them Our help, and whom We would was saved. And Our wrath cannot be warded from the guilty.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا ٱسْتَيْـَٔسَ ٱلرُّسُلُ وَظَنُّوٓا۟ أَنَّهُمْ قَدْ كُذِبُوا۟ جَآءَهُمْ نَصْرُنَا فَنُجِّىَ مَن نَّشَآءُ  وَلَا يُرَدُّ بَأْسُنَا عَنِ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{12:111}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: There was certainly in their stories a lesson for those of understanding. Never was it [i.e., the Qur’ān] a narration invented, but a confirmation of what was before it and a detailed explanation of all things and guidance and mercy for a people who believe.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: In their history verily there is a lesson for men of understanding. It is no invented story but a confirmation of the existing (Scripture) and a detailed explanation of everything, and a guidance and a mercy for folk who believe.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
لَقَدْ كَانَ فِى قَصَصِهِمْ عِبْرَةٌ لِّأُو۟لِى ٱلْأَلْبَـٰبِ  مَا كَانَ حَدِيثًا يُفْتَرَىٰ وَلَـٰكِن تَصْدِيقَ ٱلَّذِى بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَتَفْصِيلَ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ وَهُدًى وَرَحْمَةً لِّقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}

\chapter{Session 3}
\section{Surah 3, Āli `Imrān (Family of Imran)
Verses 69 -- 83}

The 89th revealed Surah. Revealed in Madinah


\noindent[\textbf{3:69}]
