\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And they will not remember except that Allāh wills. He is worthy of fear and adequate for [granting] forgiveness.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And they will not heed unless Allah willeth (it). He is the fount of fear. He is the fount of Mercy.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَمَا يَذْكُرُونَ إِلَّآ أَن يَشَآءَ ٱللَّهُ  هُوَ أَهْلُ ٱلتَّقْوَىٰ وَأَهْلُ ٱلْمَغْفِرَةِ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}

\section{Surah 41, Fuşşilat (Explained in Detail)
All Verses (1 -- 54)}

The 61st revealed Surah. Revealed in Makkah


\noindent[\textbf{41:1}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Ḥā, Meem.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Ha. Mim.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
 حمٓ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:2}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: [This is] a revelation from the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful -

\textit{M. Pickthall}: A revelation from the Beneficent, the Merciful,

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
تَنزِيلٌ مِّنَ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:3}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: A Book whose verses have been detailed, an Arabic Qur’ān for a people who know,

\textit{M. Pickthall}: A Scripture whereof the verses are expounded, a Lecture in Arabic for people who have knowledge,

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
كِتَـٰبٌ فُصِّلَتْ ءَايَـٰتُهُ قُرْءَانًا عَرَبِيًّا لِّقَوْمٍ يَعْلَمُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:4}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: As a giver of good tidings and a warner; but most of them turn away, so they do not hear.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Good tidings and a warning. But most of them turn away so that they hear not.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
بَشِيرًا وَنَذِيرًا فَأَعْرَضَ أَكْثَرُهُمْ فَهُمْ لَا يَسْمَعُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:5}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And they say, "Our hearts are within coverings [i.e., screened] from that to which you invite us, and in our ears is deafness, and between us and you is a partition, so work; indeed, we are working."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And they say: Our hearts are protected from that unto which thou (O Muhammad) callest us, and in our ears there is a deafness, and between us and thee there is a veil. Act, then. Lo! we also shall be acting.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَقَالُوا۟ قُلُوبُنَا فِىٓ أَكِنَّةٍ مِّمَّا تَدْعُونَآ إِلَيْهِ وَفِىٓ ءَاذَانِنَا وَقْرٌ وَمِن بَيْنِنَا وَبَيْنِكَ حِجَابٌ فَٱعْمَلْ إِنَّنَا عَـٰمِلُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:6}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Say, [O Muḥammad], "I am only a man like you to whom it has been revealed that your god is but one God; so take a straight course to Him and seek His forgiveness." And woe to those who associate others with Allāh –

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Say (unto them O Muhammad): I am only a mortal like you. It is inspired in me that your Allah is One Allah, therefor take the straight path unto Him and seek forgiveness of Him. And woe unto the idolaters,

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قُلْ إِنَّمَآ أَنَا بَشَرٌ مِّثْلُكُمْ يُوحَىٰٓ إِلَىَّ أَنَّمَآ إِلَـٰهُكُمْ إِلَـٰهٌ وَٰحِدٌ فَٱسْتَقِيمُوٓا۟ إِلَيْهِ وَٱسْتَغْفِرُوهُ  وَوَيْلٌ لِّلْمُشْرِكِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:7}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Those who do not give zakāh, and in the Hereafter they are disbelievers.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Who give not the poor-due, and who are disbelievers in the Hereafter.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْتُونَ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَهُم بِٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ هُمْ كَـٰفِرُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:8}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds - for them is a reward uninterrupted.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Lo! as for those who believe and do good works, for them is a reward enduring.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتِ لَهُمْ أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:9}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Say, "Do you indeed disbelieve in He who created the earth in two days and attribute to Him equals? That is the Lord of the worlds."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Say (O Muhammad, unto the idolaters): Disbelieve ye verily in Him Who created the earth in two Days, and ascribe ye unto Him rivals? He (and none else) is the Lord of the Worlds.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
۞ قُلْ أَئِنَّكُمْ لَتَكْفُرُونَ بِٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ ٱلْأَرْضَ فِى يَوْمَيْنِ وَتَجْعَلُونَ لَهُٓ أَندَادًا  ذَٰلِكَ رَبُّ ٱلْعَـٰلَمِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:10}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And He placed on it [i.e., the earth] firmly set mountains over its surface, and He blessed it and determined therein its [creatures'] sustenance in four days without distinction - for [the information of] those who ask.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: He placed therein firm hills rising above it, and blessed it and measured therein its sustenance in four Days, alike for (all) who ask;

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَجَعَلَ فِيهَا رَوَٰسِىَ مِن فَوْقِهَا وَبَـٰرَكَ فِيهَا وَقَدَّرَ فِيهَآ أَقْوَٰتَهَا فِىٓ أَرْبَعَةِ أَيَّامٍ سَوَآءً لِّلسَّآئِلِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:11}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Then He directed Himself to the heaven while it was smoke and said to it and to the earth, "Come [into being], willingly or by compulsion." They said, "We have come willingly."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Then turned He to the heaven when it was smoke, and said unto it and unto the earth: Come both of you, willingly or loth. They said: We come, obedient.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
ثُمَّ ٱسْتَوَىٰٓ إِلَى ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَهِىَ دُخَانٌ فَقَالَ لَهَا وَلِلْأَرْضِ ٱئْتِيَا طَوْعًا أَوْ كَرْهًا قَالَتَآ أَتَيْنَا طَآئِعِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:12}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And He completed them as seven heavens within two days and inspired [i.e., made known] in each heaven its command. And We adorned the nearest heaven with lamps [i.e., stars, for beauty] and as protection. That is the determination of the Exalted in Might, the Knowing.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Then He ordained them seven heavens in two Days and inspired in each heaven its mandate; and We decked the nether heaven with lamps, and rendered it inviolable. That is the measuring of the Mighty, the Knower.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَقَضَىٰهُنَّ سَبْعَ سَمَـٰوَاتٍ فِى يَوْمَيْنِ وَأَوْحَىٰ فِى كُلِّ سَمَآءٍ أَمْرَهَا  وَزَيَّنَّا ٱلسَّمَآءَ ٱلدُّنْيَا بِمَصَـٰبِيحَ وَحِفْظًا  ذَٰلِكَ تَقْدِيرُ ٱلْعَزِيزِ ٱلْعَلِيمِ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:13}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: But if they turn away, then say, "I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt [that struck] ʿAad and Thamūd.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: But if they turn away, then say: I warn you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt (which fell of old upon the tribes) of A'ad and Thamud;

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَإِنْ أَعْرَضُوا۟ فَقُلْ أَنذَرْتُكُمْ صَـٰعِقَةً مِّثْلَ صَـٰعِقَةِ عَادٍ وَثَمُودَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:14}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: [That occurred] when the messengers had come to them before them and after them, [saying], "Worship not except Allāh." They said, "If our Lord had willed, He would have sent down the angels, so indeed we, in that with which you have been sent, are disbelievers."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: When their messengers came unto them from before them and behind them, saying: Worship none but Allah! they said: If our Lord had willed, He surely would have sent down angels (unto us), so lo! we are disbelievers in that wherewith ye have been sent.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
إِذْ جَآءَتْهُمُ ٱلرُّسُلُ مِن بَيْنِ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوٓا۟ إِلَّا ٱللَّهَ  قَالُوا۟ لَوْ شَآءَ رَبُّنَا لَأَنزَلَ مَلَـٰٓئِكَةً فَإِنَّا بِمَآ أُرْسِلْتُم بِهِ كَـٰفِرُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:15}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: As for ʿAad, they were arrogant upon the earth without right and said, "Who is greater than us in strength?" Did they not consider that Allāh who created them was greater than them in strength? But they were rejecting Our signs.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: As for A'ad, they were arrogant in the land without right, and they said: Who is mightier than us in power? Could they not see that Allah Who created them, He was mightier than them in power? And they denied Our revelations.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَأَمَّا عَادٌ فَٱسْتَكْبَرُوا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ بِغَيْرِ ٱلْحَقِّ وَقَالُوا۟ مَنْ أَشَدُّ مِنَّا قُوَّةً  أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا۟ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَهُمْ هُوَ أَشَدُّ مِنْهُمْ قُوَّةً  وَكَانُوا۟ بِـَٔايَـٰتِنَا يَجْحَدُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:16}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: So We sent upon them a screaming wind during days of misfortune to make them taste the punishment of disgrace in the worldly life; but the punishment of the Hereafter is more disgracing, and they will not be helped.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Therefor We let loose on them a raging wind in evil days, that We might make them taste the torment of disgrace in the life of the world. And verily the doom of the Hereafter will be more shameful, and they will not be helped.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَأَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ رِيحًا صَرْصَرًا فِىٓ أَيَّامٍ نَّحِسَاتٍ لِّنُذِيقَهُمْ عَذَابَ ٱلْخِزْىِ فِى ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا  وَلَعَذَابُ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ أَخْزَىٰ  وَهُمْ لَا يُنصَرُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:17}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And as for Thamūd, We guided them, but they preferred blindness over guidance, so the thunderbolt of humiliating punishment seized them for what they used to earn.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And as for Thamud, We gave them guidance, but they preferred blindness to the guidance, so the bolt of the doom of humiliation overtook them because of what they used to earn.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَأَمَّا ثَمُودُ فَهَدَيْنَـٰهُمْ فَٱسْتَحَبُّوا۟ ٱلْعَمَىٰ عَلَى ٱلْهُدَىٰ فَأَخَذَتْهُمْ صَـٰعِقَةُ ٱلْعَذَابِ ٱلْهُونِ بِمَا كَانُوا۟ يَكْسِبُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:18}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And We saved those who believed and used to fear Allāh.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And We delivered those who believed and used to keep their duty to Allah.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَنَجَّيْنَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَكَانُوا۟ يَتَّقُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:19}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And [mention, O Muḥammad], the Day when the enemies of Allāh will be gathered to the Fire while they are [driven], assembled in rows,

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And (make mention of) the day when the enemies of Allah are gathered unto the Fire, they are driven on

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَيَوْمَ يُحْشَرُ أَعْدَآءُ ٱللَّهِ إِلَى ٱلنَّارِ فَهُمْ يُوزَعُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:20}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Until, when they reach it, their hearing and their eyes and their skins will testify against them of what they used to do.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Till, when they reach it, their ears and their eyes and their skins testify against them as to what they used to do.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا مَا جَآءُوهَا شَهِدَ عَلَيْهِمْ سَمْعُهُمْ وَأَبْصَـٰرُهُمْ وَجُلُودُهُم بِمَا كَانُوا۟ يَعْمَلُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:21}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And they will say to their skins, "Why have you testified against us?" They will say, "We were made to speak by Allāh, who has made everything speak; and He created you the first time, and to Him you are returned.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And they say unto their skins: Why testify ye against us? They say: Allah hath given us speech Who giveth speech to all things, and Who created you at the first, and unto Whom ye are returned.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَقَالُوا۟ لِجُلُودِهِمْ لِمَ شَهِدتُّمْ عَلَيْنَا  قَالُوٓا۟ أَنطَقَنَا ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَنطَقَ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ وَهُوَ خَلَقَكُمْ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ وَإِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:22}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And you were not covering [i.e., protecting] yourselves, lest your hearing testify against you or your sight or your skins, but you assumed that Allāh does not know much of what you do.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Ye did not hide yourselves lest your ears and your eyes and your skins should testify against you, but ye deemed that Allah knew not much of what ye did.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَمَا كُنتُمْ تَسْتَتِرُونَ أَن يَشْهَدَ عَلَيْكُمْ سَمْعُكُمْ وَلَآ أَبْصَـٰرُكُمْ وَلَا جُلُودُكُمْ وَلَـٰكِن ظَنَنتُمْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَعْلَمُ كَثِيرًا مِّمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:23}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And that was your assumption which you assumed about your Lord. It has brought you to ruin, and you have become among the losers."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: That, your thought which ye did think about your Lord, hath ruined you; and ye find yourselves (this day) among the lost.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَذَٰلِكُمْ ظَنُّكُمُ ٱلَّذِى ظَنَنتُم بِرَبِّكُمْ أَرْدَىٰكُمْ فَأَصْبَحْتُم مِّنَ ٱلْخَـٰسِرِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:24}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: So [even] if they are patient, the Fire is a residence for them; and if they ask to appease [Allāh], they will not be of those who are allowed to appease.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And though they are resigned, yet the Fire is still their home; and if they ask for favour, yet they are not of those unto whom favour can be shown.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَإِن يَصْبِرُوا۟ فَٱلنَّارُ مَثْوًى لَّهُمْ  وَإِن يَسْتَعْتِبُوا۟ فَمَا هُم مِّنَ ٱلْمُعْتَبِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:25}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And We appointed for them companions who made attractive to them what was before them and what was behind them [of sin], and the word [i.e., decree] has come into effect upon them among nations which had passed on before them of jinn and men. Indeed, they [all] were losers.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And We assigned them comrades (in the world), who made their present and their past fairseeming unto them. And the Word concerning nations of the jinn and humankind who passed away before them hath effect for them. Lo! they were ever losers.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
۞ وَقَيَّضْنَا لَهُمْ قُرَنَآءَ فَزَيَّنُوا۟ لَهُم مَّا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ وَحَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْقَوْلُ فِىٓ أُمَمٍ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِن قَبْلِهِم مِّنَ ٱلْجِنِّ وَٱلْإِنسِ  إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ خَـٰسِرِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:26}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And those who disbelieve say, "Do not listen to this Qur’ān and speak noisily during [the recitation of] it that perhaps you will overcome."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Those who disbelieve say: Heed not this Qur'an, and drown the hearing of it; haply ye may conquer.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ لَا تَسْمَعُوا۟ لِهَـٰذَا ٱلْقُرْءَانِ وَٱلْغَوْا۟ فِيهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَغْلِبُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:27}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: But We will surely cause those who disbelieve to taste a severe punishment, and We will surely recompense them for the worst of what they had been doing.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: But verily We shall cause those who disbelieve to taste an awful doom, and verily We shall requite them the worst of what they used to do.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَلَنُذِيقَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ عَذَابًا شَدِيدًا وَلَنَجْزِيَنَّهُمْ أَسْوَأَ ٱلَّذِى كَانُوا۟ يَعْمَلُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:28}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: That is the recompense of the enemies of Allāh - the Fire. For them therein is the home of eternity as recompense for what they, of Our verses, were rejecting.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: That is the reward of Allah's enemies: the Fire. Therein is their immortal home, payment forasmuch as they denied Our revelations.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
ذَٰلِكَ جَزَآءُ أَعْدَآءِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّارُ  لَهُمْ فِيهَا دَارُ ٱلْخُلْدِ  جَزَآءً بِمَا كَانُوا۟ بِـَٔايَـٰتِنَا يَجْحَدُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:29}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And those who disbelieved will [then] say, "Our Lord, show us those who misled us of the jinn and men [so] we may put them under our feet that they will be among the lowest."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And those who disbelieve will say: Our Lord! Show us those who beguiled us of the jinn and humankind. We will place them underneath our feet that they may be among the nethermost.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ رَبَّنَآ أَرِنَا ٱلَّذَيْنِ أَضَلَّانَا مِنَ ٱلْجِنِّ وَٱلْإِنسِ نَجْعَلْهُمَا تَحْتَ أَقْدَامِنَا لِيَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلْأَسْفَلِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:30}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Indeed, those who have said, "Our Lord is Allāh" and then remained on a right course - the angels will descend upon them, [saying], "Do not fear and do not grieve but receive good tidings of Paradise, which you were promised.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Lo! those who say: Our Lord is Allah, and afterward are upright, the angels descend upon them, saying: Fear not nor grieve, but hear good tidings of the paradise which ye are promised.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُوا۟ رَبُّنَا ٱللَّهُ ثُمَّ ٱسْتَقَـٰمُوا۟ تَتَنَزَّلُ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْمَلَـٰٓئِكَةُ أَلَّا تَخَافُوا۟ وَلَا تَحْزَنُوا۟ وَأَبْشِرُوا۟ بِٱلْجَنَّةِ ٱلَّتِى كُنتُمْ تُوعَدُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:31}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: We [angels] were your allies in worldly life and [are so] in the Hereafter. And you will have therein whatever your souls desire, and you will have therein whatever you request [or wish]

\textit{M. Pickthall}: We are your protecting friends in the life of the world and in the Hereafter. There ye will have (all) that your souls desire, and there ye will have (all) for which ye pray.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
نَحْنُ أَوْلِيَآؤُكُمْ فِى ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَفِى ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ  وَلَكُمْ فِيهَا مَا تَشْتَهِىٓ أَنفُسُكُمْ وَلَكُمْ فِيهَا مَا تَدَّعُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:32}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: As accommodation from a [Lord who is] Forgiving and Merciful."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: A gift of welcome from One Forgiving, Merciful.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
نُزُلًا مِّنْ غَفُورٍ رَّحِيمٍ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:33}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And who is better in speech than one who invites to Allāh and does righteousness and says, "Indeed, I am of the Muslims."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And who is better in speech than him who prayeth unto his Lord and doeth right, and saith: Lo! I am of those who are muslims (surrender unto Him).

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَمَنْ أَحْسَنُ قَوْلًا مِّمَّن دَعَآ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَعَمِلَ صَـٰلِحًا وَقَالَ إِنَّنِى مِنَ ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:34}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And not equal are the good deed and the bad. Repel [evil] by that [deed] which is better; and thereupon, the one whom between you and him is enmity [will become] as though he was a devoted friend.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: The good deed and the evil deed are not alike. Repel the evil deed with one which is better, then lo! he, between whom and thee there was enmity (will become) as though he was a bosom friend.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَلَا تَسْتَوِى ٱلْحَسَنَةُ وَلَا ٱلسَّيِّئَةُ  ٱدْفَعْ بِٱلَّتِى هِىَ أَحْسَنُ فَإِذَا ٱلَّذِى بَيْنَكَ وَبَيْنَهُ عَدَٰوَةٌ كَأَنَّهُ وَلِىٌّ حَمِيمٌ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:35}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: But none is granted it except those who are patient, and none is granted it except one having a great portion [of good].

\textit{M. Pickthall}: But none is granted it save those who are steadfast, and none is granted it save the owner of great happiness.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَمَا يُلَقَّىٰهَآ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا۟ وَمَا يُلَقَّىٰهَآ إِلَّا ذُو حَظٍّ عَظِيمٍ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:36}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And if there comes to you from Satan an evil suggestion, then seek refuge in Allāh. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And if a whisper from the devil reach thee (O Muhammad) then seek refuge in Allah. Lo! He is the Hearer, the Knower.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَإِمَّا يَنزَغَنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلشَّيْطَـٰنِ نَزْغٌ فَٱسْتَعِذْ بِٱللَّهِ  إِنَّهُ هُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:37}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And of His signs are the night and day and the sun and moon. Do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon, but prostrate to Allāh, who created them, if it should be Him that you worship.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And of His portents are the night and the day and the sun and the moon. Do not prostrate to the sun or the moon; but prostrate to Allah Who created them, if it is in truth Him Whom ye worship.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَمِنْ ءَايَـٰتِهِ ٱلَّيْلُ وَٱلنَّهَارُ وَٱلشَّمْسُ وَٱلْقَمَرُ  لَا تَسْجُدُوا۟ لِلشَّمْسِ وَلَا لِلْقَمَرِ وَٱسْجُدُوا۟ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَهُنَّ إِن كُنتُمْ إِيَّاهُ تَعْبُدُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:38}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: But if they are arrogant - then those who are near your Lord [i.e., the angels] exalt Him by night and by day, and they do not become weary.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: But if they are too proud - still those who are with thy Lord glorify Him night and day, and tire not.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَإِنِ ٱسْتَكْبَرُوا۟ فَٱلَّذِينَ عِندَ رَبِّكَ يُسَبِّحُونَ لَهُ بِٱلَّيْلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِ وَهُمْ لَا يَسْـَٔمُونَ ۩
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:39}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And of His signs is that you see the earth stilled, but when We send down upon it rain, it quivers and grows. Indeed, He who has given it life is the Giver of Life to the dead. Indeed, He is over all things competent.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And of His portents (is this): that thou seest the earth lowly, but when We send down water thereon it thrilleth and groweth. Lo! He Who quickeneth it is verily the Quickener of the Dead. Lo! He is Able to do all things.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَمِنْ ءَايَـٰتِهِٓ أَنَّكَ تَرَى ٱلْأَرْضَ خَـٰشِعَةً فَإِذَآ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْهَا ٱلْمَآءَ ٱهْتَزَّتْ وَرَبَتْ  إِنَّ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَحْيَاهَا لَمُحْىِ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰٓ  إِنَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:40}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Indeed, those who inject deviation into Our verses are not concealed from Us. So, is he who is cast into the Fire better or he who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection? Do whatever you will; indeed, He is Seeing of what you do.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Lo! those who distort Our revelations are not hid from Us. Is he who is hurled into the Fire better, or he who cometh secure on the Day of Resurrection? Do what ye will. Lo! He is Seer of what ye do.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يُلْحِدُونَ فِىٓ ءَايَـٰتِنَا لَا يَخْفَوْنَ عَلَيْنَآ  أَفَمَن يُلْقَىٰ فِى ٱلنَّارِ خَيْرٌ أَم مَّن يَأْتِىٓ ءَامِنًا يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَـٰمَةِ  ٱعْمَلُوا۟ مَا شِئْتُمْ  إِنَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:41}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Indeed, those who disbelieve in the message [i.e., the Qur’ān] after it has come to them... And indeed, it is a mighty Book.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Lo! those who disbelieve in the Reminder when it cometh unto them (are guilty), for lo! it is an unassailable Scripture.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ بِٱلذِّكْرِ لَمَّا جَآءَهُمْ  وَإِنَّهُ لَكِتَـٰبٌ عَزِيزٌ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:42}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or from behind it; [it is] a revelation from a [Lord who is] Wise and Praiseworthy.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Falsehood cannot come at it from before it or from behind it. (It is) a revelation from the Wise, the Owner of Praise.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
لَّا يَأْتِيهِ ٱلْبَـٰطِلُ مِن بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَلَا مِنْ خَلْفِهِ  تَنزِيلٌ مِّنْ حَكِيمٍ حَمِيدٍ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:43}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Nothing is said to you, [O Muḥammad], except what was already said to the messengers before you. Indeed, your Lord is a possessor of forgiveness and a possessor of painful penalty.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Naught is said unto thee (Muhammad) save what was said unto the messengers before thee. Lo! thy Lord is owner of forgiveness, and owner (also) of dire punishment.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
مَّا يُقَالُ لَكَ إِلَّا مَا قَدْ قِيلَ لِلرُّسُلِ مِن قَبْلِكَ  إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَذُو مَغْفِرَةٍ وَذُو عِقَابٍ أَلِيمٍ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:44}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And if We had made it a foreign [i.e., non-Arabic] Qur’ān, they would have said, "Why are its verses not explained in detail [in our language]? Is it a foreign [recitation] and an Arab [messenger]?" Say, "It is, for those who believe, a guidance and cure." And those who do not believe - in their ears is deafness, and it is upon them blindness. Those are being called from a distant place.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And if We had appointed it a Lecture in a foreign tongue they would assuredly have said: If only its verses were expounded (so that we might understand)? What! A foreign tongue and an Arab? - Say unto them (O Muhammad): For those who believe it is a guidance and a healing; and as for those who disbelieve, there is a deafness in their ears, and it is blindness for them. Such are called to from afar.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَلَوْ جَعَلْنَـٰهُ قُرْءَانًا أَعْجَمِيًّا لَّقَالُوا۟ لَوْلَا فُصِّلَتْ ءَايَـٰتُهُٓ  ءَا۬عْجَمِىٌّ وَعَرَبِىٌّ  قُلْ هُوَ لِلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ هُدًى وَشِفَآءٌ  وَٱلَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ فِىٓ ءَاذَانِهِمْ وَقْرٌ وَهُوَ عَلَيْهِمْ عَمًى  أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ يُنَادَوْنَ مِن مَّكَانٍۭ بَعِيدٍ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:45}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And We had already given Moses the Scripture, but it came under disagreement. And if not for a word [i.e., decree] that preceded from your Lord, it would have been concluded between them. And indeed they are, concerning it [i.e., the Qur’ān], in disquieting doubt.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And We verily gave Moses the Scripture, but there hath been dispute concerning it; and but for a Word that had already gone forth from thy Lord, it would ere now have been judged between them; but lo! they are in hopeless doubt concerning it.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَلَقَدْ ءَاتَيْنَا مُوسَى ٱلْكِتَـٰبَ فَٱخْتُلِفَ فِيهِ  وَلَوْلَا كَلِمَةٌ سَبَقَتْ مِن رَّبِّكَ لَقُضِىَ بَيْنَهُمْ  وَإِنَّهُمْ لَفِى شَكٍّ مِّنْهُ مُرِيبٍ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:46}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Whoever does righteousness - it is for his [own] soul; and whoever does evil [does so] against it. And your Lord is not ever unjust to [His] servants.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Whoso doeth right it is for his soul, and whoso doeth wrong it is against it. And thy Lord is not at all a tyrant to His slaves.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
مَّنْ عَمِلَ صَـٰلِحًا فَلِنَفْسِهِ  وَمَنْ أَسَآءَ فَعَلَيْهَا  وَمَا رَبُّكَ بِظَلَّـٰمٍ لِّلْعَبِيدِ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:47}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: To Him [alone] is attributed knowledge of the Hour. And fruits emerge not from their coverings nor does a female conceive or give birth except with His knowledge. And the Day He will call to them, "Where are My 'partners'?" they will say, "We announce to You that there is [no longer] among us any witness [to that]."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Unto Him is referred (all) knowledge of the Hour. And no fruits burst forth from their sheaths, and no female carrieth or bringeth forth but with His knowledge. And on the day when He calleth unto them: Where are now My partners? they will say: We confess unto Thee, not one of us is a witness (for them).

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
۞ إِلَيْهِ يُرَدُّ عِلْمُ ٱلسَّاعَةِ  وَمَا تَخْرُجُ مِن ثَمَرَٰتٍ مِّنْ أَكْمَامِهَا وَمَا تَحْمِلُ مِنْ أُنثَىٰ وَلَا تَضَعُ إِلَّا بِعِلْمِهِ  وَيَوْمَ يُنَادِيهِمْ أَيْنَ شُرَكَآءِى قَالُوٓا۟ ءَاذَنَّـٰكَ مَا مِنَّا مِن شَهِيدٍ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:48}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And lost from them will be those they were invoking before, and they will be certain that they have no place of escape.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And those to whom they used to cry of old have failed them, and they perceive they have no place of refuge.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَضَلَّ عَنْهُم مَّا كَانُوا۟ يَدْعُونَ مِن قَبْلُ  وَظَنُّوا۟ مَا لَهُم مِّن مَّحِيصٍ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:49}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Man is not weary of supplication for good [things], but if evil touches him, he is hopeless and despairing.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Man tireth not of praying for good, and if ill toucheth him, then he is disheartened, desperate.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
لَّا يَسْـَٔمُ ٱلْإِنسَـٰنُ مِن دُعَآءِ ٱلْخَيْرِ وَإِن مَّسَّهُ ٱلشَّرُّ فَيَـُٔوسٌ قَنُوطٌ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:50}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And if We let him taste mercy from Us after an adversity which has touched him, he will surely say, "This is [due] to me, and I do not think the Hour will occur; and [even] if I should be returned to my Lord, indeed, for me there will be with Him the best." But We will surely inform those who disbelieved about what they did, and We will surely make them taste a massive punishment.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And verily, if We cause him to taste mercy after some hurt that hath touched him, he will say: This is my own; and I deem not that the Hour will ever rise, and if I am brought back to my Lord, I surely shall be better off with Him - But We verily shall tell those who disbelieve (all) that they did, and We verily shall make them taste hard punishment.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَلَئِنْ أَذَقْنَـٰهُ رَحْمَةً مِّنَّا مِن بَعْدِ ضَرَّآءَ مَسَّتْهُ لَيَقُولَنَّ هَـٰذَا لِى وَمَآ أَظُنُّ ٱلسَّاعَةَ قَآئِمَةً وَلَئِن رُّجِعْتُ إِلَىٰ رَبِّىٓ إِنَّ لِى عِندَهُ لَلْحُسْنَىٰ  فَلَنُنَبِّئَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ بِمَا عَمِلُوا۟ وَلَنُذِيقَنَّهُم مِّنْ عَذَابٍ غَلِيظٍ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:51}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And when We bestow favor upon man, he turns away and distances himself; but when evil touches him, then he is full of extensive supplication.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: When We show favour unto man, he withdraweth and turneth aside, but when ill toucheth him then he aboundeth in prayer.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَإِذَآ أَنْعَمْنَا عَلَى ٱلْإِنسَـٰنِ أَعْرَضَ وَنَـَٔا بِجَانِبِهِ وَإِذَا مَسَّهُ ٱلشَّرُّ فَذُو دُعَآءٍ عَرِيضٍ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:52}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Say, "Have you considered: if it [i.e., the Qur’ān] is from Allāh and you disbelieved in it, who would be more astray than one who is in extreme dissension?"

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Bethink you: If it is from Allah and ye reject it - Who is further astray than one who is at open feud (with Allah)?

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قُلْ أَرَءَيْتُمْ إِن كَانَ مِنْ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ ثُمَّ كَفَرْتُم بِهِ مَنْ أَضَلُّ مِمَّنْ هُوَ فِى شِقَاقٍۭ بَعِيدٍ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:53}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth. But is it not sufficient concerning your Lord that He is, over all things, a Witness?

\textit{M. Pickthall}: We shall show them Our portents on the horizons and within themselves until it will be manifest unto them that it is the Truth. Doth not thy Lord suffice, since He is Witness over all things?

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
سَنُرِيهِمْ ءَايَـٰتِنَا فِى ٱلْـَٔافَاقِ وَفِىٓ أَنفُسِهِمْ حَتَّىٰ يَتَبَيَّنَ لَهُمْ أَنَّهُ ٱلْحَقُّ  أَوَلَمْ يَكْفِ بِرَبِّكَ أَنَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ شَهِيدٌ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{41:54}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Unquestionably, they are in doubt about the meeting with their Lord. Unquestionably He is, of all things, encompassing.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: How! Are they still in doubt about the meeting with their Lord? Lo! Is not He surrounding all things?

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
أَلَآ إِنَّهُمْ فِى مِرْيَةٍ مِّن لِّقَآءِ رَبِّهِمْ  أَلَآ إِنَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَىْءٍ مُّحِيطٌ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}

\section{Surah 68, Al-Qalam (The Pen)
Verses 1 -- 32}

The 2nd revealed Surah. Revealed in Makkah


\noindent[\textbf{68:1}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Nūn. By the pen and what they inscribe,

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Nun. By the pen and that which they write (therewith),

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
 نٓ  وَٱلْقَلَمِ وَمَا يَسْطُرُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{68:2}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: You are not, [O Muḥammad], by the favor of your Lord, a madman.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Thou art not, for thy Lord's favour unto thee, a madman.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
مَآ أَنتَ بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ بِمَجْنُونٍ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{68:3}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And indeed, for you is a reward uninterrupted.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And lo! thine verily will be a reward unfailing.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَإِنَّ لَكَ لَأَجْرًا غَيْرَ مَمْنُونٍ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{68:4}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And indeed, you are of a great moral character.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And lo! thou art of a tremendous nature.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَإِنَّكَ لَعَلَىٰ خُلُقٍ عَظِيمٍ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{68:5}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: So you will see and they will see

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And thou wilt see and they will see

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَسَتُبْصِرُ وَيُبْصِرُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{68:6}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Which of you is the afflicted [by a devil].

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Which of you is the demented.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
بِأَييِّكُمُ ٱلْمَفْتُونُ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{68:7}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has gone astray from His way, and He is most knowing of the [rightly] guided.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Lo! thy Lord is Best Aware of him who strayeth from His way, and He is Best Aware of those who walk aright.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَن ضَلَّ عَن سَبِيلِهِ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِٱلْمُهْتَدِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{68:8}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Then do not obey the deniers.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Therefor obey not thou the rejecters

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَلَا تُطِعِ ٱلْمُكَذِّبِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{68:9}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: They wish that you would soften [in your position], so they would soften [toward you].

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Who would have had thee compromise, that they may compromise.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَدُّوا۟ لَوْ تُدْهِنُ فَيُدْهِنُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{68:10}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And do not obey every worthless habitual swearer

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Neither obey thou each feeble oath-monger,

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَلَا تُطِعْ كُلَّ حَلَّافٍ مَّهِينٍ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{68:11}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: [And] scorner, going about with malicious gossip -

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Detracter, spreader abroad of slanders,

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
هَمَّازٍ مَّشَّآءٍۭ بِنَمِيمٍ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{68:12}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: A preventer of good, transgressing and sinful,

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Hinderer of the good, transgressor, malefactor

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
مَّنَّاعٍ لِّلْخَيْرِ مُعْتَدٍ أَثِيمٍ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{68:13}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Cruel, moreover, and an illegitimate pretender.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Greedy therewithal, intrusive.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
عُتُلٍّۭ بَعْدَ ذَٰلِكَ زَنِيمٍ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{68:14}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Because he is a possessor of wealth and children,

\textit{M. Pickthall}: It is because he is possessed of wealth and children

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
أَن كَانَ ذَا مَالٍ وَبَنِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{68:15}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: When Our verses are recited to him, he says, "Legends of the former peoples."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: That, when Our revelations are recited unto him, he saith: Mere fables of the men of old.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
إِذَا تُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْهِ ءَايَـٰتُنَا قَالَ أَسَـٰطِيرُ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{68:16}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: We will brand him upon the snout.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: We shall brand him on the nose.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
سَنَسِمُهُ عَلَى ٱلْخُرْطُومِ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{68:17}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Indeed, We have tried them as We tried the companions of the garden, when they swore to cut its fruit in the [early] morning

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Lo! We have tried them as We tried the owners of the garden when they vowed that they would pluck its fruit next morning,

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
إِنَّا بَلَوْنَـٰهُمْ كَمَا بَلَوْنَآ أَصْحَـٰبَ ٱلْجَنَّةِ إِذْ أَقْسَمُوا۟ لَيَصْرِمُنَّهَا مُصْبِحِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{68:18}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Without making exception.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And made no exception (for the Will of Allah);

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَلَا يَسْتَثْنُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{68:19}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: So there came upon it [i.e., the garden] an affliction from your Lord while they were asleep.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Then a visitation from thy Lord came upon it while they slept

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَطَافَ عَلَيْهَا طَآئِفٌ مِّن رَّبِّكَ وَهُمْ نَآئِمُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{68:20}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And it became as though reaped.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And in the morning it was as if plucked.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَأَصْبَحَتْ كَٱلصَّرِيمِ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{68:21}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And they called one another at morning,

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And they cried out one unto another in the morning,

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَتَنَادَوْا۟ مُصْبِحِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{68:22}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: [Saying], "Go early to your crop if you would cut the fruit."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Saying: Run unto your field if ye would pluck (the fruit).

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
أَنِ ٱغْدُوا۟ عَلَىٰ حَرْثِكُمْ إِن كُنتُمْ صَـٰرِمِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{68:23}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: So they set out, while lowering their voices,

\textit{M. Pickthall}: So they went off, saying one unto another in low tones:

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَٱنطَلَقُوا۟ وَهُمْ يَتَخَـٰفَتُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{68:24}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: [Saying], "There will surely not enter it today upon you [any] poor person."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: No needy man shall enter it to-day against you.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
أَن لَّا يَدْخُلَنَّهَا ٱلْيَوْمَ عَلَيْكُم مِّسْكِينٌ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{68:25}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And they went early in determination, [assuming themselves] able.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: They went betimes, strong in (this) purpose.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَغَدَوْا۟ عَلَىٰ حَرْدٍ قَـٰدِرِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{68:26}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: But when they saw it, they said, "Indeed, we are lost;

\textit{M. Pickthall}: But when they saw it, they said: Lo! we are in error!

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَلَمَّا رَأَوْهَا قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّا لَضَآلُّونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{68:27}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Rather, we have been deprived."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Nay, but we are desolate!

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
بَلْ نَحْنُ مَحْرُومُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{68:28}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: The most moderate of them said, "Did I not say to you, 'Why do you not exalt [Allāh]?'"

\textit{M. Pickthall}: The best among them said: Said I not unto you: Why glorify ye not (Allah)?

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَ أَوْسَطُهُمْ أَلَمْ أَقُل لَّكُمْ لَوْلَا تُسَبِّحُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{68:29}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: They said, "Exalted is our Lord! Indeed, we were wrongdoers."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: They said: Glorified be our Lord! Lo! we have been wrong-doers.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالُوا۟ سُبْحَـٰنَ رَبِّنَآ إِنَّا كُنَّا ظَـٰلِمِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{68:30}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Then they approached one another, blaming each other.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Then some of them drew near unto others, self-reproaching.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَأَقْبَلَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ يَتَلَـٰوَمُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{68:31}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: They said, "O woe to us; indeed we were transgressors.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: They said: Alas for us! In truth we were outrageous.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالُوا۟ يَـٰوَيْلَنَآ إِنَّا كُنَّا طَـٰغِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{68:32}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Perhaps our Lord will substitute for us [one] better than it. Indeed, we are toward our Lord desirous."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: It may be that our Lord will give us better than this in place thereof. Lo! we beseech our Lord.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
عَسَىٰ رَبُّنَآ أَن يُبْدِلَنَا خَيْرًا مِّنْهَآ إِنَّآ إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا رَٰغِبُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}

\section{Surah 18, Al-Kahf (The Cave)
Verses 1 -- 26}

The 69th revealed Surah. Revealed in Makkah


\noindent[\textbf{18:1}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: [All] praise is [due] to Allāh, who has sent down upon His Servant [Muḥammad ((\ar{ﷺ}))] the Book and has not made therein any deviance.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Praise be to Allah Who hath revealed the Scripture unto His slave, and hath not placed therein any crookedness,

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
 ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَنزَلَ عَلَىٰ عَبْدِهِ ٱلْكِتَـٰبَ وَلَمْ يَجْعَل لَّهُ عِوَجَا 
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{18:2}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: [He has made it] straight, to warn of severe punishment from Him and to give good tidings to the believers who do righteous deeds that they will have a good reward [i.e., Paradise]

\textit{M. Pickthall}: (But hath made it) straight, to give warning of stern punishment from Him, and to bring unto the believers who do good works the news that theirs will be a fair reward,

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَيِّمًا لِّيُنذِرَ بَأْسًا شَدِيدًا مِّن لَّدُنْهُ وَيُبَشِّرَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتِ أَنَّ لَهُمْ أَجْرًا حَسَنًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{18:3}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: In which they will remain forever

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Wherein they will abide for ever;

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
مَّـٰكِثِينَ فِيهِ أَبَدًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{18:4}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And to warn those who say, "Allāh has taken a son."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And to warn those who say: Allah hath chosen a son,

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَيُنذِرَ ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُوا۟ ٱتَّخَذَ ٱللَّهُ وَلَدًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{18:5}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: They have no knowledge of it, nor had their fathers. Grave is the word that comes out of their mouths; they speak not except a lie.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: (A thing) whereof they have no knowledge, nor (had) their fathers, Dreadful is the word that cometh out of their mouths. They speak naught but a lie.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
مَّا لَهُم بِهِ مِنْ عِلْمٍ وَلَا لِـَٔابَآئِهِمْ  كَبُرَتْ كَلِمَةً تَخْرُجُ مِنْ أَفْوَٰهِهِمْ  إِن يَقُولُونَ إِلَّا كَذِبًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{18:6}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Then perhaps you would kill yourself through grief over them, [O Muḥammad], if they do not believe in this message, [and] out of sorrow.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Yet it may be, if they believe not in this statement, that thou (Muhammad) wilt torment thy soul with grief over their footsteps.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَلَعَلَّكَ بَـٰخِعٌ نَّفْسَكَ عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَـٰرِهِمْ إِن لَّمْ يُؤْمِنُوا۟ بِهَـٰذَا ٱلْحَدِيثِ أَسَفًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{18:7}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Indeed, We have made that which is on the earth adornment for it that We may test them [as to] which of them is best in deed.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Lo! We have placed all that is on the earth as an ornament thereof that We may try them: which of them is best in conduct.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
إِنَّا جَعَلْنَا مَا عَلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ زِينَةً لَّهَا لِنَبْلُوَهُمْ أَيُّهُمْ أَحْسَنُ عَمَلًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{18:8}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And indeed, We will make that which is upon it [into] a barren ground.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And lo! We shall make all that is thereon a barren mound.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَإِنَّا لَجَـٰعِلُونَ مَا عَلَيْهَا صَعِيدًا جُرُزًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{18:9}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Or have you thought that the companions of the cave and the inscription were, among Our signs, a wonder?

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Or deemest thou that the People of the Cave and the Inscription are a wonder among Our portents?

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
أَمْ حَسِبْتَ أَنَّ أَصْحَـٰبَ ٱلْكَهْفِ وَٱلرَّقِيمِ كَانُوا۟ مِنْ ءَايَـٰتِنَا عَجَبًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{18:10}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: [Mention] when the youths retreated to the cave and said, "Our Lord, grant us from Yourself mercy and prepare for us from our affair right guidance."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: When the young men fled for refuge to the Cave and said: Our Lord! Give us mercy from Thy presence, and shape for us right conduct in our plight.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
إِذْ أَوَى ٱلْفِتْيَةُ إِلَى ٱلْكَهْفِ فَقَالُوا۟ رَبَّنَآ ءَاتِنَا مِن لَّدُنكَ رَحْمَةً وَهَيِّئْ لَنَا مِنْ أَمْرِنَا رَشَدًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{18:11}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: So We cast [a cover of sleep] over their ears within the cave for a number of years.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Then We sealed up their hearing in the Cave for a number of years.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَضَرَبْنَا عَلَىٰٓ ءَاذَانِهِمْ فِى ٱلْكَهْفِ سِنِينَ عَدَدًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{18:12}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Then We awakened them that We might show which of the two factions was most precise in calculating what [extent] they had remained in time.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And afterward We raised them up that We might know which of the two parties would best calculate the time that they had tarried.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
ثُمَّ بَعَثْنَـٰهُمْ لِنَعْلَمَ أَىُّ ٱلْحِزْبَيْنِ أَحْصَىٰ لِمَا لَبِثُوٓا۟ أَمَدًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{18:13}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: It is We who relate to you, [O Muḥammad], their story in truth. Indeed, they were youths who believed in their Lord, and We increased them in guidance.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: We narrate unto thee their story with truth. Lo! they were young men who believed in their Lord, and We increased them in guidance.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
نَّحْنُ نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ نَبَأَهُم بِٱلْحَقِّ  إِنَّهُمْ فِتْيَةٌ ءَامَنُوا۟ بِرَبِّهِمْ وَزِدْنَـٰهُمْ هُدًى
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{18:14}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And We bound [i.e., made firm] their hearts when they stood up and said, "Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth. Never will we invoke besides Him any deity. We would have certainly spoken, then, an excessive transgression.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And We made firm their hearts when they stood forth and said: Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth. We cry unto no Allah beside Him, for then should we utter an enormity.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَرَبَطْنَا عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمْ إِذْ قَامُوا۟ فَقَالُوا۟ رَبُّنَا رَبُّ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ لَن نَّدْعُوَا۟ مِن دُونِهِٓ إِلَـٰهًا  لَّقَدْ قُلْنَآ إِذًا شَطَطًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{18:15}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: These, our people, have taken besides Him deities. Why do they not bring for [worship of] them a clear evidence? And who is more unjust than one who invents about Allāh a lie?"

\textit{M. Pickthall}: These, our people, have chosen (other) gods beside Him though they bring no clear warrant (vouchsafed) to them. And who doth greater wrong than he who inventeth a lie concerning Allah?

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
هَـٰٓؤُلَآءِ قَوْمُنَا ٱتَّخَذُوا۟ مِن دُونِهِٓ ءَالِهَةً  لَّوْلَا يَأْتُونَ عَلَيْهِم بِسُلْطَـٰنٍۭ بَيِّنٍ  فَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ ٱفْتَرَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِبًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{18:16}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: [The youths said to one another], "And when you have withdrawn from them and that which they worship other than Allāh, retreat to the cave. Your Lord will spread out for you of His mercy and will prepare for you from your affair facility."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And when ye withdraw from them and that which they worship except Allah, then seek refuge in the Cave; your Lord will spread for you of His mercy and will prepare for you a pillow in your plight.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَإِذِ ٱعْتَزَلْتُمُوهُمْ وَمَا يَعْبُدُونَ إِلَّا ٱللَّهَ فَأْوُٓا۟ إِلَى ٱلْكَهْفِ يَنشُرْ لَكُمْ رَبُّكُم مِّن رَّحْمَتِهِ وَيُهَيِّئْ لَكُم مِّنْ أَمْرِكُم مِّرْفَقًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{18:17}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And [had you been present], you would see the sun when it rose, inclining away from their cave on the right, and when it set, passing away from them on the left, while they were [lying] within an open space thereof. That was from the signs of Allāh. He whom Allāh guides is the [rightly] guided, but he whom He sends astray - never will you find for him a protecting guide.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And thou mightest have seen the sun when it rose move away from their cave to the right, and when it set go past them on the left, and they were in the cleft thereof. That was (one) of the portents of Allah. He whom Allah guideth, he indeed is led aright, and he whom He sendeth astray, for him thou wilt not find a guiding friend.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
۞ وَتَرَى ٱلشَّمْسَ إِذَا طَلَعَت تَّزَٰوَرُ عَن كَهْفِهِمْ ذَاتَ ٱلْيَمِينِ وَإِذَا غَرَبَت تَّقْرِضُهُمْ ذَاتَ ٱلشِّمَالِ وَهُمْ فِى فَجْوَةٍ مِّنْهُ  ذَٰلِكَ مِنْ ءَايَـٰتِ ٱللَّهِ  مَن يَهْدِ ٱللَّهُ فَهُوَ ٱلْمُهْتَدِ  وَمَن يُضْلِلْ فَلَن تَجِدَ لَهُ وَلِيًّا مُّرْشِدًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{18:18}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And you would think them awake, while they were asleep. And We turned them to the right and to the left, while their dog stretched his forelegs at the entrance. If you had looked at them, you would have turned from them in flight and been filled by them with terror.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And thou wouldst have deemed them waking though they were asleep, and We caused them to turn over to the right and the left, and their dog stretching out his paws on the threshold. If thou hadst observed them closely thou hadst assuredly turned away from them in flight, and hadst been filled with awe of them.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَتَحْسَبُهُمْ أَيْقَاظًا وَهُمْ رُقُودٌ  وَنُقَلِّبُهُمْ ذَاتَ ٱلْيَمِينِ وَذَاتَ ٱلشِّمَالِ  وَكَلْبُهُم بَـٰسِطٌ ذِرَاعَيْهِ بِٱلْوَصِيدِ  لَوِ ٱطَّلَعْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ لَوَلَّيْتَ مِنْهُمْ فِرَارًا وَلَمُلِئْتَ مِنْهُمْ رُعْبًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{18:19}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And similarly, We awakened them that they might question one another. Said a speaker from among them, "How long have you remained [here]?" They said, "We have remained a day or part of a day." They said, "Your Lord is most knowing of how long you remained. So send one of you with this silver coin of yours to the city and let him look to which is the best of food and bring you provision from it and let him be cautious. And let no one be aware of you.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And in like manner We awakened them that they might question one another. A speaker from among them said: How long have ye tarried? They said: We have tarried a day or some part of a day, (Others) said: Your Lord best knoweth what ye have tarried. Now send one of you with this your silver coin unto the city, and let him see what food is purest there and bring you a supply thereof. Let him be courteous and let no man know of you.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَكَذَٰلِكَ بَعَثْنَـٰهُمْ لِيَتَسَآءَلُوا۟ بَيْنَهُمْ  قَالَ قَآئِلٌ مِّنْهُمْ كَمْ لَبِثْتُمْ  قَالُوا۟ لَبِثْنَا يَوْمًا أَوْ بَعْضَ يَوْمٍ  قَالُوا۟ رَبُّكُمْ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا لَبِثْتُمْ فَٱبْعَثُوٓا۟ أَحَدَكُم بِوَرِقِكُمْ هَـٰذِهِٓ إِلَى ٱلْمَدِينَةِ فَلْيَنظُرْ أَيُّهَآ أَزْكَىٰ طَعَامًا فَلْيَأْتِكُم بِرِزْقٍ مِّنْهُ وَلْيَتَلَطَّفْ وَلَا يُشْعِرَنَّ بِكُمْ أَحَدًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{18:20}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Indeed, if they come to know of you, they will stone you or return you to their religion. And never would you succeed, then - ever."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: For they, if they should come to know of you, will stone you or turn you back to their religion; then ye will never prosper.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
إِنَّهُمْ إِن يَظْهَرُوا۟ عَلَيْكُمْ يَرْجُمُوكُمْ أَوْ يُعِيدُوكُمْ فِى مِلَّتِهِمْ وَلَن تُفْلِحُوٓا۟ إِذًا أَبَدًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{18:21}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And similarly, We caused them to be found that they [who found them] would know that the promise of Allāh is truth and that of the Hour there is no doubt. [That was] when they disputed among themselves about their affair and [then] said, "Construct over them a structure. Their Lord is most knowing about them." Said those who prevailed in the matter, "We will surely take [for ourselves] over them a masjid."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And in like manner We disclosed them (to the people of the city) that they might know that the promise of Allah is true, and that, as for the Hour, there is no doubt concerning it. When (the people of the city) disputed of their case among themselves, they said: Build over them a building; their Lord knoweth best concerning them. Those who won their point said: We verily shall build a place of worship over them.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَكَذَٰلِكَ أَعْثَرْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ لِيَعْلَمُوٓا۟ أَنَّ وَعْدَ ٱللَّهِ حَقٌّ وَأَنَّ ٱلسَّاعَةَ لَا رَيْبَ فِيهَآ إِذْ يَتَنَـٰزَعُونَ بَيْنَهُمْ أَمْرَهُمْ  فَقَالُوا۟ ٱبْنُوا۟ عَلَيْهِم بُنْيَـٰنًا  رَّبُّهُمْ أَعْلَمُ بِهِمْ  قَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ غَلَبُوا۟ عَلَىٰٓ أَمْرِهِمْ لَنَتَّخِذَنَّ عَلَيْهِم مَّسْجِدًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{18:22}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: They [i.e., people] will say there were three, the fourth of them being their dog; and they will say there were five, the sixth of them being their dog - guessing at the unseen; and they will say there were seven, and the eighth of them was their dog. Say, [O Muḥammad], "My Lord is most knowing of their number. None knows them except a few. So do not argue about them except with an obvious argument and do not inquire about them among [the speculators] from anyone."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: (Some) will say: They were three, their dog the fourth, and (some) say: Five, their dog the sixth, guessing at random; and (some) say: Seven, and their dog the eighth. Say (O Muhammad): My Lord is Best Aware of their number. None knoweth them save a few. So contend not concerning them except with an outward contending, and ask not any of them to pronounce concerning them.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
سَيَقُولُونَ ثَلَـٰثَةٌ رَّابِعُهُمْ كَلْبُهُمْ وَيَقُولُونَ خَمْسَةٌ سَادِسُهُمْ كَلْبُهُمْ رَجْمًا بِٱلْغَيْبِ  وَيَقُولُونَ سَبْعَةٌ وَثَامِنُهُمْ كَلْبُهُمْ  قُل رَّبِّىٓ أَعْلَمُ بِعِدَّتِهِم مَّا يَعْلَمُهُمْ إِلَّا قَلِيلٌ  فَلَا تُمَارِ فِيهِمْ إِلَّا مِرَآءً ظَـٰهِرًا وَلَا تَسْتَفْتِ فِيهِم مِّنْهُمْ أَحَدًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{18:23}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And never say of anything, "Indeed, I will do that tomorrow,"

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And say not of anything: Lo! I shall do that tomorrow,

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَلَا تَقُولَنَّ لِشَا۟ىْءٍ إِنِّى فَاعِلٌ ذَٰلِكَ غَدًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{18:24}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Except [when adding], "If Allāh wills." And remember your Lord when you forget [it] and say, "Perhaps my Lord will guide me to what is nearer than this to right conduct."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Except if Allah will. And remember thy Lord when thou forgettest, and say: It may be that my Lord guideth me unto a nearer way of truth than this.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
إِلَّآ أَن يَشَآءَ ٱللَّهُ  وَٱذْكُر رَّبَّكَ إِذَا نَسِيتَ وَقُلْ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَهْدِيَنِ رَبِّى لِأَقْرَبَ مِنْ هَـٰذَا رَشَدًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{18:25}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And they remained in their cave for three hundred years and exceeded by nine.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And (it is said) they tarried in their Cave three hundred years and add nine.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَلَبِثُوا۟ فِى كَهْفِهِمْ ثَلَـٰثَ مِا۟ئَةٍ سِنِينَ وَٱزْدَادُوا۟ تِسْعًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{18:26}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Say, "Allāh is most knowing of how long they remained. He has [knowledge of] the unseen [aspects] of the heavens and the earth. How Seeing is He and how Hearing! They have not besides Him any protector, and He shares not His legislation with anyone."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Say: Allah is Best Aware how long they tarried. His is the Invisible of the heavens and the earth. How clear of sight is He and keen of hearing! They have no protecting friend beside Him, and He maketh none to share in His government.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قُلِ ٱللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا لَبِثُوا۟  لَهُ غَيْبُ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ  أَبْصِرْ بِهِ وَأَسْمِعْ  مَا لَهُم مِّن دُونِهِ مِن وَلِىٍّ وَلَا يُشْرِكُ فِى حُكْمِهِٓ أَحَدًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}

\section{Surah 18, Al-Kahf (The Cave)
Verses 83 -- 99}

The 69th revealed Surah. Revealed in Makkah


\noindent[\textbf{18:83}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And they ask you, [O Muḥammad], about Dhul-Qarnayn. Say, "I will recite to you about him a report."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: They will ask thee of Dhu'l-Qarneyn. Say: I shall recite unto you a remembrance of him.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَيَسْـَٔلُونَكَ عَن ذِى ٱلْقَرْنَيْنِ  قُلْ سَأَتْلُوا۟ عَلَيْكُم مِّنْهُ ذِكْرًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{18:84}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Indeed, We established him upon the earth, and We gave him from everything a way [i.e., means].

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Lo! We made him strong in the land and gave him unto every thing a road.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
إِنَّا مَكَّنَّا لَهُ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَءَاتَيْنَـٰهُ مِن كُلِّ شَىْءٍ سَبَبًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{18:85}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: So he followed a way

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And he followed a road

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَأَتْبَعَ سَبَبًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{18:86}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Until, when he reached the setting of the sun [i.e., the west], he found it [as if] setting in a body of dark water, and he found near it a people. We [i.e., Allāh] said, "O Dhul-Qarnayn, either you punish [them] or else adopt among them [a way of] goodness."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Till, when he reached the setting-place of the sun, he found it setting in a muddy spring, and found a people thereabout. We said: O Dhu'l-Qarneyn! Either punish or show them kindness.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا بَلَغَ مَغْرِبَ ٱلشَّمْسِ وَجَدَهَا تَغْرُبُ فِى عَيْنٍ حَمِئَةٍ وَوَجَدَ عِندَهَا قَوْمًا  قُلْنَا يَـٰذَا ٱلْقَرْنَيْنِ إِمَّآ أَن تُعَذِّبَ وَإِمَّآ أَن تَتَّخِذَ فِيهِمْ حُسْنًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{18:87}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: He said, "As for one who wrongs, we will punish him. Then he will be returned to his Lord, and He will punish him with a terrible punishment [i.e., Hellfire].

\textit{M. Pickthall}: He said: As for him who doeth wrong, we shall punish him, and then he will be brought back unto his Lord, Who will punish him with awful punishment!

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَ أَمَّا مَن ظَلَمَ فَسَوْفَ نُعَذِّبُهُ ثُمَّ يُرَدُّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِ فَيُعَذِّبُهُ عَذَابًا نُّكْرًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{18:88}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: But as for one who believes and does righteousness, he will have a reward of the best [i.e., Paradise], and we [i.e., Dhul-Qarnayn] will speak to him from our command with ease."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: But as for him who believeth and doeth right, good will be his reward, and We shall speak unto him a mild command.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَأَمَّا مَنْ ءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَـٰلِحًا فَلَهُ جَزَآءً ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ  وَسَنَقُولُ لَهُ مِنْ أَمْرِنَا يُسْرًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{18:89}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Then he followed a way

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Then he followed a road

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
ثُمَّ أَتْبَعَ سَبَبًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{18:90}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Until, when he came to the rising of the sun [i.e., the east], he found it rising on a people for whom We had not made against it any shield.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Till, when he reached the rising-place of the sun, he found it rising on a people for whom We had appointed no shelter therefrom.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا بَلَغَ مَطْلِعَ ٱلشَّمْسِ وَجَدَهَا تَطْلُعُ عَلَىٰ قَوْمٍ لَّمْ نَجْعَل لَّهُم مِّن دُونِهَا سِتْرًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{18:91}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Thus. And We had encompassed [all] that he had in knowledge.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: So (it was). And We knew all concerning him.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
كَذَٰلِكَ وَقَدْ أَحَطْنَا بِمَا لَدَيْهِ خُبْرًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{18:92}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Then he followed a way

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Then he followed a road

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
ثُمَّ أَتْبَعَ سَبَبًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{18:93}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Until, when he reached [a pass] between two mountains, he found beside them a people who could hardly understand [his] speech.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Till, when he came between the two mountains, he found upon their hither side a folk that scarce could understand a saying.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا بَلَغَ بَيْنَ ٱلسَّدَّيْنِ وَجَدَ مِن دُونِهِمَا قَوْمًا لَّا يَكَادُونَ يَفْقَهُونَ قَوْلًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{18:94}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: They said, "O Dhul-Qarnayn, indeed Gog and Magog are [great] corrupters in the land. So may we assign for you an expenditure that you might make between us and them a barrier?"

\textit{M. Pickthall}: They said: O Dhu'l-Qarneyn! Lo! Gog and Magog are spoiling the land. So may we pay thee tribute on condition that thou set a barrier between us and them?

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالُوا۟ يَـٰذَا ٱلْقَرْنَيْنِ إِنَّ يَأْجُوجَ وَمَأْجُوجَ مُفْسِدُونَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ فَهَلْ نَجْعَلُ لَكَ خَرْجًا عَلَىٰٓ أَن تَجْعَلَ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَهُمْ سَدًّا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{18:95}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: He said, "That in which my Lord has established me is better [than what you offer], but assist me with strength [i.e., manpower]; I will make between you and them a dam.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: He said: That wherein my Lord hath established me is better (than your tribute). Do but help me with strength (of men), I will set between you and them a bank.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَ مَا مَكَّنِّى فِيهِ رَبِّى خَيْرٌ فَأَعِينُونِى بِقُوَّةٍ أَجْعَلْ بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَهُمْ رَدْمًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{18:96}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Bring me bars of iron" - until, when he had leveled [them] between the two mountain walls, he said, "Blow [with bellows]," until when he had made it [like] fire, he said, "Bring me, that I may pour over it molten copper."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Give me pieces of iron - till, when he had levelled up (the gap) between the cliffs, he said: Blow! - till, when he had made it a fire, he said: Bring me molten copper to pour thereon.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
ءَاتُونِى زُبَرَ ٱلْحَدِيدِ  حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا سَاوَىٰ بَيْنَ ٱلصَّدَفَيْنِ قَالَ ٱنفُخُوا۟  حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَعَلَهُ نَارًا قَالَ ءَاتُونِىٓ أُفْرِغْ عَلَيْهِ قِطْرًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{18:97}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: So they [i.e., Gog and Magog] were unable to pass over it, nor were they able [to effect] in it any penetration.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And (Gog and Magog) were not able to surmount, nor could they pierce (it).

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَمَا ٱسْطَـٰعُوٓا۟ أَن يَظْهَرُوهُ وَمَا ٱسْتَطَـٰعُوا۟ لَهُ نَقْبًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{18:98}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: [Dhul-Qarnayn] said, "This is a mercy from my Lord; but when the promise of my Lord comes [i.e., approaches], He will make it level, and ever is the promise of my Lord true."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: He said: This is a mercy from my Lord; but when the promise of my Lord cometh to pass, He will lay it low, for the promise of my Lord is true.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَ هَـٰذَا رَحْمَةٌ مِّن رَّبِّى  فَإِذَا جَآءَ وَعْدُ رَبِّى جَعَلَهُ دَكَّآءَ  وَكَانَ وَعْدُ رَبِّى حَقًّا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{18:99}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And We will leave them that day surging over each other, and [then] the Horn will be blown, and We will assemble them in [one] assembly.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And on that day we shall let some of them surge against others, and the Trumpet will be blown. Then We shall gather them together in one gathering.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
۞ وَتَرَكْنَا بَعْضَهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ يَمُوجُ فِى بَعْضٍ  وَنُفِخَ فِى ٱلصُّورِ فَجَمَعْنَـٰهُمْ جَمْعًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}

\section{Surah 17, Al-'Isrā (The Night Journey)
Verses 78 -- 100}

The 50th revealed Surah. Revealed in Makkah


\noindent[\textbf{17:78}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Establish prayer at the decline of the sun [from its meridian] until the darkness of the night and [also] the Qur’ān [i.e., recitation] of dawn. Indeed, the recitation of dawn is ever witnessed.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Establish worship at the going down of the sun until the dark of night, and (the recital of) the Qur'an at dawn. Lo! (the recital of) the Qur'an at dawn is ever witnessed.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
أَقِمِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ لِدُلُوكِ ٱلشَّمْسِ إِلَىٰ غَسَقِ ٱلَّيْلِ وَقُرْءَانَ ٱلْفَجْرِ  إِنَّ قُرْءَانَ ٱلْفَجْرِ كَانَ مَشْهُودًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{17:79}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And from [part of] the night, pray with it [i.e., recitation of the Qur’ān] as additional [worship] for you; it is expected that your Lord will resurrect you to a praised station.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And some part of the night awake for it, a largess for thee. It may be that thy Lord will raise thee to a praised estate.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَمِنَ ٱلَّيْلِ فَتَهَجَّدْ بِهِ نَافِلَةً لَّكَ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَبْعَثَكَ رَبُّكَ مَقَامًا مَّحْمُودًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{17:80}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And say, "My Lord, cause me to enter a sound entrance and to exit a sound exit and grant me from Yourself a supporting authority."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And say: My Lord! Cause me to come in with a firm incoming and to go out with a firm outgoing. And give me from Thy presence a sustaining Power.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَقُل رَّبِّ أَدْخِلْنِى مُدْخَلَ صِدْقٍ وَأَخْرِجْنِى مُخْرَجَ صِدْقٍ وَٱجْعَل لِّى مِن لَّدُنكَ سُلْطَـٰنًا نَّصِيرًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{17:81}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And say, "Truth has come, and falsehood has departed. Indeed is falsehood, [by nature], ever bound to depart."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And say: Truth hath come and falsehood hath vanished away. Lo! falsehood is ever bound to vanish.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَقُلْ جَآءَ ٱلْحَقُّ وَزَهَقَ ٱلْبَـٰطِلُ  إِنَّ ٱلْبَـٰطِلَ كَانَ زَهُوقًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{17:82}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And We send down of the Qur’ān that which is healing and mercy for the believers, but it does not increase the wrongdoers except in loss.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And We reveal of the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy for believers though it increase the evil-doers in naught save ruin.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَنُنَزِّلُ مِنَ ٱلْقُرْءَانِ مَا هُوَ شِفَآءٌ وَرَحْمَةٌ لِّلْمُؤْمِنِينَ  وَلَا يَزِيدُ ٱلظَّـٰلِمِينَ إِلَّا خَسَارًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{17:83}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And when We bestow favor upon man [i.e., the disbeliever], he turns away and distances himself; and when evil touches him, he is ever despairing.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And when We make life pleasant unto man, he turneth away and is averse; and when ill toucheth him he is in despair.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَإِذَآ أَنْعَمْنَا عَلَى ٱلْإِنسَـٰنِ أَعْرَضَ وَنَـَٔا بِجَانِبِهِ  وَإِذَا مَسَّهُ ٱلشَّرُّ كَانَ يَـُٔوسًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{17:84}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Say, "Each works according to his manner, but your Lord is most knowing of who is best guided in way."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Say: Each one doth according to his rule of conduct, and thy Lord is Best Aware of him whose way is right.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قُلْ كُلٌّ يَعْمَلُ عَلَىٰ شَاكِلَتِهِ فَرَبُّكُمْ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنْ هُوَ أَهْدَىٰ سَبِيلًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{17:85}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And they ask you, [O Muḥammad], about the soul. Say, "The soul is of the affair [i.e., concern] of my Lord. And you [i.e., mankind] have not been given of knowledge except a little."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: They are asking thee concerning the Spirit. Say: The Spirit is by command of my Lord, and of knowledge ye have been vouchsafed but little.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَيَسْـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلرُّوحِ  قُلِ ٱلرُّوحُ مِنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّى وَمَآ أُوتِيتُم مِّنَ ٱلْعِلْمِ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{17:86}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And if We willed, We could surely do away with that which We revealed to you. Then you would not find for yourself concerning it an advocate against Us.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And if We willed We could withdraw that which We have revealed unto thee, then wouldst thou find no guardian for thee against Us in respect thereof.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَلَئِن شِئْنَا لَنَذْهَبَنَّ بِٱلَّذِىٓ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْكَ ثُمَّ لَا تَجِدُ لَكَ بِهِ عَلَيْنَا وَكِيلًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{17:87}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Except [We have left it with you] as a mercy from your Lord. Indeed, His favor upon you has ever been great.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: (It is naught) save mercy from thy Lord. Lo! His kindness unto thee was ever great.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
إِلَّا رَحْمَةً مِّن رَّبِّكَ  إِنَّ فَضْلَهُ كَانَ عَلَيْكَ كَبِيرًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{17:88}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Say, "If mankind and the jinn gathered in order to produce the like of this Qur’ān, they could not produce the like of it, even if they were to each other assistants."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Say: Verily, though mankind and the jinn should assemble to produce the like of this Qur'an, they could not produce the like thereof though they were helpers one of another.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قُل لَّئِنِ ٱجْتَمَعَتِ ٱلْإِنسُ وَٱلْجِنُّ عَلَىٰٓ أَن يَأْتُوا۟ بِمِثْلِ هَـٰذَا ٱلْقُرْءَانِ لَا يَأْتُونَ بِمِثْلِهِ وَلَوْ كَانَ بَعْضُهُمْ لِبَعْضٍ ظَهِيرًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{17:89}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And We have certainly diversified for the people in this Qur’ān from every [kind of] example, but most of the people refused except disbelief.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And verily We have displayed for mankind in this Qur'an all kind of similitudes, but most of mankind refuse aught save disbelief.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَلَقَدْ صَرَّفْنَا لِلنَّاسِ فِى هَـٰذَا ٱلْقُرْءَانِ مِن كُلِّ مَثَلٍ فَأَبَىٰٓ أَكْثَرُ ٱلنَّاسِ إِلَّا كُفُورًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{17:90}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And they say, "We will not believe you until you break open for us from the ground a spring

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And they say: We will not put faith in thee till thou cause a spring to gush forth from the earth for us;

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَقَالُوا۟ لَن نُّؤْمِنَ لَكَ حَتَّىٰ تَفْجُرَ لَنَا مِنَ ٱلْأَرْضِ يَنبُوعًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{17:91}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Or [until] you have a garden of palm trees and grapes and make rivers gush forth within them in force [and abundance]

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Or thou have a garden of date-palms and grapes, and cause rivers to gush forth therein abundantly;

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
أَوْ تَكُونَ لَكَ جَنَّةٌ مِّن نَّخِيلٍ وَعِنَبٍ فَتُفَجِّرَ ٱلْأَنْهَـٰرَ خِلَـٰلَهَا تَفْجِيرًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{17:92}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Or you make the heaven fall upon us in fragments as you have claimed or you bring Allāh and the angels before [us]

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Or thou cause the heaven to fall upon us piecemeal, as thou hast pretended, or bring Allah and the angels as a warrant;

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
أَوْ تُسْقِطَ ٱلسَّمَآءَ كَمَا زَعَمْتَ عَلَيْنَا كِسَفًا أَوْ تَأْتِىَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْمَلَـٰٓئِكَةِ قَبِيلًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{17:93}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Or you have a house of ornament [i.e., gold] or you ascend into the sky. And [even then], we will not believe in your ascension until you bring down to us a book we may read." Say, "Exalted is my Lord! Was I ever but a human messenger?"

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Or thou have a house of gold; or thou ascend up into heaven, and even then we will put no faith in thine ascension till thou bring down for us a book that we can read. Say (O Muhammad): My Lord be Glorified! Am I aught save a mortal messenger?

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
أَوْ يَكُونَ لَكَ بَيْتٌ مِّن زُخْرُفٍ أَوْ تَرْقَىٰ فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَلَن نُّؤْمِنَ لِرُقِيِّكَ حَتَّىٰ تُنَزِّلَ عَلَيْنَا كِتَـٰبًا نَّقْرَؤُهُ  قُلْ سُبْحَانَ رَبِّى هَلْ كُنتُ إِلَّا بَشَرًا رَّسُولًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{17:94}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And what prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them except that they said, "Has Allāh sent a human messenger?"

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And naught prevented mankind from believing when the guidance came unto them save that they said: Hath Allah sent a mortal as (His) messenger?

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَمَا مَنَعَ ٱلنَّاسَ أَن يُؤْمِنُوٓا۟ إِذْ جَآءَهُمُ ٱلْهُدَىٰٓ إِلَّآ أَن قَالُوٓا۟ أَبَعَثَ ٱللَّهُ بَشَرًا رَّسُولًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{17:95}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Say, "If there were upon the earth angels walking securely, We would have sent down to them from the heaven an angel [as a] messenger."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Say: If there were in the earth angels walking secure, We had sent down for them from heaven an angel as messenger.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قُل لَّوْ كَانَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مَلَـٰٓئِكَةٌ يَمْشُونَ مُطْمَئِنِّينَ لَنَزَّلْنَا عَلَيْهِم مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَلَكًا رَّسُولًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{17:96}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Say, "Sufficient is Allāh as Witness between me and you. Indeed He is ever, concerning His servants, Aware and Seeing."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Say: Allah sufficeth for a witness between me and you. Lo! He is Knower, Seer of His slaves.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قُلْ كَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ شَهِيدًا بَيْنِى وَبَيْنَكُمْ  إِنَّهُ كَانَ بِعِبَادِهِ خَبِيرًا بَصِيرًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{17:97}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And whoever Allāh guides - he is the [rightly] guided; and whoever He sends astray - you will never find for them protectors besides Him, and We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection [fallen] on their faces - blind, dumb and deaf. Their refuge is Hell; every time it subsides, We increase [for] them blazing fire.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And he whom Allah guideth, he is led aright; while, as for him whom He sendeth astray, for them thou wilt find no protecting friends beside Him, and We shall assemble them on the Day of Resurrection on their faces, blind, dumb and deaf; their habitation will be hell; whenever it abateth, We increase the flame for them.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَمَن يَهْدِ ٱللَّهُ فَهُوَ ٱلْمُهْتَدِ  وَمَن يُضْلِلْ فَلَن تَجِدَ لَهُمْ أَوْلِيَآءَ مِن دُونِهِ  وَنَحْشُرُهُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَـٰمَةِ عَلَىٰ وُجُوهِهِمْ عُمْيًا وَبُكْمًا وَصُمًّا  مَّأْوَىٰهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ  كُلَّمَا خَبَتْ زِدْنَـٰهُمْ سَعِيرًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{17:98}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: That is their recompense because they disbelieved in Our verses and said, "When we are bones and crumbled particles, will we [truly] be resurrected [in] a new creation?"

\textit{M. Pickthall}: That is their reward because they disbelieved Our revelations and said: When we are bones and fragments shall we, forsooth, be raised up as a new creation?

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
ذَٰلِكَ جَزَآؤُهُم بِأَنَّهُمْ كَفَرُوا۟ بِـَٔايَـٰتِنَا وَقَالُوٓا۟ أَءِذَا كُنَّا عِظَـٰمًا وَرُفَـٰتًا أَءِنَّا لَمَبْعُوثُونَ خَلْقًا جَدِيدًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{17:99}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Do they not see that Allāh, who created the heavens and earth, is [the one] Able to create the likes of them? And He has appointed for them a term, about which there is no doubt. But the wrongdoers refuse except disbelief.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Have they not seen that Allah Who created the heavens and the earth is Able to create the like of them, and hath appointed for them an end whereof there is no doubt? But the wrong-doers refuse aught save disbelief.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
۞ أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا۟ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ قَادِرٌ عَلَىٰٓ أَن يَخْلُقَ مِثْلَهُمْ وَجَعَلَ لَهُمْ أَجَلًا لَّا رَيْبَ فِيهِ فَأَبَى ٱلظَّـٰلِمُونَ إِلَّا كُفُورًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{17:100}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Say [to them], "If you possessed the depositories of the mercy of my Lord, then you would withhold out of fear of spending." And ever has man been stingy.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Say (unto them): If ye possessed the treasures of the mercy of my Lord, ye would surely hold them back for fear of spending, for man was ever grudging.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قُل لَّوْ أَنتُمْ تَمْلِكُونَ خَزَآئِنَ رَحْمَةِ رَبِّىٓ إِذًا لَّأَمْسَكْتُمْ خَشْيَةَ ٱلْإِنفَاقِ  وَكَانَ ٱلْإِنسَـٰنُ قَتُورًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}

\section{Surah 25, Al-Furqān (The Criterion)
Verses 1 -- 29}

The 42nd revealed Surah. Revealed in Makkah


\noindent[\textbf{25:1}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His Servant that he may be to the worlds a warner -

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Blessed is He Who hath revealed unto His slave the Criterion (of right and wrong), that he may be a warner to the peoples.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
 تَبَارَكَ ٱلَّذِى نَزَّلَ ٱلْفُرْقَانَ عَلَىٰ عَبْدِهِ لِيَكُونَ لِلْعَـٰلَمِينَ نَذِيرًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{25:2}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and who has not taken a son and has not had a partner in dominion and has created each thing and determined it with [precise] determination.
