\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: None will have [power of] intercession except he who had taken from the Most Merciful a covenant.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: They will have no power of intercession, save him who hath made a covenant with his Lord.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
لَّا يَمْلِكُونَ ٱلشَّفَـٰعَةَ إِلَّا مَنِ ٱتَّخَذَ عِندَ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ عَهْدًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{19:88}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken [for Himself] a son."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And they say: The Beneficent hath taken unto Himself a son.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَقَالُوا۟ ٱتَّخَذَ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنُ وَلَدًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{19:89}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: You have done an atrocious thing.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Assuredly ye utter a disastrous thing

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
لَّقَدْ جِئْتُمْ شَيْـًٔا إِدًّا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{19:90}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: The heavens almost rupture therefrom and the earth splits open and the mountains collapse in devastation

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Whereby almost the heavens are torn, and the earth is split asunder and the mountains fall in ruins,

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
تَكَادُ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتُ يَتَفَطَّرْنَ مِنْهُ وَتَنشَقُّ ٱلْأَرْضُ وَتَخِرُّ ٱلْجِبَالُ هَدًّا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{19:91}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: That they attribute to the Most Merciful a son.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: That ye ascribe unto the Beneficent a son,

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
أَن دَعَوْا۟ لِلرَّحْمَـٰنِ وَلَدًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{19:92}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And it is not appropriate for the Most Merciful that He should take a son.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: When it is not meet for (the Majesty of) the Beneficent that He should choose a son.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَمَا يَنبَغِى لِلرَّحْمَـٰنِ أَن يَتَّخِذَ وَلَدًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{19:93}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: There is no one in the heavens and earth but that he comes to the Most Merciful as a servant.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: There is none in the heavens and the earth but cometh unto the Beneficent as a slave.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
إِن كُلُّ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ إِلَّآ ءَاتِى ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ عَبْدًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{19:94}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: He has enumerated them and counted them a [full] counting.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Verily He knoweth them and numbereth them with (right) numbering.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
لَّقَدْ أَحْصَىٰهُمْ وَعَدَّهُمْ عَدًّا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{19:95}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And all of them are coming to Him on the Day of Resurrection alone.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And each one of them will come unto Him on the Day of Resurrection, alone.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَكُلُّهُمْ ءَاتِيهِ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَـٰمَةِ فَرْدًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{19:96}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Lo! those who believe and do good works, the Beneficent will appoint for them love.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتِ سَيَجْعَلُ لَهُمُ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنُ وُدًّا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{19:97}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: So, [O Muḥammad], We have only made it [i.e., the Qur’ān] easy in your tongue [i.e., the Arabic language] that you may give good tidings thereby to the righteous and warn thereby a hostile people.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And We make (this Scripture) easy in thy tongue, (O Muhammad) only that thou mayst bear good tidings therewith unto those who ward off (evil), and warn therewith the froward folk.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَإِنَّمَا يَسَّرْنَـٰهُ بِلِسَانِكَ لِتُبَشِّرَ بِهِ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ وَتُنذِرَ بِهِ قَوْمًا لُّدًّا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{19:98}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And how many have We destroyed before them of generations? Do you perceive of them anyone or hear from them a sound?

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And how many a generation before them have We destroyed! Canst thou (Muhammad) see a single man of them, or hear from them the slightest sound?

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَكَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا قَبْلَهُم مِّن قَرْنٍ هَلْ تُحِسُّ مِنْهُم مِّنْ أَحَدٍ أَوْ تَسْمَعُ لَهُمْ رِكْزًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}

\section{Surah 20, Ţāhā (Ta-Ha)
All Verses (1 -- 135)}

The 45th revealed Surah. Revealed in Makkah


\noindent[\textbf{20:1}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Ṭā, Hā.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Ta. Ha.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
 طه
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:2}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: We have not sent down to you the Qur’ān that you be distressed

\textit{M. Pickthall}: We have not revealed unto thee (Muhammad) this Qur'an that thou shouldst be distressed,

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
مَآ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْكَ ٱلْقُرْءَانَ لِتَشْقَىٰٓ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:3}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: But only as a reminder for those who fear [Allāh] -

\textit{M. Pickthall}: But as a reminder unto him who feareth,

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
إِلَّا تَذْكِرَةً لِّمَن يَخْشَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:4}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: A revelation from He who created the earth and highest heavens,

\textit{M. Pickthall}: A revelation from Him Who created the earth and the high heavens,

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
تَنزِيلًا مِّمَّنْ خَلَقَ ٱلْأَرْضَ وَٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ ٱلْعُلَى
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:5}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: The Most Merciful [who is] above the Throne established.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: The Beneficent One, Who is established on the Throne.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنُ عَلَى ٱلْعَرْشِ ٱسْتَوَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:6}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: To Him belongs what is in the heavens and what is on the earth and what is between them and what is under the soil.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Unto Him belongeth whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is in the earth, and whatsoever is between them, and whatsoever is beneath the sod.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
لَهُ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا وَمَا تَحْتَ ٱلثَّرَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:7}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And if you speak aloud - then indeed, He knows the secret and what is [even] more hidden.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And if thou speakest aloud, then lo! He knoweth the secret (thought) and (that which is yet) more hidden.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَإِن تَجْهَرْ بِٱلْقَوْلِ فَإِنَّهُ يَعْلَمُ ٱلسِّرَّ وَأَخْفَى
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:8}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Allāh - there is no deity except Him. To Him belong the best names.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Allah! There is no Allah save Him. His are the most beautiful names.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ  لَهُ ٱلْأَسْمَآءُ ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:9}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And has the story of Moses reached you? -

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Hath there come unto thee the story of Moses?

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَهَلْ أَتَىٰكَ حَدِيثُ مُوسَىٰٓ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:10}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: When he saw a fire and said to his family, "Stay here; indeed, I have perceived a fire; perhaps I can bring you a torch or find at the fire some guidance."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: When he saw a fire and said unto his folk: Lo! Wait! I see a fire afar off. Peradventure I may bring you a brand therefrom or may find guidance at the fire.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
إِذْ رَءَا نَارًا فَقَالَ لِأَهْلِهِ ٱمْكُثُوٓا۟ إِنِّىٓ ءَانَسْتُ نَارًا لَّعَلِّىٓ ءَاتِيكُم مِّنْهَا بِقَبَسٍ أَوْ أَجِدُ عَلَى ٱلنَّارِ هُدًى
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:11}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And when he came to it, he was called, "O Moses,

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And when he reached it, he was called by name: O Moses!

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَلَمَّآ أَتَىٰهَا نُودِىَ يَـٰمُوسَىٰٓ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:12}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Indeed, I am your Lord, so remove your sandals. Indeed, you are in the blessed valley of Ṭuwā.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Lo! I, even I, am thy Lord, So take off thy shoes, for lo! thou art in the holy valley of Tuwa.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
إِنِّىٓ أَنَا رَبُّكَ فَٱخْلَعْ نَعْلَيْكَ  إِنَّكَ بِٱلْوَادِ ٱلْمُقَدَّسِ طُوًى
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:13}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And I have chosen you, so listen to what is revealed [to you].

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And I have chosen thee, so hearken unto that which is inspired.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَأَنَا ٱخْتَرْتُكَ فَٱسْتَمِعْ لِمَا يُوحَىٰٓ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:14}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Indeed, I am Allāh. There is no deity except Me, so worship Me and establish prayer for My remembrance.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Lo! I, even I, am Allah, There is no Allah save Me. So serve Me and establish worship for My remembrance.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
إِنَّنِىٓ أَنَا ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنَا فَٱعْبُدْنِى وَأَقِمِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ لِذِكْرِىٓ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:15}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Indeed, the Hour is coming - I almost conceal it - so that every soul may be recompensed according to that for which it strives.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Lo! the Hour is surely coming. But I will to keep it hidden, that every soul may be rewarded for that which it striveth (to achieve).

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
إِنَّ ٱلسَّاعَةَ ءَاتِيَةٌ أَكَادُ أُخْفِيهَا لِتُجْزَىٰ كُلُّ نَفْسٍۭ بِمَا تَسْعَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:16}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: So do not let one avert you from it who does not believe in it and follows his desire, for you [then] would perish.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Therefor, let not him turn thee aside from (the thought of) it who believeth not therein but followeth his own desire, lest thou perish.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَلَا يَصُدَّنَّكَ عَنْهَا مَن لَّا يُؤْمِنُ بِهَا وَٱتَّبَعَ هَوَىٰهُ فَتَرْدَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:17}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And what is that in your right hand, O Moses?"

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And what is that in thy right hand, O Moses?

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَمَا تِلْكَ بِيَمِينِكَ يَـٰمُوسَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:18}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: He said, "It is my staff; I lean upon it, and I bring down leaves for my sheep and I have therein other uses."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: He said: This is my staff whereon I lean, and wherewith I bear down branches for my sheep, and wherein I find other uses.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَ هِىَ عَصَاىَ أَتَوَكَّؤُا۟ عَلَيْهَا وَأَهُشُّ بِهَا عَلَىٰ غَنَمِى وَلِىَ فِيهَا مَـَٔارِبُ أُخْرَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:19}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: [Allāh] said, "Throw it down, O Moses."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: He said: Cast it down, O Moses!

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَ أَلْقِهَا يَـٰمُوسَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:20}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: So he threw it down, and thereupon it was a snake, moving swiftly.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: So he cast it down, and lo! it was a serpent, gliding.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَأَلْقَىٰهَا فَإِذَا هِىَ حَيَّةٌ تَسْعَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:21}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: [Allāh] said, "Seize it and fear not; We will return it to its former condition.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: He said: Grasp it and fear not. We shall return it to its former state.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَ خُذْهَا وَلَا تَخَفْ  سَنُعِيدُهَا سِيرَتَهَا ٱلْأُولَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:22}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And draw in your hand to your side; it will come out white without disease - another sign,

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And thrust thy hand within thine armpit, it will come forth white without hurt. (That will be) another token.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَٱضْمُمْ يَدَكَ إِلَىٰ جَنَاحِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَآءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوٓءٍ ءَايَةً أُخْرَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:23}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: That We may show you [some] of Our greater signs.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: That We may show thee (some) of Our greater portents,

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
لِنُرِيَكَ مِنْ ءَايَـٰتِنَا ٱلْكُبْرَى
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:24}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Go to Pharaoh. Indeed, he has transgressed [i.e., tyrannized]."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Go thou unto Pharaoh! Lo! he hath transgressed (the bounds).

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
ٱذْهَبْ إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّهُ طَغَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:25}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: [Moses] said, "My Lord, expand [i.e., relax] for me my breast [with assurance]

\textit{M. Pickthall}: (Moses) said: My Lord! relieve my mind

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَ رَبِّ ٱشْرَحْ لِى صَدْرِى
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:26}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And ease for me my task

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And ease my task for me;

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَيَسِّرْ لِىٓ أَمْرِى
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:27}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And untie the knot from my tongue

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And loose a knot from my tongue,

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَٱحْلُلْ عُقْدَةً مِّن لِّسَانِى
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:28}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: That they may understand my speech.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: That they may understand my saying.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
يَفْقَهُوا۟ قَوْلِى
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:29}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And appoint for me a minister [i.e., assistant] from my family -

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Appoint for me a henchman from my folk,

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَٱجْعَل لِّى وَزِيرًا مِّنْ أَهْلِى
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:30}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Aaron, my brother.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Aaron, my brother.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
هَـٰرُونَ أَخِى
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:31}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Increase through him my strength

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Confirm my strength with him

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
ٱشْدُدْ بِهِٓ أَزْرِى
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:32}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And let him share my task

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And let him share my task,

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَأَشْرِكْهُ فِىٓ أَمْرِى
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:33}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: That we may exalt You much

\textit{M. Pickthall}: That we may glorify Thee much

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
كَىْ نُسَبِّحَكَ كَثِيرًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:34}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And remember You much.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And much remember Thee.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَنَذْكُرَكَ كَثِيرًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:35}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Indeed, You are of us ever Seeing."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Lo! Thou art ever Seeing us.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
إِنَّكَ كُنتَ بِنَا بَصِيرًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:36}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: [Allāh] said, "You have been granted your request, O Moses.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: He said: Thou art granted thy request, O Moses.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَ قَدْ أُوتِيتَ سُؤْلَكَ يَـٰمُوسَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:37}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And We had already conferred favor upon you another time,

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And indeed, another time, already We have shown thee favour,

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَلَقَدْ مَنَنَّا عَلَيْكَ مَرَّةً أُخْرَىٰٓ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:38}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: When We inspired to your mother what We inspired,

\textit{M. Pickthall}: When we inspired in thy mother that which is inspired,

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
إِذْ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّكَ مَا يُوحَىٰٓ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:39}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: [Saying], 'Cast him into the chest and cast it into the river, and the river will throw it onto the bank; there will take him an enemy to Me and an enemy to him.' And I bestowed upon you love from Me that you would be brought up under My eye [i.e., observation and care].

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Saying: Throw him into the ark, and throw it into the river, then the river shall throw it on to the bank, and there an enemy to Me and an enemy to him shall take him. And I endued thee with love from Me that thou mightest be trained according to My will,

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
أَنِ ٱقْذِفِيهِ فِى ٱلتَّابُوتِ فَٱقْذِفِيهِ فِى ٱلْيَمِّ فَلْيُلْقِهِ ٱلْيَمُّ بِٱلسَّاحِلِ يَأْخُذْهُ عَدُوٌّ لِّى وَعَدُوٌّ لَّهُ  وَأَلْقَيْتُ عَلَيْكَ مَحَبَّةً مِّنِّى وَلِتُصْنَعَ عَلَىٰ عَيْنِىٓ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:40}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: [And We favored you] when your sister went and said, 'Shall I direct you to someone who will be responsible for him?' So We restored you to your mother that she might be content and not grieve. And you killed someone, but We saved you from retaliation and tried you with a [severe] trial. And you remained [some] years among the people of Madyan. Then you came [here] at the decreed time, O Moses.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: When thy sister went and said: Shall I show you one who will nurse him? and we restored thee to thy mother that her eyes might be refreshed and might not sorrow. And thou didst kill a man and We delivered thee from great distress, and tried thee with a heavy trial. And thou didst tarry years among the folk of Midian. Then camest thou (hither) by (My) providence, O Moses,

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
إِذْ تَمْشِىٓ أُخْتُكَ فَتَقُولُ هَلْ أَدُلُّكُمْ عَلَىٰ مَن يَكْفُلُهُ  فَرَجَعْنَـٰكَ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّكَ كَىْ تَقَرَّ عَيْنُهَا وَلَا تَحْزَنَ  وَقَتَلْتَ نَفْسًا فَنَجَّيْنَـٰكَ مِنَ ٱلْغَمِّ وَفَتَنَّـٰكَ فُتُونًا  فَلَبِثْتَ سِنِينَ فِىٓ أَهْلِ مَدْيَنَ ثُمَّ جِئْتَ عَلَىٰ قَدَرٍ يَـٰمُوسَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:41}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And I produced you for Myself.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And I have attached thee to Myself.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَٱصْطَنَعْتُكَ لِنَفْسِى
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:42}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Go, you and your brother, with My signs and do not slacken in My remembrance.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Go, thou and thy brother, with My tokens, and be not faint in remembrance of Me.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
ٱذْهَبْ أَنتَ وَأَخُوكَ بِـَٔايَـٰتِى وَلَا تَنِيَا فِى ذِكْرِى
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:43}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Go, both of you, to Pharaoh. Indeed, he has transgressed.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Go, both of you, unto Pharaoh. Lo! he hath transgressed (the bounds).

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
ٱذْهَبَآ إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّهُ طَغَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:44}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And speak to him with gentle speech that perhaps he may be reminded or fear [Allāh]."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And speak unto him a gentle word, that peradventure he may heed or fear.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَقُولَا لَهُ قَوْلًا لَّيِّنًا لَّعَلَّهُ يَتَذَكَّرُ أَوْ يَخْشَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:45}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: They said, "Our Lord, indeed we are afraid that he will hasten [punishment] against us or that he will transgress."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: They said: Our Lord! Lo! we fear that he may be beforehand with us or that he may play the tyrant.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَا رَبَّنَآ إِنَّنَا نَخَافُ أَن يَفْرُطَ عَلَيْنَآ أَوْ أَن يَطْغَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:46}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: [Allāh] said, "Fear not. Indeed, I am with you both; I hear and I see.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: He said: Fear not. Lo! I am with you twain, Hearing and Seeing.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَ لَا تَخَافَآ  إِنَّنِى مَعَكُمَآ أَسْمَعُ وَأَرَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:47}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: So go to him and say, 'Indeed, we are messengers of your Lord, so send with us the Children of Israel and do not torment them. We have come to you with a sign from your Lord. And peace will be upon he who follows the guidance.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: So go ye unto him and say: Lo! we are two messengers of thy Lord. So let the children of Israel go with us, and torment them not. We bring thee a token from thy Lord. And peace will be for him who followeth right guidance.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَأْتِيَاهُ فَقُولَآ إِنَّا رَسُولَا رَبِّكَ فَأَرْسِلْ مَعَنَا بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ وَلَا تُعَذِّبْهُمْ  قَدْ جِئْنَـٰكَ بِـَٔايَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّكَ  وَٱلسَّلَـٰمُ عَلَىٰ مَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ ٱلْهُدَىٰٓ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:48}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Indeed, it has been revealed to us that the punishment will be upon whoever denies and turns away.'"

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Lo! it hath been revealed unto us that the doom will be for him who denieth and turneth away.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
إِنَّا قَدْ أُوحِىَ إِلَيْنَآ أَنَّ ٱلْعَذَابَ عَلَىٰ مَن كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:49}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: [Pharaoh] said, "So who is the Lord of you two, O Moses?"

\textit{M. Pickthall}: (Pharaoh) said: Who then is the Lord of you twain, O Moses?

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَ فَمَن رَّبُّكُمَا يَـٰمُوسَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:50}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: He said, "Our Lord is He who gave each thing its form and then guided [it]."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: He said: Our Lord is He Who gave unto everything its nature, then guided it aright.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَ رَبُّنَا ٱلَّذِىٓ أَعْطَىٰ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ خَلْقَهُ ثُمَّ هَدَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:51}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: [Pharaoh] said, "Then what is the case of the former generations?"

\textit{M. Pickthall}: He said: What then is the state of the generations of old?

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَ فَمَا بَالُ ٱلْقُرُونِ ٱلْأُولَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:52}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: [Moses] said, "The knowledge thereof is with my Lord in a record. My Lord neither errs nor forgets."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: He said: The knowledge thereof is with my Lord in a Record. My Lord neither erreth nor forgetteth,

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَ عِلْمُهَا عِندَ رَبِّى فِى كِتَـٰبٍ  لَّا يَضِلُّ رَبِّى وَلَا يَنسَى
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:53}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: [It is He] who has made for you the earth as a bed [spread out] and inserted therein for you roadways and sent down from the sky, rain and produced thereby categories of various plants.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Who hath appointed the earth as a bed and hath threaded roads for you therein and hath sent down water from the sky and thereby We have brought forth divers kinds of vegetation,

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
ٱلَّذِى جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلْأَرْضَ مَهْدًا وَسَلَكَ لَكُمْ فِيهَا سُبُلًا وَأَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءً فَأَخْرَجْنَا بِهِٓ أَزْوَٰجًا مِّن نَّبَاتٍ شَتَّىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:54}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Eat [therefrom] and pasture your livestock. Indeed in that are signs for those of intelligence.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: (Saying): Eat ye and feed your cattle. Lo! herein verily are portents for men of thought.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
كُلُوا۟ وَٱرْعَوْا۟ أَنْعَـٰمَكُمْ  إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَـَٔايَـٰتٍ لِّأُو۟لِى ٱلنُّهَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:55}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: From it [i.e., the earth] We created you, and into it We will return you, and from it We will extract you another time.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Thereof We created you, and thereunto We return you, and thence We bring you forth a second time.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
۞ مِنْهَا خَلَقْنَـٰكُمْ وَفِيهَا نُعِيدُكُمْ وَمِنْهَا نُخْرِجُكُمْ تَارَةً أُخْرَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:56}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And We certainly showed him [i.e., Pharaoh] Our signs - all of them - but he denied and refused.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And We verily did show him all Our tokens, but he denied them and refused.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَلَقَدْ أَرَيْنَـٰهُ ءَايَـٰتِنَا كُلَّهَا فَكَذَّبَ وَأَبَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:57}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: He said, "Have you come to us to drive us out of our land with your magic, O Moses?

\textit{M. Pickthall}: He said: Hast come to drive us out from our land by thy magic, O Moses?

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَ أَجِئْتَنَا لِتُخْرِجَنَا مِنْ أَرْضِنَا بِسِحْرِكَ يَـٰمُوسَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:58}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Then we will surely bring you magic like it, so make between us and you an appointment, which we will not fail to keep and neither will you, in a place assigned."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: But we surely can produce for thee magic the like thereof; so appoint a tryst between us and you, which neither we nor thou shall fail to keep, at a place convenient (to us both).

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَلَنَأْتِيَنَّكَ بِسِحْرٍ مِّثْلِهِ فَٱجْعَلْ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَكَ مَوْعِدًا لَّا نُخْلِفُهُ نَحْنُ وَلَآ أَنتَ مَكَانًا سُوًى
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:59}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: [Moses] said, "Your appointment is on the day of the festival when the people assemble at mid-morning."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: (Moses) said: Your tryst shall be the day of the feast, and let the people assemble when the sun hath risen high.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَ مَوْعِدُكُمْ يَوْمُ ٱلزِّينَةِ وَأَن يُحْشَرَ ٱلنَّاسُ ضُحًى
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:60}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: So Pharaoh went away, put together his plan, and then came [to Moses].

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Then Pharaoh went and gathered his strength, then came (to the appointed tryst).

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَتَوَلَّىٰ فِرْعَوْنُ فَجَمَعَ كَيْدَهُ ثُمَّ أَتَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:61}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Moses said to them [i.e., the magicians summoned by Pharaoh], "Woe to you! Do not invent a lie against Allāh or He will exterminate you with a punishment; and he has failed who invents [such falsehood]."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Moses said unto them: Woe unto you! Invent not a lie against Allah, lest He extirpate you by some punishment. He who lieth faileth miserably.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَ لَهُم مُّوسَىٰ وَيْلَكُمْ لَا تَفْتَرُوا۟ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِبًا فَيُسْحِتَكُم بِعَذَابٍ  وَقَدْ خَابَ مَنِ ٱفْتَرَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:62}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: So they disputed over their affair among themselves and concealed their private conversation.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Then they debated one with another what they must do, and they kept their counsel secret.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَتَنَـٰزَعُوٓا۟ أَمْرَهُم بَيْنَهُمْ وَأَسَرُّوا۟ ٱلنَّجْوَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:63}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: They said, "Indeed, these are two magicians who want to drive you out of your land with their magic and do away with your most exemplary way [i.e., religion or tradition].

\textit{M. Pickthall}: They said: Lo! these are two wizards who would drive you out from your country by their magic, and destroy your best traditions;

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالُوٓا۟ إِنْ هَـٰذَٰنِ لَسَـٰحِرَٰنِ يُرِيدَانِ أَن يُخْرِجَاكُم مِّنْ أَرْضِكُم بِسِحْرِهِمَا وَيَذْهَبَا بِطَرِيقَتِكُمُ ٱلْمُثْلَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:64}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: So resolve upon your plan and then come [forward] in line. And he has succeeded today who overcomes."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: So arrange your plan, and come in battle line. Whoso is uppermost this day will be indeed successful.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَأَجْمِعُوا۟ كَيْدَكُمْ ثُمَّ ٱئْتُوا۟ صَفًّا  وَقَدْ أَفْلَحَ ٱلْيَوْمَ مَنِ ٱسْتَعْلَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:65}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: They said, "O Moses, either you throw or we will be the first to throw."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: They said: O Moses! Either throw first, or let us be the first to throw?

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالُوا۟ يَـٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِمَّآ أَن تُلْقِىَ وَإِمَّآ أَن نَّكُونَ أَوَّلَ مَنْ أَلْقَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:66}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: He said, "Rather, you throw." And suddenly their ropes and staffs seemed to him from their magic that they were moving [like snakes].

\textit{M. Pickthall}: He said: Nay, do ye throw! Then lo! their cords and their staves, by their magic, appeared to him as though they ran.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَ بَلْ أَلْقُوا۟  فَإِذَا حِبَالُهُمْ وَعِصِيُّهُمْ يُخَيَّلُ إِلَيْهِ مِن سِحْرِهِمْ أَنَّهَا تَسْعَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:67}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And he sensed within himself apprehension, did Moses.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And Moses conceived a fear in his mind.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَأَوْجَسَ فِى نَفْسِهِ خِيفَةً مُّوسَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:68}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: We [i.e., Allāh] said, "Fear not. Indeed, it is you who are superior.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: We said: Fear not! Lo! thou art the higher.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قُلْنَا لَا تَخَفْ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:69}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And throw what is in your right hand; it will swallow up what they have crafted. What they have crafted is but the trick of a magician, and the magician will not succeed wherever he is."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Throw that which is in thy right hand! It will eat up that which they have made. Lo! that which they have made is but a wizard's artifice, and a wizard shall not be successful to whatever point (of skill) he may attain.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَأَلْقِ مَا فِى يَمِينِكَ تَلْقَفْ مَا صَنَعُوٓا۟  إِنَّمَا صَنَعُوا۟ كَيْدُ سَـٰحِرٍ  وَلَا يُفْلِحُ ٱلسَّاحِرُ حَيْثُ أَتَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:70}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: So the magicians fell down in prostration. They said, "We have believed in the Lord of Aaron and Moses."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Then the wizards were (all) flung down prostrate, crying: We believe in the Lord of Aaron and Moses.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَأُلْقِىَ ٱلسَّحَرَةُ سُجَّدًا قَالُوٓا۟ ءَامَنَّا بِرَبِّ هَـٰرُونَ وَمُوسَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:71}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: [Pharaoh] said, "You believed him [i.e., Moses] before I gave you permission. Indeed, he is your leader who has taught you magic. So I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides, and I will crucify you on the trunks of palm trees, and you will surely know which of us is more severe in [giving] punishment and more enduring."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: (Pharaoh) said: Ye put faith in him before I give you leave. Lo! he is your chief who taught you magic. Now surely I shall cut off your hands and your feet alternately, and I shall crucify you on the trunks of palm trees, and ye shall know for certain which of us hath sterner and more lasting punishment.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَ ءَامَنتُمْ لَهُ قَبْلَ أَنْ ءَاذَنَ لَكُمْ  إِنَّهُ لَكَبِيرُكُمُ ٱلَّذِى عَلَّمَكُمُ ٱلسِّحْرَ  فَلَأُقَطِّعَنَّ أَيْدِيَكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُم مِّنْ خِلَـٰفٍ وَلَأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمْ فِى جُذُوعِ ٱلنَّخْلِ وَلَتَعْلَمُنَّ أَيُّنَآ أَشَدُّ عَذَابًا وَأَبْقَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:72}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: They said, "Never will we prefer you over what has come to us of clear proofs and [over] He who created us. So decree whatever you are to decree. You can only decree for this worldly life.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: They said: We choose thee not above the clear proofs that have come unto us, and above Him Who created us. So decree what thou wilt decree. Thou wilt end for us only this life of the world.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالُوا۟ لَن نُّؤْثِرَكَ عَلَىٰ مَا جَآءَنَا مِنَ ٱلْبَيِّنَـٰتِ وَٱلَّذِى فَطَرَنَا  فَٱقْضِ مَآ أَنتَ قَاضٍ  إِنَّمَا تَقْضِى هَـٰذِهِ ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَآ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:73}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Indeed, we have believed in our Lord that He may forgive us our sins and what you compelled us [to do] of magic. And Allāh is better and more enduring."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Lo! we believe in our Lord, that He may forgive us our sins and the magic unto which thou didst force us. Allah is better and more lasting.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
إِنَّآ ءَامَنَّا بِرَبِّنَا لِيَغْفِرَ لَنَا خَطَـٰيَـٰنَا وَمَآ أَكْرَهْتَنَا عَلَيْهِ مِنَ ٱلسِّحْرِ  وَٱللَّهُ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰٓ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:74}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Indeed, whoever comes to his Lord as a criminal - indeed, for him is Hell; he will neither die therein nor live.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Lo! whoso cometh guilty unto his Lord, verily for him is hell. There he will neither die nor live.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
إِنَّهُ مَن يَأْتِ رَبَّهُ مُجْرِمًا فَإِنَّ لَهُ جَهَنَّمَ لَا يَمُوتُ فِيهَا وَلَا يَحْيَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:75}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: But whoever comes to Him as a believer having done righteous deeds - for those will be the highest degrees [in position]:

\textit{M. Pickthall}: But whoso cometh unto Him a believer, having done good works, for such are the high stations;

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَمَن يَأْتِهِ مُؤْمِنًا قَدْ عَمِلَ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتِ فَأُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ لَهُمُ ٱلدَّرَجَـٰتُ ٱلْعُلَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:76}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Gardens of perpetual residence beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally. And that is the reward of one who purifies himself.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Gardens of Eden underneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide for ever. That is the reward of him who groweth.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
جَنَّـٰتُ عَدْنٍ تَجْرِى مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلْأَنْهَـٰرُ خَـٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا  وَذَٰلِكَ جَزَآءُ مَن تَزَكَّىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:77}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And We had inspired to Moses, "Travel by night with My servants and strike for them a dry path through the sea; you will not fear being overtaken [by Pharaoh] nor be afraid [of drowning]."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And verily We inspired Moses, saying: Take away My slaves by night and strike for them a dry path in the sea, fearing not to be overtaken, neither being afraid (of the sea).

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَلَقَدْ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنْ أَسْرِ بِعِبَادِى فَٱضْرِبْ لَهُمْ طَرِيقًا فِى ٱلْبَحْرِ يَبَسًا لَّا تَخَـٰفُ دَرَكًا وَلَا تَخْشَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:78}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: So Pharaoh pursued them with his soldiers, and there covered them from the sea that which covered them,

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Then Pharaoh followed them with his hosts and there covered them that which did cover them of the sea.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَأَتْبَعَهُمْ فِرْعَوْنُ بِجُنُودِهِ فَغَشِيَهُم مِّنَ ٱلْيَمِّ مَا غَشِيَهُمْ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:79}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And Pharaoh led his people astray and did not guide [them].

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And Pharaoh led his folk astray, he did not guide them.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَأَضَلَّ فِرْعَوْنُ قَوْمَهُ وَمَا هَدَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:80}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: O Children of Israel, We delivered you from your enemy, and We made an appointment with you at the right side of the mount, and We sent down to you manna and quails,

\textit{M. Pickthall}: O Children of Israel! We delivered you from your enemy, and we made a covenant with you on the holy mountain's side, and sent down on you the manna and the quails,

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
يَـٰبَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ قَدْ أَنجَيْنَـٰكُم مِّنْ عَدُوِّكُمْ وَوَٰعَدْنَـٰكُمْ جَانِبَ ٱلطُّورِ ٱلْأَيْمَنَ وَنَزَّلْنَا عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْمَنَّ وَٱلسَّلْوَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:81}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: [Saying], "Eat from the good things with which We have provided you and do not transgress [or oppress others] therein, lest My anger should descend upon you. And he upon whom My anger descends has certainly fallen [i.e., perished]."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: (Saying): Eat of the good things wherewith We have provided you, and transgress not in respect thereof lest My wrath come upon you: and he on whom My wrath cometh, he is lost indeed.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
كُلُوا۟ مِن طَيِّبَـٰتِ مَا رَزَقْنَـٰكُمْ وَلَا تَطْغَوْا۟ فِيهِ فَيَحِلَّ عَلَيْكُمْ غَضَبِى  وَمَن يَحْلِلْ عَلَيْهِ غَضَبِى فَقَدْ هَوَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:82}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: But indeed, I am the Perpetual Forgiver of whoever repents and believes and does righteousness and then continues in guidance.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And lo! verily I am Forgiving toward him who repenteth and believeth and doeth good, and afterward walketh aright.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَإِنِّى لَغَفَّارٌ لِّمَن تَابَ وَءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَـٰلِحًا ثُمَّ ٱهْتَدَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:83}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: [Allāh said], "And what made you hasten from your people, O Moses?"

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And (it was said): What hath made thee hasten from thy folk, O Moses?

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
۞ وَمَآ أَعْجَلَكَ عَن قَوْمِكَ يَـٰمُوسَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:84}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: He said, "They are close upon my tracks, and I hastened to You, my Lord, that You be pleased."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: He said: They are close upon my track. I hastened unto Thee, my Lord, that Thou mightest be well pleased.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَ هُمْ أُو۟لَآءِ عَلَىٰٓ أَثَرِى وَعَجِلْتُ إِلَيْكَ رَبِّ لِتَرْضَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:85}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: [Allāh] said, "But indeed, We have tried your people after you [departed], and the Sāmirī has led them astray."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: He said: Lo! We have tried thy folk in thine absence, and As-Samiri hath misled them.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَ فَإِنَّا قَدْ فَتَنَّا قَوْمَكَ مِن بَعْدِكَ وَأَضَلَّهُمُ ٱلسَّامِرِىُّ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:86}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: So Moses returned to his people, angry and grieved. He said, "O my people, did your Lord not make you a good promise? Then, was the time [of its fulfillment] too long for you, or did you wish that wrath from your Lord descend upon you, so you broke your promise [of obedience] to me?"

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Then Moses went back unto his folk, angry and sad. He said: O my people! Hath not your Lord promised you a fair promise? Did the time appointed then appear too long for you, or did ye wish that wrath from your Lord should come upon you, that ye broke tryst with me?

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَرَجَعَ مُوسَىٰٓ إِلَىٰ قَوْمِهِ غَضْبَـٰنَ أَسِفًا  قَالَ يَـٰقَوْمِ أَلَمْ يَعِدْكُمْ رَبُّكُمْ وَعْدًا حَسَنًا  أَفَطَالَ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْعَهْدُ أَمْ أَرَدتُّمْ أَن يَحِلَّ عَلَيْكُمْ غَضَبٌ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ فَأَخْلَفْتُم مَّوْعِدِى
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:87}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: They said, "We did not break our promise to you by our will, but we were made to carry burdens from the ornaments of the people [of Pharaoh], so we threw them [into the fire], and thus did the Sāmirī throw."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: They said: We broke not tryst with thee of our own will, but we were laden with burdens of ornaments of the folk, then cast them (in the fire), for thus As-Samiri proposed.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالُوا۟ مَآ أَخْلَفْنَا مَوْعِدَكَ بِمَلْكِنَا وَلَـٰكِنَّا حُمِّلْنَآ أَوْزَارًا مِّن زِينَةِ ٱلْقَوْمِ فَقَذَفْنَـٰهَا فَكَذَٰلِكَ أَلْقَى ٱلسَّامِرِىُّ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:88}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And he extracted for them [the statue of] a calf which had a lowing sound, and they said, "This is your god and the god of Moses, but he forgot."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Then he produced for them a calf, of saffron hue, which gave forth a lowing sound. And they cried: This is your god and the god of Moses, but he hath forgotten.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَأَخْرَجَ لَهُمْ عِجْلًا جَسَدًا لَّهُ خُوَارٌ فَقَالُوا۟ هَـٰذَآ إِلَـٰهُكُمْ وَإِلَـٰهُ مُوسَىٰ فَنَسِىَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:89}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Did they not see that it could not return to them any speech [i.e., response] and that it did not possess for them any harm or benefit?

\textit{M. Pickthall}: See they not, then, that it returneth no saying unto them and possesseth for them neither hurt nor use?

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
أَفَلَا يَرَوْنَ أَلَّا يَرْجِعُ إِلَيْهِمْ قَوْلًا وَلَا يَمْلِكُ لَهُمْ ضَرًّا وَلَا نَفْعًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:90}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And Aaron had already told them before [the return of Moses], "O my people, you are only being tested by it, and indeed, your Lord is the Most Merciful, so follow me and obey my order."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And Aaron indeed had told them beforehand: O my people! Ye are but being seduced therewith, for lo! your Lord is the Beneficent, so follow me and obey my order.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَلَقَدْ قَالَ لَهُمْ هَـٰرُونُ مِن قَبْلُ يَـٰقَوْمِ إِنَّمَا فُتِنتُم بِهِ  وَإِنَّ رَبَّكُمُ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنُ فَٱتَّبِعُونِى وَأَطِيعُوٓا۟ أَمْرِى
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:91}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: They said, "We will never cease being devoted to it [i.e., the calf] until Moses returns to us."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: They said: We shall by no means cease to be its votaries till Moses return unto us.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالُوا۟ لَن نَّبْرَحَ عَلَيْهِ عَـٰكِفِينَ حَتَّىٰ يَرْجِعَ إِلَيْنَا مُوسَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:92}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: [Moses] said, "O Aaron, what prevented you, when you saw them going astray,

\textit{M. Pickthall}: He (Moses) said: O Aaron! What held thee back when thou didst see them gone astray,

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَ يَـٰهَـٰرُونُ مَا مَنَعَكَ إِذْ رَأَيْتَهُمْ ضَلُّوٓا۟
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:93}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: From following me? Then have you disobeyed my order?"

\textit{M. Pickthall}: That thou followedst me not? Hast thou then disobeyed my order?

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
أَلَّا تَتَّبِعَنِ  أَفَعَصَيْتَ أَمْرِى
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:94}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: [Aaron] said, "O son of my mother, do not seize [me] by my beard or by my head. Indeed, I feared that you would say, 'You caused division among the Children of Israel, and you did not observe [or await] my word.'"

\textit{M. Pickthall}: He said: O son of my mother! Clutch not my beard nor my head! I feared lest thou shouldst say: Thou hast caused division among the Children of Israel, and hast not waited for my word.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَ يَبْنَؤُمَّ لَا تَأْخُذْ بِلِحْيَتِى وَلَا بِرَأْسِىٓ  إِنِّى خَشِيتُ أَن تَقُولَ فَرَّقْتَ بَيْنَ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ وَلَمْ تَرْقُبْ قَوْلِى
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:95}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: [Moses] said, "And what is your case, O Sāmirī?"

\textit{M. Pickthall}: (Moses) said: And what hast thou to say, O Samiri?

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَ فَمَا خَطْبُكَ يَـٰسَـٰمِرِىُّ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:96}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: He said, "I saw what they did not see, so I took a handful [of dust] from the track of the messenger and threw it, and thus did my soul entice me."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: He said: I perceived what they perceive not, so I seized a handful from the footsteps of the messenger, and then threw it in. Thus my soul commended to me.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَ بَصُرْتُ بِمَا لَمْ يَبْصُرُوا۟ بِهِ فَقَبَضْتُ قَبْضَةً مِّنْ أَثَرِ ٱلرَّسُولِ فَنَبَذْتُهَا وَكَذَٰلِكَ سَوَّلَتْ لِى نَفْسِى
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:97}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: [Moses] said, "Then go. And indeed, it is [decreed] for you in [this] life to say, 'No contact.' And indeed, you have an appointment [in the Hereafter] you will not fail to keep. And look at your 'god' to which you remained devoted. We will surely burn it and blow it [i.e., its ashes] into the sea with a blast.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: (Moses) said: Then go! and lo! in this life it is for thee to say: Touch me not! and lo! there is for thee a tryst thou canst not break. Now look upon thy god of which thou hast remained a votary. Verily we will burn it and will scatter its dust over the sea.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَ فَٱذْهَبْ فَإِنَّ لَكَ فِى ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ أَن تَقُولَ لَا مِسَاسَ  وَإِنَّ لَكَ مَوْعِدًا لَّن تُخْلَفَهُ  وَٱنظُرْ إِلَىٰٓ إِلَـٰهِكَ ٱلَّذِى ظَلْتَ عَلَيْهِ عَاكِفًا  لَّنُحَرِّقَنَّهُ ثُمَّ لَنَنسِفَنَّهُ فِى ٱلْيَمِّ نَسْفًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:98}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Your god is only Allāh, except for whom there is no deity. He has encompassed all things in knowledge."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Your Allah is only Allah, than Whom there is no other Allah. He embraceth all things in His knowledge.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
إِنَّمَآ إِلَـٰهُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِى لَآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ  وَسِعَ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ عِلْمًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:99}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Thus, [O Muḥammad], We relate to you from the news of what has preceded. And We have certainly given you from Us a message [i.e., the Qur’ān].

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Thus relate We unto thee (Muhammad) some tidings of that which happened of old, and We have given thee from Our presence a reminder.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
كَذَٰلِكَ نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ مِنْ أَنبَآءِ مَا قَدْ سَبَقَ  وَقَدْ ءَاتَيْنَـٰكَ مِن لَّدُنَّا ذِكْرًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:100}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Whoever turns away from it - then indeed, he will bear on the Day of Resurrection a burden [i.e., great sin],

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Whoso turneth away from it, he verily will bear a burden on the Day of Resurrection,

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
مَّنْ أَعْرَضَ عَنْهُ فَإِنَّهُ يَحْمِلُ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَـٰمَةِ وِزْرًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:101}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: [Abiding] eternally therein, and evil it is for them on the Day of Resurrection as a load -

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Abiding under it - an evil burden for them on the Day of Resurrection,

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
خَـٰلِدِينَ فِيهِ  وَسَآءَ لَهُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَـٰمَةِ حِمْلًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:102}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: The Day the Horn will be blown. And We will gather the criminals, that Day, blue-eyed.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: The day when the Trumpet is blown. On that day we assemble the guilty white-eyed (with terror),

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
يَوْمَ يُنفَخُ فِى ٱلصُّورِ  وَنَحْشُرُ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ يَوْمَئِذٍ زُرْقًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:103}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: They will murmur among themselves, "You remained not but ten [days in the world]."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Murmuring among themselves: Ye have tarried but ten (days).

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
يَتَخَـٰفَتُونَ بَيْنَهُمْ إِن لَّبِثْتُمْ إِلَّا عَشْرًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:104}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: We are most knowing of what they say when the best of them in manner [i.e., wisdom or speech] will say, "You remained not but one day."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: We are Best Aware of what they utter when their best in conduct say: Ye have tarried but a day.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
نَّحْنُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا يَقُولُونَ إِذْ يَقُولُ أَمْثَلُهُمْ طَرِيقَةً إِن لَّبِثْتُمْ إِلَّا يَوْمًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:105}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And they ask you about the mountains, so say, "My Lord will blow them away with a blast.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: They will ask thee of the mountains (on that day). Say: My Lord will break them into scattered dust.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَيَسْـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلْجِبَالِ فَقُلْ يَنسِفُهَا رَبِّى نَسْفًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:106}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And He will leave it [i.e., the earth] a level plain;

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And leave it as an empty plain,

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَيَذَرُهَا قَاعًا صَفْصَفًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:107}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: You will not see therein a depression or an elevation."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Wherein thou seest neither curve nor ruggedness.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
لَّا تَرَىٰ فِيهَا عِوَجًا وَلَآ أَمْتًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:108}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: That Day, they [i.e., everyone] will follow [the call of] the Caller [with] no deviation therefrom, and [all] voices will be stilled before the Most Merciful, so you will not hear except a whisper [of footsteps].

\textit{M. Pickthall}: On that day they follow the summoner who deceiveth not, and voices are hushed for the Beneficent, and thou hearest but a faint murmur.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
يَوْمَئِذٍ يَتَّبِعُونَ ٱلدَّاعِىَ لَا عِوَجَ لَهُ  وَخَشَعَتِ ٱلْأَصْوَاتُ لِلرَّحْمَـٰنِ فَلَا تَسْمَعُ إِلَّا هَمْسًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:109}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: That Day, no intercession will benefit except [that of] one to whom the Most Merciful has given permission and has accepted his word.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: On that day no intercession availeth save (that of) him unto whom the Beneficent hath given leave and whose word He accepteth.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
يَوْمَئِذٍ لَّا تَنفَعُ ٱلشَّفَـٰعَةُ إِلَّا مَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنُ وَرَضِىَ لَهُ قَوْلًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:110}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: He [i.e., Allāh] knows what is [presently] before them and what will be after them, but they do not encompass it [i.e., what He knows] in knowledge.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: He knoweth (all) that is before them and (all) that is behind them, while they cannot compass it in knowledge.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِهِ عِلْمًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:111}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And [all] faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining. And he will have failed who carries injustice.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And faces humble themselves before the Living, the Eternal. And he who beareth (a burden of) wrongdoing is indeed a failure (on that day).

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
۞ وَعَنَتِ ٱلْوُجُوهُ لِلْحَىِّ ٱلْقَيُّومِ  وَقَدْ خَابَ مَنْ حَمَلَ ظُلْمًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:112}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: But he who does of righteous deeds while he is a believer - he will neither fear injustice nor deprivation.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And he who hath done some good works, being a believer, he feareth not injustice nor begrudging (of his wage).

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِنَ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتِ وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ فَلَا يَخَافُ ظُلْمًا وَلَا هَضْمًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:113}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And thus We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur’ān and have diversified therein the warnings that perhaps they will avoid [sin] or it would cause them remembrance.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Thus we have revealed it as a Lecture in Arabic, and have displayed therein certain threats, that peradventure they may keep from evil or that it may cause them to take heed.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَكَذَٰلِكَ أَنزَلْنَـٰهُ قُرْءَانًا عَرَبِيًّا وَصَرَّفْنَا فِيهِ مِنَ ٱلْوَعِيدِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَّقُونَ أَوْ يُحْدِثُ لَهُمْ ذِكْرًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:114}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: So high [above all] is Allāh, the Sovereign, the Truth. And, [O Muḥammad], do not hasten with [recitation of] the Qur’ān before its revelation is completed to you, and say, "My Lord, increase me in knowledge."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Then exalted be Allah, the True King! And hasten not (O Muhammad) with the Qur'an ere its revelation hath been perfected unto thee, and say: My Lord! Increase me in knowledge.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَتَعَـٰلَى ٱللَّهُ ٱلْمَلِكُ ٱلْحَقُّ  وَلَا تَعْجَلْ بِٱلْقُرْءَانِ مِن قَبْلِ أَن يُقْضَىٰٓ إِلَيْكَ وَحْيُهُ  وَقُل رَّبِّ زِدْنِى عِلْمًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:115}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And We had already taken a promise from Adam before, but he forgot; and We found not in him determination.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And verily We made a covenant of old with Adam, but he forgot, and We found no constancy in him.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَلَقَدْ عَهِدْنَآ إِلَىٰٓ ءَادَمَ مِن قَبْلُ فَنَسِىَ وَلَمْ نَجِدْ لَهُ عَزْمًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:116}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And [mention] when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," and they prostrated, except Iblees; he refused.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And when We said unto the angels: Fall prostrate before Adam, they fell prostrate (all) save Iblis; he refused.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَإِذْ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَـٰٓئِكَةِ ٱسْجُدُوا۟ لِـَٔادَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ إِبْلِيسَ أَبَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:117}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: So We said, "O Adam, indeed this is an enemy to you and to your wife. Then let him not remove you from Paradise so you would suffer.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Therefor we said: O Adam! This is an enemy unto thee and unto thy wife, so let him not drive you both out of the Garden so that thou come to toil.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَقُلْنَا يَـٰٓـَٔادَمُ إِنَّ هَـٰذَا عَدُوٌّ لَّكَ وَلِزَوْجِكَ فَلَا يُخْرِجَنَّكُمَا مِنَ ٱلْجَنَّةِ فَتَشْقَىٰٓ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:118}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Indeed, it is [promised] for you not to be hungry therein or be unclothed.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: It is (vouchsafed) unto thee that thou hungerest not therein nor art naked,

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
إِنَّ لَكَ أَلَّا تَجُوعَ فِيهَا وَلَا تَعْرَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:119}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And indeed, you will not be thirsty therein or be hot from the sun."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And that thou thirstest not therein nor art exposed to the sun's heat.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَأَنَّكَ لَا تَظْمَؤُا۟ فِيهَا وَلَا تَضْحَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:120}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Then Satan whispered to him; he said, "O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and possession that will not deteriorate?"

\textit{M. Pickthall}: But the devil whispered to him, saying: O Adam! Shall I show thee the tree of immortality and power that wasteth not away?

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَوَسْوَسَ إِلَيْهِ ٱلشَّيْطَـٰنُ قَالَ يَـٰٓـَٔادَمُ هَلْ أَدُلُّكَ عَلَىٰ شَجَرَةِ ٱلْخُلْدِ وَمُلْكٍ لَّا يَبْلَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:121}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And they [i.e., Adam and his wife] ate of it, and their private parts became apparent to them, and they began to fasten over themselves from the leaves of Paradise. And Adam disobeyed his Lord and erred.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Then they twain ate thereof, so that their shame became apparent unto them, and they began to hide by heaping on themselves some of the leaves of the Garden. And Adam disobeyed his Lord, so went astray.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَأَكَلَا مِنْهَا فَبَدَتْ لَهُمَا سَوْءَٰتُهُمَا وَطَفِقَا يَخْصِفَانِ عَلَيْهِمَا مِن وَرَقِ ٱلْجَنَّةِ  وَعَصَىٰٓ ءَادَمُ رَبَّهُ فَغَوَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:122}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Then his Lord chose him and turned to him in forgiveness and guided [him].

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Then his Lord chose him, and relented toward him, and guided him.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
ثُمَّ ٱجْتَبَـٰهُ رَبُّهُ فَتَابَ عَلَيْهِ وَهَدَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:123}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: [Allāh] said, "Descend from it [i.e., Paradise] - all, [your descendants] being enemies to one another. And if there should come to you guidance from Me - then whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray [in the world] nor suffer [in the Hereafter].

\textit{M. Pickthall}: He said: Go down hence, both of you, one of you a foe unto the other. But when there come unto you from Me a guidance, then whoso followeth My guidance, he will not go astray nor come to grief.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَ ٱهْبِطَا مِنْهَا جَمِيعًا  بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ  فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُم مِّنِّى هُدًى فَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ هُدَاىَ فَلَا يَضِلُّ وَلَا يَشْقَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:124}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And whoever turns away from My remembrance - indeed, he will have a depressed [i.e., difficult] life, and We will gather [i.e., raise] him on the Day of Resurrection blind."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: But he who turneth away from remembrance of Me, his will be a narrow life, and I shall bring him blind to the assembly on the Day of Resurrection.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَمَنْ أَعْرَضَ عَن ذِكْرِى فَإِنَّ لَهُ مَعِيشَةً ضَنكًا وَنَحْشُرُهُ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَـٰمَةِ أَعْمَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:125}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: He will say, "My Lord, why have you raised me blind while I was [once] seeing?"

\textit{M. Pickthall}: He will say: My Lord! Wherefor hast Thou gathered me (hither) blind, when I was wont to see?

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَ رَبِّ لِمَ حَشَرْتَنِىٓ أَعْمَىٰ وَقَدْ كُنتُ بَصِيرًا
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:126}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: [Allāh] will say, "Thus did Our signs come to you, and you forgot [i.e., disregarded] them; and thus will you this Day be forgotten."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: He will say: So (it must be). Our revelations came unto thee but thou didst forget them. In like manner thou art forgotten this Day.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَ كَذَٰلِكَ أَتَتْكَ ءَايَـٰتُنَا فَنَسِيتَهَا  وَكَذَٰلِكَ ٱلْيَوْمَ تُنسَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:127}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And thus do We recompense he who transgressed and did not believe in the signs of his Lord. And the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe and more enduring.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Thus do We reward him who is prodigal and believeth not the revelations of his Lord; and verily the doom of the Hereafter will be sterner and more lasting.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَكَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى مَنْ أَسْرَفَ وَلَمْ يُؤْمِن بِـَٔايَـٰتِ رَبِّهِ  وَلَعَذَابُ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ أَشَدُّ وَأَبْقَىٰٓ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:128}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Then, has it not become clear to them how many generations We destroyed before them as they walk among their dwellings? Indeed in that are signs for those of intelligence.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Is it not a guidance for them (to know) how many a generation We destroyed before them, amid whose dwellings they walk? Lo! therein verily are signs for men of thought.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
أَفَلَمْ يَهْدِ لَهُمْ كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا قَبْلَهُم مِّنَ ٱلْقُرُونِ يَمْشُونَ فِى مَسَـٰكِنِهِمْ  إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَـَٔايَـٰتٍ لِّأُو۟لِى ٱلنُّهَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:129}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And if not for a word that preceded from your Lord, it [i.e., punishment] would have been an obligation [due immediately], and [if not for] a specified term [decreed].

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And but for a decree that had already gone forth from thy Lord, and a term already fixed, the judgment would have been inevitable (in this world).

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَلَوْلَا كَلِمَةٌ سَبَقَتْ مِن رَّبِّكَ لَكَانَ لِزَامًا وَأَجَلٌ مُّسَمًّى
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:130}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: So be patient over what they say and exalt [Allāh] with praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting; and during periods of the night [exalt Him] and at the ends of the day, that you may be satisfied.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Therefor (O Muhammad), bear with what they say, and celebrate the praise of thy Lord ere the rising of the sun and ere the going down thereof. And glorify Him some hours of the night and at the two ends of the day, that thou mayst find acceptance.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَٱصْبِرْ عَلَىٰ مَا يَقُولُونَ وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ ٱلشَّمْسِ وَقَبْلَ غُرُوبِهَا  وَمِنْ ءَانَآئِ ٱلَّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْ وَأَطْرَافَ ٱلنَّهَارِ لَعَلَّكَ تَرْضَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:131}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And do not extend your eyes toward that by which We have given enjoyment to [some] categories of them, [its being but] the splendor of worldly life by which We test them. And the provision of your Lord is better and more enduring.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And strain not thine eyes toward that which We cause some wedded pairs among them to enjoy, the flower of the life of the world, that We may try them thereby. The provision of thy Lord is better and more lasting.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَلَا تَمُدَّنَّ عَيْنَيْكَ إِلَىٰ مَا مَتَّعْنَا بِهِٓ أَزْوَٰجًا مِّنْهُمْ زَهْرَةَ ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا لِنَفْتِنَهُمْ فِيهِ  وَرِزْقُ رَبِّكَ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:132}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And enjoin prayer upon your family [and people] and be steadfast therein. We ask you not for provision; We provide for you, and the [best] outcome is for [those of] righteousness.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And enjoin upon thy people worship, and be constant therein. We ask not of thee a provision: We provided for thee. And the sequel is for righteousness.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَأْمُرْ أَهْلَكَ بِٱلصَّلَوٰةِ وَٱصْطَبِرْ عَلَيْهَا  لَا نَسْـَٔلُكَ رِزْقًا  نَّحْنُ نَرْزُقُكَ  وَٱلْعَـٰقِبَةُ لِلتَّقْوَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:133}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And they say, "Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?" Has there not come to them evidence of what was in the former scriptures?

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And they say: If only he would bring us a miracle from his Lord! Hath there not come unto them the proof of what is in the former scriptures?

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَقَالُوا۟ لَوْلَا يَأْتِينَا بِـَٔايَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّهِٓ  أَوَلَمْ تَأْتِهِم بَيِّنَةُ مَا فِى ٱلصُّحُفِ ٱلْأُولَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:134}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And if We had destroyed them with a punishment before him, they would have said, "Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger so we could have followed Your verses [i.e., teachings] before we were humiliated and disgraced?"

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And if we had destroyed them with some punishment before it, they would assuredly have said: Our Lord! If only Thou hadst sent unto us a messenger, so that we might have followed Thy revelations before we were (thus) humbled and disgraced!

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَلَوْ أَنَّآ أَهْلَكْنَـٰهُم بِعَذَابٍ مِّن قَبْلِهِ لَقَالُوا۟ رَبَّنَا لَوْلَآ أَرْسَلْتَ إِلَيْنَا رَسُولًا فَنَتَّبِعَ ءَايَـٰتِكَ مِن قَبْلِ أَن نَّذِلَّ وَنَخْزَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{20:135}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Say, "Each [of us] is waiting; so wait. For you will know who are the companions of the sound path and who is guided."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Say: Each is awaiting; so await ye! Ye will come to know who are the owners of the path of equity, and who is right.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قُلْ كُلٌّ مُّتَرَبِّصٌ فَتَرَبَّصُوا۟  فَسَتَعْلَمُونَ مَنْ أَصْحَـٰبُ ٱلصِّرَٰطِ ٱلسَّوِىِّ وَمَنِ ٱهْتَدَىٰ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}

\section{Surah 21, Al-'Anbyā (The Prophets)
All Verses (1 -- 112)}

The 73rd revealed Surah. Revealed in Makkah


\noindent[\textbf{21:1}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: [The time of] their account has approached for the people, while they are in heedlessness turning away.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Their reckoning draweth nigh for mankind, while they turn away in heedlessness.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
 ٱقْتَرَبَ لِلنَّاسِ حِسَابُهُمْ وَهُمْ فِى غَفْلَةٍ مُّعْرِضُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{21:2}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: No mention [i.e., revelation] comes to them anew from their Lord except that they listen to it while they are at play

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Never cometh there unto them a new reminder from their Lord but they listen to it while they play,

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
مَا يَأْتِيهِم مِّن ذِكْرٍ مِّن رَّبِّهِم مُّحْدَثٍ إِلَّا ٱسْتَمَعُوهُ وَهُمْ يَلْعَبُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{21:3}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: With their hearts distracted. And those who do wrong conceal their private conversation, [saying], "Is this [Prophet] except a human being like you? So would you approach magic while you are aware [of it]?"

\textit{M. Pickthall}: With hearts preoccupied. And they confer in secret. The wrong-doers say: Is this other than a mortal like you? Will ye then succumb to magic when ye see (it)?

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
لَاهِيَةً قُلُوبُهُمْ  وَأَسَرُّوا۟ ٱلنَّجْوَى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا۟ هَلْ هَـٰذَآ إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِّثْلُكُمْ  أَفَتَأْتُونَ ٱلسِّحْرَ وَأَنتُمْ تُبْصِرُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{21:4}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: He [the Prophet ((\ar{ﷺ}))] said, "My Lord knows whatever is said throughout the heaven and earth, and He is the Hearing, the Knowing."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: He saith: My Lord knoweth what is spoken in the heaven and the earth. He is the Hearer, the Knower.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالَ رَبِّى يَعْلَمُ ٱلْقَوْلَ فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ  وَهُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{21:5}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: But they say, "[The revelation is but] a mixture of false dreams; rather, he has invented it; rather, he is a poet. So let him bring us a sign just as the previous [messengers] were sent [with miracles]."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Nay, say they, (these are but) muddled dreams; nay, he hath but invented it; nay, he is but a poet. Let him bring us a portent even as those of old (who were Allah's messengers) were sent (with portents).

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
بَلْ قَالُوٓا۟ أَضْغَـٰثُ أَحْلَـٰمٍۭ بَلِ ٱفْتَرَىٰهُ بَلْ هُوَ شَاعِرٌ فَلْيَأْتِنَا بِـَٔايَةٍ كَمَآ أُرْسِلَ ٱلْأَوَّلُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{21:6}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Not a [single] city which We destroyed believed before them, so will they believe?

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Not a township believed of those which We destroyed before them (though We sent them portents): would they then believe?

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
مَآ ءَامَنَتْ قَبْلَهُم مِّن قَرْيَةٍ أَهْلَكْنَـٰهَآ  أَفَهُمْ يُؤْمِنُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{21:7}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And We sent not before you, [O Muḥammad], except men to whom We revealed [the message], so ask the people of the message [i.e., former scriptures] if you do not know.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And We sent not (as Our messengers) before thee other than men, whom We inspired. Ask the followers of the Reminder if ye know not?

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَا قَبْلَكَ إِلَّا رِجَالًا نُّوحِىٓ إِلَيْهِمْ  فَسْـَٔلُوٓا۟ أَهْلَ ٱلذِّكْرِ إِن كُنتُمْ لَا تَعْلَمُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{21:8}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And We did not make them [i.e., the prophets] forms not eating food, nor were they immortal [on earth].

\textit{M. Pickthall}: We gave them not bodies that would not eat food, nor were they immortals.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَمَا جَعَلْنَـٰهُمْ جَسَدًا لَّا يَأْكُلُونَ ٱلطَّعَامَ وَمَا كَانُوا۟ خَـٰلِدِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{21:9}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Then We fulfilled for them the promise, and We saved them and whom We willed and destroyed the transgressors.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Then we fulfilled the promise unto them. So we delivered them and whom We would, and We destroyed the prodigals.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
ثُمَّ صَدَقْنَـٰهُمُ ٱلْوَعْدَ فَأَنجَيْنَـٰهُمْ وَمَن نَّشَآءُ وَأَهْلَكْنَا ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{21:10}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: We have certainly sent down to you a Book [i.e., the Qur’ān] in which is your mention. Then will you not reason?

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Now We have revealed unto you a Scripture wherein is your Reminder. Have ye then no sense?

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
لَقَدْ أَنزَلْنَآ إِلَيْكُمْ كِتَـٰبًا فِيهِ ذِكْرُكُمْ  أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{21:11}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And how many a city which was unjust have We shattered and produced after it another people.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: How many a community that dealt unjustly have We shattered, and raised up after them another folk!

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَكَمْ قَصَمْنَا مِن قَرْيَةٍ كَانَتْ ظَالِمَةً وَأَنشَأْنَا بَعْدَهَا قَوْمًا ءَاخَرِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{21:12}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And when they [i.e., its inhabitants] perceived Our punishment, at once they fled from it.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And, when they felt Our might, behold them fleeing from it!

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَلَمَّآ أَحَسُّوا۟ بَأْسَنَآ إِذَا هُم مِّنْهَا يَرْكُضُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{21:13}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: [Some angels said], "Do not flee but return to where you were given luxury and to your homes - perhaps you will be questioned."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: (But it was said unto them): Flee not, but return to that (existence) which emasculated you and to your dwellings, that ye may be questioned.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
لَا تَرْكُضُوا۟ وَٱرْجِعُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰ مَآ أُتْرِفْتُمْ فِيهِ وَمَسَـٰكِنِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُسْـَٔلُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{21:14}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: They said, "O woe to us! Indeed, we were wrongdoers."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: They cried: Alas for us! we were wrong-doers.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
قَالُوا۟ يَـٰوَيْلَنَآ إِنَّا كُنَّا ظَـٰلِمِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{21:15}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And that declaration of theirs did not cease until We made them [as] a harvest [mowed down], extinguished [like a fire].

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And this their crying ceased not till We made them as reaped corn, extinct.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
فَمَا زَالَت تِّلْكَ دَعْوَىٰهُمْ حَتَّىٰ جَعَلْنَـٰهُمْ حَصِيدًا خَـٰمِدِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{21:16}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And We did not create the heaven and earth and that between them in play.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: We created not the heaven and the earth and all that is between them in play.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَمَا خَلَقْنَا ٱلسَّمَآءَ وَٱلْأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا لَـٰعِبِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{21:17}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Had We intended to take a diversion, We could have taken it from [what is] with Us - if [indeed] We were to do so.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: If We had wished to find a pastime, We could have found it in Our presence - if We ever did.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
لَوْ أَرَدْنَآ أَن نَّتَّخِذَ لَهْوًا لَّٱتَّخَذْنَـٰهُ مِن لَّدُنَّآ إِن كُنَّا فَـٰعِلِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{21:18}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Rather, We dash the truth upon falsehood, and it destroys it, and thereupon it departs. And for you is destruction from that which you describe.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Nay, but We hurl the true against the false, and it doth break its head and lo! it vanisheth. And yours will be woe for that which ye ascribe (unto Him).

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
بَلْ نَقْذِفُ بِٱلْحَقِّ عَلَى ٱلْبَـٰطِلِ فَيَدْمَغُهُ فَإِذَا هُوَ زَاهِقٌ  وَلَكُمُ ٱلْوَيْلُ مِمَّا تَصِفُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{21:19}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: To Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth. And those near Him [i.e., the angels] are not prevented by arrogance from His worship, nor do they tire.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Unto Him belongeth whosoever is in the heavens and the earth. And those who dwell in His presence are not too proud to worship Him, nor do they weary;

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَلَهُ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ  وَمَنْ عِندَهُ لَا يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ عَنْ عِبَادَتِهِ وَلَا يَسْتَحْسِرُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{21:20}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: They exalt [Him] night and day [and] do not slacken.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: They glorify (Him) night and day; they flag not.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
يُسَبِّحُونَ ٱلَّيْلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ لَا يَفْتُرُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{21:21}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Or have they [i.e., men] taken for themselves gods from the earth who resurrect [the dead]?

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Or have they chosen gods from the earth who raise the dead?

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
أَمِ ٱتَّخَذُوٓا۟ ءَالِهَةً مِّنَ ٱلْأَرْضِ هُمْ يُنشِرُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{21:22}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Had there been within them [i.e., the heavens and earth] gods besides Allāh, they both would have been ruined. So exalted is Allāh, Lord of the Throne, above what they describe.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: If there were therein gods beside Allah, then verily both (the heavens and the earth) had been disordered. Glorified be Allah, the Lord of the Throne, from all that they ascribe (unto Him).

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
لَوْ كَانَ فِيهِمَآ ءَالِهَةٌ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُ لَفَسَدَتَا  فَسُبْحَـٰنَ ٱللَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَرْشِ عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{21:23}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: He will not be questioned as to that which He doeth, but they will be questioned.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
لَا يُسْـَٔلُ عَمَّا يَفْعَلُ وَهُمْ يُسْـَٔلُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{21:24}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Or have they taken gods besides Him? Say, [O Muḥammad], "Produce your proof. This [Qur’ān] is the message for those with me and the message of those before me." But most of them do not know the truth, so they are turning away.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Or have they chosen other gods beside Him? say: Bring your proof (of their godhead). This is the Reminder of those with me and those before me, but most of them know not the Truth and so they are averse.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
أَمِ ٱتَّخَذُوا۟ مِن دُونِهِٓ ءَالِهَةً  قُلْ هَاتُوا۟ بُرْهَـٰنَكُمْ  هَـٰذَا ذِكْرُ مَن مَّعِىَ وَذِكْرُ مَن قَبْلِى  بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ ٱلْحَقَّ  فَهُم مُّعْرِضُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{21:25}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And We sent not before you any messenger except We revealed to him that, "There is no deity except Me, so worship Me."

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And We sent no messenger before thee but We inspired him, (saying): There is no Allah save Me (Allah), so worship Me.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ مِن رَّسُولٍ إِلَّا نُوحِىٓ إِلَيْهِ أَنَّهُ لَآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنَا فَٱعْبُدُونِ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{21:26}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son." Exalted is He! Rather, they are [but] honored servants.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And they say: The Beneficent hath taken unto Himself a son. Be He Glorified! Nay, but (those whom they call sons) are honoured slaves;

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَقَالُوا۟ ٱتَّخَذَ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنُ وَلَدًا  سُبْحَـٰنَهُ  بَلْ عِبَادٌ مُّكْرَمُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{21:27}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: They cannot precede Him in word, and they act by His command.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: They speak not until He hath spoken, and they act by His command.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
لَا يَسْبِقُونَهُ بِٱلْقَوْلِ وَهُم بِأَمْرِهِ يَعْمَلُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{21:28}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: He knows what is [presently] before them and what will be after them, and they cannot intercede except on behalf of one whom He approves. And they, from fear of Him, are apprehensive.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: He knoweth what is before them and what is behind them, and they cannot intercede except for him whom He accepteth, and they quake for awe of Him.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ وَلَا يَشْفَعُونَ إِلَّا لِمَنِ ٱرْتَضَىٰ وَهُم مِّنْ خَشْيَتِهِ مُشْفِقُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{21:29}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And whoever of them should say, "Indeed, I am a god besides Him" - that one We would recompense with Hell. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And one of them who should say: Lo! I am a god beside Him, that one We should repay with hell. Thus We Repay wrong-doers.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
۞ وَمَن يَقُلْ مِنْهُمْ إِنِّىٓ إِلَـٰهٌ مِّن دُونِهِ فَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِيهِ جَهَنَّمَ  كَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى ٱلظَّـٰلِمِينَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{21:30}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: Have those who disbelieved not considered that the heavens and the earth were a joined entity, and then We separated them and made from water every living thing? Then will they not believe?

\textit{M. Pickthall}: Have not those who disbelieve known that the heavens and the earth were of one piece, then We parted them, and we made every living thing of water? Will they not then believe?

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
أَوَلَمْ يَرَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓا۟ أَنَّ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ كَانَتَا رَتْقًا فَفَتَقْنَـٰهُمَا  وَجَعَلْنَا مِنَ ٱلْمَآءِ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ حَىٍّ  أَفَلَا يُؤْمِنُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{21:31}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And We placed within the earth firmly set mountains, lest it should shift with them, and We made therein [mountain] passes [as] roads that they might be guided.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And We have placed in the earth firm hills lest it quake with them, and We have placed therein ravines as roads that haply they may find their way.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَجَعَلْنَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ رَوَٰسِىَ أَن تَمِيدَ بِهِمْ وَجَعَلْنَا فِيهَا فِجَاجًا سُبُلًا لَّعَلَّهُمْ يَهْتَدُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{21:32}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And We made the sky a protected ceiling, but they, from its signs, are turning away.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And we have made the sky a roof withheld (from them). Yet they turn away from its portents.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَجَعَلْنَا ٱلسَّمَآءَ سَقْفًا مَّحْفُوظًا  وَهُمْ عَنْ ءَايَـٰتِهَا مُعْرِضُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{21:33}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And it is He who created the night and the day and the sun and the moon; all [heavenly bodies] in an orbit are swimming.

\textit{M. Pickthall}: And He it is Who created the night and the day, and the sun and the moon. They float, each in an orbit.

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ ٱلَّيْلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ وَٱلشَّمْسَ وَٱلْقَمَرَ  كُلٌّ فِى فَلَكٍ يَسْبَحُونَ
\end{Arabic}
}
\vspace{0.5ex}



\noindent[\textbf{21:34}]
\textit{Saheeh Intl.}: And We did not grant to any man before you eternity [on earth]; so if you die - would they be eternal?

\textit{M. Pickthall}: We appointed immortality for no mortal before thee. What! if thou diest, can they be immortal!

{\Large
\begin{Arabic}
